title: CC Subscriber ECU configuration states
body: 355 v7 CC Subscriber ECU configuration states Version history:(7):Purpose: To define the possible states (including necessary handling) of CC Subscriber ECU configuration using allowed CCP data.Source:Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 65555v6ASIL: QM - Not safety relevanta) CC legacy general principles:The ECU/system shall determine what appropriate action(s) are to be taken for a specific function/feature when utilizing a default configuration or validated CCP data. The ECU/system failure mode handling/operating strategy might contain additional routines that need to be handled and documented. Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU CC Subscriber ECUs shall implement default values for CCPs based on any required default operating condition so that the appropriate functionality can be achieved and where necessary failure mode management actions shall be active.The default operating conditions are dependent on the strategic requirements of the ECU. The operation of the functions within the ECU strategy shall be in line with FMEA rules affecting safety of the vehicle and occupants and customer satisfaction in the absence of configuration information. Wherever possible the vehicle should operate normally. If the vehicle could be made dangerous or perform unsatisfactory for the customer/occupant, then failure mode management actions need to be executed to prevent or change this vehicle behaviour. The failure mode management actions shall be in respect of the ECU FMEA recommended actions.b) Two CC Subscriber ECU states are defined as follows:Bulk State: In this state to receive required Car Config parameters for the first time and keep state until all have been evaluated valid:The below applies to every CCP that the subscriber ECU expects to receive and evaluate:Whenever a valid CCP value is available/received it shall be used.For a received but not valid CCP value, use the ECU default value for that parameter instead.Valid Configuration State: In this state only to detect a possible change in car config parameter values:The below applies to every CCP that the subscriber ECU expects to receive and evaluate:For a received but not valid CCP value, consider using the previously stored valid value for that parameter instead.CC Subscriber state guidelines provided for configuration using CCP data (distributed within the VCP signal) in chapter Guideline subscriber states.c) Evaluation of a CCP value implies that (compared to whatever configuration the ECU/system currently utilizes) the ECU/system must determine if a received CCP value is valid, e.g. recognized, within valid range for acceptance, possible to transition to if ECU already has a Valid Configuration State etc.

title: CC Subscriber ECU in Bulk (unconfigured) state
body: 356 v6 CC Subscriber ECU in Bulk (unconfigured) state Version history:(6):Purpose: To identify an unconfigured/bulk state.Source:Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 65556v5ASIL: QM - Not safety relevantIf the CC Subscriber ECU has not received or does not contain expected CCP data after 30 seconds from its application boot-up sequence while residing within ECU delivery default/Bulk State, the CC Subscriber ECU shall use DTC "Car Configuration – Not Configured" U2300- Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU 55, DTC test according to [CCF_2] UDS Data.

title: Routines for receiving VCP signal (CC Domain Master excluded)
body: 357 v9 Routines for receiving VCP signal (CC Domain Master excluded) Version history:(9):Purpose: To assure flexibility of the CC Subscriber ECUs when receiving Car Configuration data.Source:Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 65561v7ASIL: QM - Not safety relevanta) The CC Subscriber ECU shall be able to read BlockID#, in the VCP signals, arriving in any order, in accordance with table VCP signal mapping in chapter Record of tables.b) The CC Subscriber ECU shall be able to receive and process every arrival of a BlockID in the Vehicle configuration signals VehCfgPrm and VehCfgPrmExt.

title: Invalid or unrecognized parameter values
body: 358 v7 Invalid or unrecognized parameter values Version history:(7):Purpose: To prevent any damage/security risk internally/externally in the CC Subscriber ECU associated with invalid or unrecognized parameter values.Source:Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 65582v6ASIL: QM - Not safety relevantIf any CCP value(s) used for configuration (including values $00_H$ and $FF_H$ ) is received and evaluated invalid or unrecognized by the CC Subscriber ECU, the related function shall perform the following actions:a) Enter a safe mode (depending on ECU strategy in line with FMEA rules) if there is an imminent risk of serious errors.b) Use DTC "Car Configuration –Invalid/Incompatible Configuration" U2300-56, DTC test according to [CCF_2] UDS Data.c) Minimize (avoid if possible) the impact on functions not related to parameter usage.Note: For functions that are not safety nor security critical, whose behaviour/setting would be a similar or equal even if a received CCP value is not expected, a range of CCP values could be adopted as valid, e.g. CCP value range 0x01 to 0xFE is valid for configuration.

title: Configuration of ECU with updated CCP data
body: 359 v7 Configuration of ECU with updated CCP data Version history:(7): Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU Purpose: To enable automatic configuration/re-configuration of ECU SW using updated CCP data.Source:Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 65583v6ASIL: QM - Not safety relevanta) The CC Subscriber ECU shall have two separate states of configuration relating to Central Car Configuration parameters. The "Bulk State" is when the ECU is delivered/built-in without pre-programming, i.e. factory settings. The "Valid Configuration State" is when all expected/allowed CCP values are in use and have been received and evaluated valid at least once.b) The CC Subscriber ECU is required to transition from "Bulk State" -> "Valid Configuration State" after a complete set of expected CCPs have been evaluated valid and used for SW configuration.

title: Selection of CCPs in VCP signal
body: 360 v4 Selection of CCPs in VCP signal Version history:(4):Purpose: To ensure that the correct CC Subscriber ECUs get the correct Car Configuration data, and to avoid misuse of CCP data resulting in unnecessary SW-updates when changes on CCP definitions occur.Source:Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 65584v3ASIL: QM - Not safety relevantThe CC Subscriber ECU shall use information in a parameter list or equivalent (released/extracted from CCdB) containing the CCP numbers that the CC Subscriber ECU has requested use for or is required to configure by.The BlockID# (in the VCP signal), and byte position, in which a specific CCP can be obtained, shall be according to table VCP signal mapping in chapter Record of tables.

title: Car Configuration data storage
body: 361 v7 Car Configuration data storage Version history:(7):Purpose: The CC Subscriber ECU must be able to maintain parameter values between normal drive cycles, ECU resets, power cycles and low voltage due to engine cranking.Source:Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 65585v6ASIL: QM - Not safety relevant Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU All CC Subscriber ECUs shall store their valid CCP data used for configuration in non-volatile memory (NVM). The format/interpretation of the parameter(s) to be stored shall be specified in the SWRS of each ECU subscribing to that parameter.

title: Car Configuration parameter definition
body: 362 v3 Car Configuration parameter definition Version history:(3):Purpose: To assure that each Car Configuration parameter is used according to its original purpose.Source:Verification Method: AnalysisLegacy ID: 65586v2ASIL: QM - Not safety relevantA Car Configuration parameter shall have the same definition in the CC Subscriber ECU as in CCdB.

title: Handling of parameter data
body: 363 v4 Handling of parameter data Version history:(4):Purpose: General handling when reading CCPs within VCP signal and to avoid faulty ECU and vehicle behaviour respectively.Source:Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 65587v3ASIL: QM - Not safety relevanta) CCP value 00h indicates that the CCP is not in use (not defined), e.g. not used within vehicle project/platform or spare/reserved CCP for future use.b) CCP value FFh indicates that the CCP has been generated erroneously.c) CCP value 00h and FFh shall not be used for any ECU SW configuration.

title: ECU configuration after boot-up
body: 364 v6 ECU configuration after boot-up Version history:(6):Purpose: Enabling correct/updated CC Subscriber ECU configuration after ECU boot-up. Evaluation check of received parameters, after ECU boot-up, expected to be run only once per driving cycle.Source:Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 65588v5ASIL: QM - Not safety relevantAfter ECU application boot-up sequence the CC Subscriber ECU shall use the current set of stored CCP values (or default configuration if no previous data received/available). Document Name Base Tech SWRS DHU Once, as soon as a new set of parameter values is received, the CC Subscriber ECU shall evaluate the new parameter values, dependent on which configuration state the CC Subscriber ECU currently resides in (see requirement CC Subscriber ECU configuration states).

There are two major types of configuration methods: Global and Local. Configuration parameters, often compiled within a SW file that may contain only one of those two distinct parameter types. Local parameters may either reside in a separate file or can be embedded in ECU's software. Properties for SW Configuration files:Handled according to approved SW handling processes.Traceable in individual car.Downloaded at assembly plants or service shops.Stored in SW databases. GEELYGeely Automotive Research Institute(Ningbo)Co.Ltd Document TypeNote-SWRS Document Release StatusRELEASED Document No Revision005 Volume No01 Page No101(1572) Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU 4.1.2.1.1.1 Configuration Using Global ParametersGlobal parameters denote major systems, functions and features implemented in vehicle via ECU applications. Global parameters notion is often termed Central Car Configuration (or CarConfig in short), are used to configure ECU functions centrally over a distributed network during run-time.The CarConfig file is generated when the vehicle is built or updated; therefore it is unique per vehicle. Parameter values are stored in the Central Electronics Module or equivalent, from where they are transmitted on all networks to the ECUs requiring them.It is strongly recommended to choose each parameter as specific and function oriented as possible. This facilitates to reconfigure multiple ECUs just by generating & downloading new CarConfig file.In general following guidelines should be fulfilled when applying global parameters changes:Each parameter value shall specifically point out the behaviour of the function using that parameter. A parameter with an indirect effect on the functional behaviour (e.g. market code or date) shall not be used, for two reasons:If the relationship between the indirect parameter and the functional requirements is changed (e.g. the legislation on the market is changed) the function will no longer behave correctly.If a new code for the indirect parameter is introduced (e.g. new market) the new parameter code cannot be used to configure the function without re-writing the software in the receiving ECU.It shall not be possible to add an accessory function by only altering a parameter value. Adding an accessory function (e.g. cruise control) must involve the download of additional software (i.e. a new software part number).A global parameter should not be unique to a specific ECU; i.e. other ECUs would preferably be able to use it. Thus it gets usage potential by multiple modules/features as desired by CarConfig notion; otherwise this should be solved locally.It's not allowed to re-define (name & content of) existing parameter values, if they have already been used in customer cars.A global Parameter can not be dynamic relying on a network signal from another module as to calculate the parameter value to be published over the network.The parameter would rather be generic and not for a specific platform usage solely, to facilitate carry over/back of nodes & functions.Following are specifications of two Global parameters currently in use: Parameter Module Configurable Item Value Comments Variant Code 245 PEDESTRIAN PROTECTION Without Pedestrian Protection EZ01 With Pedestrian Protection EZ02 Without Stop/Start CP01 SIN CP02 246 STOP/START LOGIC SIN/SIG CP03 SID CP04 SINS CP05 GEELYGeely Automotive Research Institute(Ningbo)Co.Ltd Document TypeNote-SWRS Document Release StatusRELEASED Document No Revision005 Volume No01 Page No102(1572) Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU 4.1.2.1.1.2 Configuration Using Local ParametersLocal parameters consist of a set of values to configure ECU application, often packed in a binary file. They are kreate as a part of the ECU Software, stored in the SW database and are traceable via SW article numbers. They are downloaded or updated at assembly plants or at service shops. This type is used when the global parameters usage is not possible or appropriate to use; they are used in single ECU, not accessible to other ECUs. Local parameters can either exist in a separate file or be embedded in ECU software.Example:Calibration values for diesel injectors.Calibration values for SRS.4.1.2.1.1.3 Special cases of the Local parametersLocal calibration data are parameters temporarily applied in ECUs during development phases for tests and calibration/optimization purposes. These parameters are generated, applied and stored locally in concerned developing departments.Example:Calibration and optimization data for ECM software.4.1.2.1.2 Customer SettingsCustomer settings is a collective name referred to all those available options to select or adjust some pre-defined set of functions or features e.g. to enhance users' comfort or vehicle usability and performance (adaption to driving conditions etc). Settings are activated or modified through customer choice using available HMI (buttons, Center Stack, displays). The customer has the option to save own settings in available profiles, to re-load them for activation at next driving session.Customer settings have following properties:Not traceable to individual cars by OEM databasesSettings can be done by customer via HMIDefault settings can be done via ECU applicationsProfiles are backed-up to be restored after a car service session4.1.2.1.2.1 Types of Customer SettingsAll customers setting will in next platform are stored and re-stored using Profile notion; however, Customer settings can roughly be divided in two types:Personal settings:The customer can select, modify or adjust some pre-defined set of settings to improve vehicle comfort, usability etc.Examples include adjustments for:Side mirror, Seat (position, heat), Steering wheel (height, force level), Climate, and Infotainment system features.Driving settings: Document Name Base Tech SWRS DHU These settings contain the functions to enhance vehicle usability and performance, e.g. adaption to changing driving conditions etc. Examples are activation of: ECO Mode, Extended EV mode, Sport Mode, PAS settings, DSTC settings, LDW settings. 4.1.2.1.3 Summary of Configuration Types The table below summarizes major vehicle configuration types, theirs sources, download methods and storage area. Configuration Type Data Source Realization Storage area Global Parameter Team Center/Variant Structure SWDL gl-PIE Local Parameter Team Center/Variant Structure SWDL or embedded in SW applications gl-PIE Local Calibration Data Locally at concerned departments SWDL or embedded in SW applications Locally at concerned departments Customer Settings ECU software or similar files Initially as default values in ECU application; later via customers. In-vehicle back-up so that customer may restore them after service. 4.1.2.1.4 Introduction 4.1.2.1.4.1 Document Purpose This document aims to guide users through the subject and terminology for different types of configuration parameters and customer settings. 4.1.2.1.5 Definitions and Abbreviations Abbr. Stands for Description CCdB Car Configuration Database Tool & Data Base for generating CarConfig data DSTC Dynamic Stabilization & Traction System EV Electric Vehicle ECU Electronic Control Unit Microcontroller-based module LDW Lane Departure Warning An active safety feature PAS Parking Assist System An audio/video based assisting feature P-spec Product specification Vehicle building data, unique for each car SW Soft Ware 4.1.2.1.6 Background There are different configuration methods for vehicles systems and functions. Following chapters make an effort to explain and establish common terminology within organisation. Although to make any change in car functions often involves ECU application configured with new input values, here we reserve the term CONFIGURATION for major & permanent (i.e. by SWDL) configuration of ECU software, and the term SETTINGS for activating and adjustments in current implemented functions. Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU The configuration types and settings explained here are:Vehicle SW Configuration methods:Central Car ConfigurationLocal ConfigurationTemporary calibration/optimization dataCustomer Settings categories:Personal SettingsDriving SettingsThe purpose of configuration and settings could be to:Control, modify, or optimize the behaviour of system or device functions.Reduce the number of software or hardware variants.Input static calibration & optimization values for system or device functions.Share common data or information.Store shared data in common area.The following configuration methods are in use:Software download, Central Car ConfigurationSoftware download, Local ECU ConfigurationIncorporating local parameters in SW applicationsSelecting the desired settings via HMI, by customerHaving default setting values via ECU applications4.2 Diag & ECU Platform - proj reqs4.2.1 SRD Diagnostics and ECU Platform4.2.1.1 Diagnostics and ECU Platform4.2.1.1.1 IntroductionStatement of Work (SOW)Diagnostics and ECU Platform Statement Of Work is the name of the SOW (Statement Of Work) from Diagnostics & ECU Platform and it is essential that it is part of the ESOW for each node that intend to use requirements from our area.This SOW defines the additional required engineering tasks, responsibilities and deliverables for the design, engineering development, quality assurance and test of an Electronic Control Unit (ECU) / Subsystem that shall conform to the Vehicle Program requirements on Diagnostics and ECU Platform.SW PlatformIssues with regards to the AUTOSAR platform and its development are described in the SOWs (mentioned above) with the Tier 1. Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU The main purpose of SWDL is:- Reduced time for developmentAvoided lead time for hardware changes- Reduced number of hardware partnumbersVariants are configured with softwareLess delivery unitsLess units in stock saves space (factory, aftersales and suppliers)- The vehicle is after production possible to changeUpdating of software “quality issues”New functionality “replaces hardware changes”Upgrade “increased/changed functionality”A bootloader consists of a primary and secondary bootloader (xBL) that supports the software download protocol. The bootloader always gain program control after a reset, and passes the control over to the application when it has determined that no download is requested.The software download concept is based on a primary bootloader that is fixed in the ECU and always executed at power on before the application is started and a secondary bootloader that is downloaded before downloading the applications and configuration datafiles.Software download functionality is not a part of the AUTOSAR based ECU architecture. To support software download a bootloader shall be used (a stand alone application). Enter and exit of the bootloader is handled by a common API, known by the AUTOSAR based ECU architecture and the bootloader.CarConfigCar Configuration is used to organize car specific information and to minimize the software variants by sending out information about the car over the multiplexed network. This makes it possible to use the same software to perform functions that differ between the car models.4.2.1.1.1.1 Definitions & Abbreviations Abbr. title: Component Selection - CAN Physical Interfaces
body: 1630 v3 Component Selection - CAN Physical Interfaces Version history:(3):Purpose: This is to prevent extra DC load on the network.Source: This is necessary for maintaining the CAN signal voltage level specified in partially powered networkVerification Method: AnalysisLegacy ID: 76513v1For power-switched ECUs an “ideal passive” transceiver shall be used. Transceivers shall not leak more than 5μA from an active CAN bus, in power-off mode.For battery-powered ECUs a transceiver with sleep functionality must be used.The list of approved components is available in Components For Physical Interfaces, for reference see Diagnostics & ECU Platform - Requisite documents.Note: This requirement is valid for all CAN ECU's.

title: No priority inversion
body: 1632 v2 No priority inversion Version history:(2):Purpose: The concept of guaranteed worst case latency offers several advantages to the system designer as well as to the node designer and node supplier. The SDB team will use guaranteed worst case latency to design a set of frames which will fulfil the signalling requirements given in the specifications defining vehicle functions. It will also be possible to guarantee that no signals will be overwritten, even when they have been transferred over gateways.Guaranteed worst case latency also permits busload to be significantly higher than the 30% often seen as the practical limit for reliable communication on CAN buses.The communication driver shall be designed to be free of priority inversion when frames are transmitted on the CAN bus by AUTOSAR based ECU's. If all CAN stacks are designed according to the priority inversion avoidance (PIA) concept it becomes possible to analyse the bus behaviour a priori. This analysis makes it possible to calculate and guarantee the worst case latency of all frames.Source: EESE Strategic DecisionVerification Method: AnalysisLegacy ID: 77275v1The communication driver shall be designed to be free of priority inversion when frames are transmitted on the CAN bus. 96055 v2 Terminating ECUs on CAN Version history:(2): Add the Terminal in the DHU Private CAN1Purpose:Source: ECU topologyVerification Method: AnalysisLegacy ID:List of terminating ECUs for each CAN network Table: Terminating ECUs CAN Network Terminating ECU1 Terminating ECU2 Propulsion CAN ECM VGM Chassis CAN1 ECM SAS Chassis CAN2 ECM VDDM Passive Safety CAN ASDM SRS AD Redundancy CAN PSCM FLC Safety CAN FD1 FSRL FSRR GEELYGeely Automotive Research Institute(Ningbo)Co.Ltd Document TypeNote-SWRS Document Release StatusRELEASED Document No Revision005 Volume No01 Page No123(1572) Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU Safety CAN FD2 ASDM FLR Safety CAN FD3 SODL SODR Safety CAN FD4 ASDM PAS Body Exposed CAN HCML HCMR Body CAN CEM CCM DHU Private CAN1 DHU SWTL Connectivity CAN HS VGM TCAM Private CAN1 FLC IMU Private CAN2 BECM EVCC Private Info CAN IHU/DHU AUD Diagnostics CAN VGM Tester 4.2.1.5 FlexRay Network4.2.1.5.1 Requirements

title: FlexRay Backbone - FlexRay Schedule Coordinator
body: 1636 v3 FlexRay Backbone - FlexRay Schedule Coordinator Version history:(3): Change the Verification Method from Test to Analysis Purpose: To define which ECU is the FlexRay Schedule Coordinator (FrSC) on the network FlexRay Backbone. The FrSC have the responsibility to inform the other ECU's on the FlexRay bus which FlexRay Schedule is active for the moment. For the time being there are two schedules available: Application Schedule 1 and Bootloader Schedule 1. The way to inform the other ECU's by the FrSC is to transmit a special signal called FlexRay NetworkStatus parameter (FRNetworkStatus).Source: FlexRay Data Link Layer, Bootloader - UDSonFR, UDSonFRVerification Method: AnalysisLegacy ID: 288973v1The VCM / VGM is the FlexRay Coordinator on the network FlexRay Backbone. Note: This requirement is valid for VCM / VGM.

Note that an ECU can be a slave on FlexRay and a master on CAN and vice versa. The missing frame master, located at the FlexRay Backbone network is the VCM / VGM.Note: This requirement is valid for VCM / VGM on the network FlexRay Backbone.

title: LIN Master
body: 1653 v2 LIN Master Version history: (2): Purpose: To ensure full compatibility with the network design tool (VNA). Source: LIN Standard Verification Method: Analysis Legacy ID: 76526v1 All LIN Master nodes shall follow the LIN Specification Package version 2.1 or newer so they can be moved between LIN networks. LIN Datalink Layer, for reference see Diagnostics & ECU Platform - Requisite documents, contains both LIN Specification Package 1.3 and LIN Specification Package 2.x.

title: Diagnostic IP routing algorithm
body: 1640 v3 Diagnostic IP routing algorithm Version history:(3): Change the name VCM to VGMPurpose: Clarification of how the diagnostic IP routing algorithm shall work.Source:Verification Method: AnalysisLegacy ID: 342169v0A general rule for the Edge Node to be able to decide what kind of diagnostic message which shall be send over the IP-links or other vehicle network (CAN, LIN, FlexRay) is to investigate the IP address and search for the Domain ID.If the three lowest nibbles of the ECU address matches the three lowest nibbles in an IP address, use this IP address when route/gateway diagnostic messages. Otherwise use the IP address of the domain master for diagnostic messages. (i.e. IP address that match ECU address [Domain ID].0.1).Example ECU: VGM (Edge node) has active DoIP TCP connections from [198.18.34.1] & [198.18.2.18]When a request for 0x1201 is received the following happens: 0x1201 means domain 2 => IP / Eth interface, The three lowest nibbles in 0x1201 matches the three lowest nibbles in 198.18.34.1 => use the connection with IP 198.18.34.1When a request for 0x1212 is received the three lowest nibbles in 0x1212 matches the three lowest nibbles in 198.18.2.18 => use the connection associated with IP 198.18.2.18When a request for 0x1241 is received the three lowest nibbles in 0x1241 does not match the three lowest nibbles in the IP address for any active connection => Try with the domain master address 0x1201 instead => 0x1201 matches the three lowest nibbles in 198.18.34.1 => use the connection with IP 198.18.34.1When a request for 0x1341 is received, domain 3 is still IP/Eth, the three lowest nibbles in 0x1341 does not match the three lowest nibbles in the IP address of any active connection => Try with the domain master address 0x1301 instead => 0x1301 does not match any active connection => Send DoIP Nack(Unknown Target Address) to tester.

Revise the note of IP Command port.Purpose: to define the port range for each application typeSource:Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: port group Range definition note IP Command port 50000+SID the SID should not be 0x01 and the max value is51000 (SID=0x3E8) IP Link Manager port 50001 fixed number for IP Link Manager RTP port 53248 to 53503 the port number is from 0xD000 to 0xD0FF Applicative port 31000 to 31050 the port for other in-vehicle applications exceptIP Command and RTP 4.2.1.7.1.1 RTP configuration4.2.1.7.1.1.1 SSRC 96017 v3 X-callVersion history:(3): 1.Revise the Requirement name: from "Emergency Assist" to "X-call"2.Revise the stream name: from "Emergency Assist audio stream" to "X-call audio stream"Purpose: To define the SSRC for X-call audio stream.Source:Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU For the X-call audio stream, the SSRC shall be set to 0xFFFF0000. 117371 v2 Emergency Video Record Version history:(2): 1.Change name from "360 Video Recording" to "Emergency Video Record".2.Add purpose for the requirement.Purpose: To define the SSRC for Emergency Video Record video stream.Source:Verification Method: TestLegacy ID:For the Emergency Video Record video stream, the SSRC shall be set to 0xFFFF0031.4.2.1.7.1.1.2 Media formats4.2.1.7.1.1.2.1 Audio format 96887 v4 X-call Version history:(4): 1.Revise the requirement name: from "Emergency Assist" to "X-call"Purpose: To clarity which audio format shell be defined, and define the number of channels.Source:Verification Method: AnalysisLegacy ID:For the audio communication of the X-call use case between TCAM and IHU/DHU, the audio format delivered over RTP shall be specified by the suppliers of TCAM and IHU/DHU. title: Bootloader CAN busoff handling
body: 1662 v2 Bootloader CAN busoff handling Version history:(2): Change the Verification Method from Test to AnalysisPurpose: To increase availability of the system. Avoid that an ECU gets stuck in bus-off state, or exits programming session due to network errors.Source:Verification Method: AnalysisLegacy ID: 392111v0If hardware support automatic CAN busoff recovery, that recovery mechanism shall be enabled.If hardware doesn't support automatic bus-off recovery the bootloader shall check all active CAN controllers for bus-off status at maximum 10 ms intervals and if bus-off is detected start the bus-off recovery sequence within 10ms.This requirement applies to Primary Boot Loader (PBL) and Secondary Boot Loader (SBL).Note: If a permanent busoff condition is detected that can not be recovered, and a complete and compatible application exist, the S3server timer shall still run and will finally elapse, causing and exit of the programming session.

title: Separate software files
body: 1667 v3 Separate software files Version history:(3):Purpose: To reduce the amount of non-diffable content in software files and to enable the possibility of flexible ECU updates. Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU Source:Verification Method: AnalysisLegacy ID:Purpose:In order to increase software flexibility and reduce the amount of non-diffable content in vbf-files, all graphics, fonts, and speech files used by an ECU must be delivered separately without any software dependencies.Note:This requirement is applicable for ECUs which stores vehicle HMI, fonts, or speech related files.

title: In-Place Reconstruction of Delta Files
body: 6411 v1 In-Place Reconstruction of Delta Files Version history:(1):Purpose: To reduce the time spent on the programming phase and the time spent in transfer over data communication networks.Source: General Bootloader requirements - Delta encodingVerification Method: AnalysisLegacy ID:The ECU shall support in-place reconstruction of software delta files according to the [Delta Encoding] specification.This requirement is applicable for ECUs which software size exceeds 10MB in size or exceeds 10min in programming time.Note: The programming time is calculated from the first EraseMemory/RequestDownload request to the last positively confirmed RequestTransferExit/CheckMemory response (SBL is excluded from this time calculation).4.2.1.10 AUTOSAR4.2.1.10.1 Requirements

title: Communication Gateway Processing
body: 1669 v2 Communication Gateway Processing Version history:(2):Purpose: To guarantee message timing.Source: Communication GatewayVerification Method: AnalysisLegacy ID: 76543v1The gateway functionality (which is a part of the communication layer) shall run every Communication SW processing period.Note: This requirement is valid for all ECU having more than one bus interface. Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU

title: Communication Stack Processing Period
body: 1670 v3 Communication Stack Processing Period Version history:(3):Purpose: To be able to optimize network performance.Source: -Verification Method: AnalysisLegacy ID: 76539v2The Communication stack processing period shall be 5,0 ms.Note: This requirement is valid for all ECUs with CAN, FlexRay, or LIN Master bus interfaces.

title: Communication Stack Processing Period Jitter
body: 1671 v4 Communication Stack Processing Period Jitter Version history:(4):Purpose: To be able to optimize network performance.Source: -Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 76542v2The jitter of the Communication stack processing period shall be less than 1 ms.Note: This requirement is valid for all ECUs with CAN, FlexRay, or LIN Master bus interfaces.

title: AUTOSAR version
body: 1672 v1 AUTOSAR version Version history:(1):Purpose: Specify AUTOSAR version.Source:Verification Method: AnalysisLegacy ID: 353876v0AUTOSAR version 4.2.2 shall be used.Note: Other revisions such as 4.0.3 may be used after agreement with the base technology team.4.2.1.11 Startup Time4.2.1.11.1 Requirements

title: Startup Time
body: 1673 v2 Startup Time Version history:(2): Change the Verification Method to Test Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU Purpose: In order to conform with tools used during manufacturing, and reduce the time spent in workshops and over-the-air diagnostics/SWDL use cases.Source:Verification Method: TestLegacy ID:Purpose:The ECU shall startup within 2,5 seconds and have full diagnostic and software download capabilities within this time. The time shall be measured from a state where the power to the ECU is completely turned off until it is capable of receiving diagnostic requests from both an internal tester in the vehicle, and an external tester connected through OBD.Note: This requirement is valid for all ECUs with diagnostics and/or software download capabilities, and is applicable for both AUTOSAR based microcontrollers and microcontrollers running an operating system such as Linux.4.3 Communication4.3.1 A2B Data Link Layer4.3.1.1 A2B Data Link Layer4.3.1.1.1 A2B System

title: A2B System Configuration responsibility
body: 366 v1 A2B System Configuration responsibility Version history:(1):Purpose: To define the responsibility for developing a A2B System configuration.Source:Verification Method: InspectionLegacy ID: 432021v0The system owner for the specific use case is responsible to develop and define the configuration parameters for A2B.

title: Define the origin of A2B configuration
body: 367 v1 Define the origin of A2B configuration Version history:(1):Purpose: To define the origin of A2B configurationSource:Verification Method: AnalysisLegacy ID: 432016v0The A2B configuration that shall be used in a particular A2B system shall be defined and stored in the node's Local Configuration.The configuration shall contain all transceiver register settings for the master plus all slaves that are needed for the A2B-system to work. Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU

title: Multiple A2B System configurations
body: 368 v1 Multiple A2B System configurations Version history:(1):Purpose: Define handling of multiple configuration possibilities.Source:Verification Method: AnalysisLegacy ID: 432020v0If multiple configurations of an A2B bus depending on the Car Configuration are used, shall all possible configurations be stored in a Local Configuration and the selection of which shall be used will be by a parameter in the Car Configuration.Note 1: The usage of multiple configurations are optional.

title: Read and write to A2B chip registers
body: 369 v1 Read and write to A2B chip registers Version history:(1):Purpose: To define that it shall be possible to read and write to the A2B internal registers.Source: [A2B-DL-10] and [A2B-DL-11]Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 432125v0It shall be possible to read and write to the internal registers of an A2B chip via diagnostic commands.

title: Response cycle calculation
body: 370 v2 Response cycle calculation Version history:(2):Purpose: The response time for a frame from Master to last slave and back again shall be calculated to guarantee the timing requirement.Source: [A2B-DL-1]Verification Method: AnalysisLegacy ID: 429458v1A response cycle calculation shall be performed in the Audio Channel Plan for the master and for each slave.The formula used is provided in Response Cycle Formula, reference in [A2B-DL-12].

title: SWDL the A2B configuration
body: 371 v1 SWDL the A2B configuration Version history:(1):Purpose: To require that the A2B configuration parameters shall be possible to download to the ECU. Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU Source: REQPROD 432016, 432020 and 432021Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 432024v0The A2B configuration parameters shall be possible to download to the ECU as a Local configuration and a Car Configuration file.4.3.1.1.2 A2B Data Link Layer - General Requirements4.3.1.1.2.1 Node Discovery

title: Master node PLL
body: 372 v2 Master node PLL Version history:(2):Purpose: Host initialization of A2B MasterSource: [A2B-DL-10]Verification Method: AnalysisLegacy ID: 429451v1When the Host starts the A2B Master transceiver, the Host shall provide master clock to let the transceiver lock its PLL on this frequency. The master transceiver generates an interrupt when its PLL has locked and this interrupt must be detected by the Host.The Host shall set a DTC for absence of A2B PLL lock if no interrupt are received within 25ms.

title: Response cycle parameter programming
body: 373 v2 Response cycle parameter programming Version history:(2):Purpose: Provide a valid response cycle value to all nodes.Source: [A2B-DL-1]Verification Method: AnalysisLegacy ID: 429459v1The Host shall set the response cycle parameter values on the master and on each slave with the values calculated in the audio channel plan.

title: Slave discovery and initialization
body: 374 v2 Slave discovery and initialization Version history:(2):Purpose: Host responsibilities and method of slave initialization.Source: [A2B-DL-11]Verification Method: AnalysisLegacy ID: 429452v1The Host shall after the Master has started carry out a node discovery and initialize all nodes present on the bus with the A2B node configuration from the Local Configuration.The slave discovery and initialization should be preferably be performed as described in Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU "Advanced Discovery Flow", [A2B-DL-11].

title: Slave discovery timeout
body: 375 v2 Slave discovery timeout Version history:(2): Purpose: Define the slave discovery timeout.Source: [A2B-DL-10]Verification Method: AnalysisLegacy ID: 429453v1 The slave discovery timeout for each slave shall be less than 50 ms.Note 1: this time starts at the writing of SWCTL= 0x01 4.3.1.1.2.2 Transmission settings

title: Data Rate
body: 376 v2 Data Rate Version history:(2): Purpose: Handle extended data rates, i.e. double sample rate.Source: [A2B-DL-1] and [A2B-DL-11]Verification Method: AnalysisLegacy ID: 429456v1 The normal data rate for an Audio Channel is 48 kHz. The audio channel plan may specify that an audio channel has an Increased Data Rate.Note: Increased Data Rate is defined in [A2B-DL-11]

title: PDM Compatibility
body: 377 v1 PDM Compatibility Version history:(1): Purpose: To define the compatible TDM mode when PDM is selected as an input format.Source: [A2B-DL-10]Verification Method:Legacy ID: 432276v0 A transceiver using a PDM input port are only allowed to use TDM2 on all other ports.

title: Preferred TDM modes
body: 378 v2 Preferred TDM modes Version history:(2): Purpose: To define available TDM modes.Source: [A2B-DL-10] and [A2B-DL-11]Verification Method: Analysis Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU Legacy ID: 429457v1Preferred TDM modes are TDM2, TDM4, TDM8, TDM16 and TDM32.Note 1: A transceiver uses same TDM-mode on all ports.

title: Reduced mode
body: 379 v1 Reduced mode Version history:(1):Purpose: To require that reduced mode is not allowed and the reason is that it's not fully specified.Source: [A2B-DL-11]Verification Method: AnalysisLegacy ID: 432047v0Reduced mode is not allowed to be used. This mode is disabled when the REDUCE bit is equal to 0.

title: Stream slot size
body: 380 v2 Stream slot size Version history:(2):Purpose: Define the available payload size on A2B.Source: [A2B-DL-10] and [A2B-DL-11]Verification Method: AnalysisLegacy ID: 429454v1The default slot size on up- respective down-stream shall be 24 bits.

title: TDM channel size
body: 381 v2 TDM channel size Version history:(2):Purpose: Define the available payload size on TDM.Source: [A2B-DL-10] and [A2B-DL-11]Verification Method: AnalysisLegacy ID: 429455v1The default TDM channel size shall be 32 bits.Note 1: As the stream slot is normally only 24 bits, the available payload is 24bits.4.3.1.1.3 A2B Data Link Layer - Fault handling4.3.1.1.3.1 Fault handling

title: Critical fault reset
body: 382 v2 Critical fault reset Version history:(2): Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU Purpose:Prohibit automatic reconnection in case of a critical fault.Source:[A2B-DL-11]Verification Method:TestLegacy ID:429463v1The host shall not try to reconnect a bus where a critical fault has occurred until restart conditions has been met. The restart conditions has to be specified in each application/project.Note 1: Non-critical and critical faults are defined by AD in [A2B-DL-11].

title: Critical fault shutdown
body: 383 v2 Critical fault shutdown Version history:(2):Purpose:If a critical fault are detected, the bus shall be shut down.Source:[A2B-DL-11]Verification Method:TestLegacy ID:429462v1If a critical fault (See Note 1) occurs the bus shall be shut down, the host shall clear the master transceivers A2B_SWCTL.ENSW bit.Note 1: A2B_SWCTL is a register in the A2B transceiver and ENSW is a specific bit in this register.Note 2: Non-critical and critical faults are defined by AD in [A2B-DL-11].

title: ENSW-bit clearing
body: 384 v2 ENSW-bit clearing Version history:(2):Purpose:The ENSW-bit shall be cleared in last non-affected node in case of line fault.Source:[A2B-DL-11]Verification Method:AnalysisLegacy ID:429461v1If a line fault has opened the bias switch (power feed to next bus segment) the host software shall clear the A2B_SWCTL.ENSW bit in the closest node to the fault. This only applies for non-critical faults.Note 1: A2B_SWCTL is a register in the A2B transceiver and ENSW is a specific bit in this register.Note 2: Non-critical and critical faults are defined by AD in [A2B-DL-11].

title: Non critical fault restart
body: 385 v2 Non critical fault restart Version history:(2):Purpose:The A2B shall restart after a non-critical fault.Source:[A2B-DL-11]Verification Method:AnalysisLegacy ID:429460v1 Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU When a non-critical fault (See [A2B-DL-1]) has occurred the host shall re-do node discovery to determine the localization of the fault (as specified in the [A2B-DL-10]).The host shall then initialize all discovered non-faulty nodes to create a partially working A2B system.Note 1. Non-critical and critical faults are defined by AD in [A2B-DL-11].4.3.1.1.3.2 Transmission fault detection

title: Bit error counter threshold
body: 386 v1 Bit error counter threshold Version history:(i):Purpose: Define the value of the bit error threshold counter in order to get a reasonable sensitivity of the detection.Source: REQPROD 432016, [A2B-DL-10] and [A2B-DL-11]Verification Method: AnalysisLegacy ID: 430928v0The bit error counter threshold value shall be set to 8, unless otherwise specified. The counter is reset at power up. The bit error counter threshold shall be stored in the Local Configuration.

title: Bit error detection on control data
body: 387 v1 Bit error detection on control data Version history:(i):Purpose: Define which bit error types that shall be detected.Source: [A2B-DL-11]Verification Method: AnalysisLegacy ID: 430926v0The following transmission errors shall be detected and a DTC shall be set by the host: CRC error in the interrupt response frame, header count error & missed synchronization response frame.Note 1: The used names corresponds to register fields terminology used in [A2B-DL-11]

title: Bit error detection on payload
body: 388 v1 Bit error detection on payload Version history:(i):Purpose: Define which bit error types that shall be detectedSource: [A2B-DL-11]Verification Method: AnalysisLegacy ID: 430927v0The following transmission errors shall be detected and a DTC shall be set in each slave with the bit error count register: CRC error in a control or response frame, Data decoding errors& streaming data parity error. GEELYGeely Automotive Research Institute(Ningbo)Co.Ltd Document TypeNote-SWRS Document Release StatusRELEASED Document No Revision005 Volume No01 Page No172(1572) Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU Note 1: The used names corresponds to register fields terminology used in [A2B-DL.11]Note 2: Payload data is not resent in case of errors, if necessary this has to be considered in the transportation layer (or similar).

title: External interrupts
body: 389 v1 External interrupts Version history:(1):Purpose: Placeholder for the eventual usage of A2B transceiver external interrupts.Source: [A2B-DL-10] and [A2B-DL-11]Verification Method: AnalysisLegacy ID: 430930v0The master node shall have the capability to catch an external interrupt (i.e. an IO-pin interrupt) from all slaves. The purpose of this interrupt shall be defined for each A2B project.Note 1: The usage of this interrupt on slaves are optional.

title: I2C access errors
body: 390 v1 I2C access errors Version history:(1):Purpose: Detect I2C access error on external components.Source: [A2B-DL-10] and [A2B-DL-11]Verification Method: AnalysisLegacy ID: 430929v0An I2C access error on a device outside the transceiver on a slave shall be detected by the host and a DTC shall be set. The action of this error shall be defined for each slave that uses I2C outside the transceiver. If I2C access error occurs on internal communication to an A2B slave transceiver, the host shall try again two times. The EEPROM and the I2C device in the figure below are optional.Host & Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU Version history:(2):Purpose: To define that the host shall detect if a slave node is missing.Source: REQPROD 432016 and 432020Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 427770v1The host connected to the master transceiver shall have the ability to discover if an expected slave node is not present. A DTC shall be set in this case.Note 1: The number of nodes connected are defined in Car Configuration.4.3.1.1.4 Definitions & Abbrevitations Abbrevitation Description A2B Automotive Audio Bus (A trademark of Analog Devices) AD Analog Devices, Inc DSP Digital Signal Processor ECU Electronic Control Unit, An electronic component normally containing one or more micro controllers that interfaces with the environment by means of sensors, actuators and often communicates with one or more data buses. ENSW Enable Switch I2S Inter-IC Sound, a digital audio bus for node internal usage. SWCTL Switch Control TDM Time Division Multiplexing PDM Pulse Density Modulation Definition Description Downstream The bus direction towards the last slave. Car Configuration This is collection of different configuration parameters for different ECU's in a car and the parameters are distributed over the internal communication buses to the destination ECU. Host A host is the microcontroller or DSP which is connected to the A2B master transceiver. Local Configuration This is a collection of parameters to configure an ECU. Local Powered A node with power supplied from a power source other than its upstream A2B link. A master node is always a local powered node. Master The originator of clock and downstream data. The master is connected to a host processor that is responsible for the programming of the master. Node Electronic Control Module. In this context is a node the same as an ECU. Phantom powered A slave node with power supplied from the A2B-wires. A phantom powered node is generally not connected with other wires than Figure: A2B optional configuration. As thus bus is a proprietary bus concept from Analog Devices this document specifies the usage of transceivers and necessary settings need to get a working bus.As it only specifies the usage of A2B, all demands in the specifics ECU's technical regulation has to be fulfilled as well.The level of this document has a rough relation to the data link layer in the OSI-model, and parts of the physical, network and transport which in the A2B-case are handled by its configuration.Attention: failure to comply with the requirements of this specification by any ECU using A2B may result in a non-functional audio bus. title: Standards for CAN interface
body: 392 v4 Standards for CAN interface Version history:(4):Purpose: Specification of CAN protocolSource: N.A.Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 53881v2The interface shall be specified according to CAN standard using bit rate specified in section Network Transmission Speed 500 kbps. References can be found in [Ext CAN DL 3], [Ext CAN DL 4] and [Ext CAN DL 5].

title: The priority between standard documents and this document Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU
body: 393 v4 The priority between standard documents and this document Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU Version history:(4):Purpose: To optimise the CAN system solutionSource: N.A.Verification Method: AnalysisLegacy ID: 53850v2In case of discrepancy between the standard documents and this specification, this specification has precedence.4.3.2.1.1.1 ECU LevelThe power supply voltage level at the node shall be measured continuously. HW and SW inaccuracy in the monitoring of the supply voltage level must be taken into account when the ECU is designed. The ECU must meet this operating voltage range requirement also in a worst case condition.Network communication outside the mandatory voltage range is encouraged on the condition that the ECU can correctly read and write messages and cause no disturbance to the network. There must be margins in both ends of the operating voltage range in regards to the voltage level where communication becomes unreliable or is no longer possible due hardware constraints.

title: Communication protocol
body: 394 v3 Communication protocol Version history:(3):Purpose: Specification of CAN protocol usedSource: N.A.Verification Method: AnalysisLegacy ID: 53848v2Controller Area Network (CAN) in accordance with CAN V2.0 [Ext CAN DL 2] .

title: Behaviour outside normal supply voltage range
body: 395 v3 Behaviour outside normal supply voltage range Version history:(3):Purpose: Ensure stability at high and low supply voltageSource: N.A.Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 53883v2 Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU Hysteresis shall be used to ensure stable behaviour under low and high supply voltage conditions. Hysteresis shall be minimum 100mV.Note: This requirement addresses bus communication only and is not aligned with the operating voltage range requirement for the specific ECU.

title: CAN bus level during reset
body: 396 v3 CAN bus level during reset Version history:(3):Purpose: Prevent the ECU from disturbing the network during a local reset.Source: N.A.Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 53884v2Modules shall not drive the CAN bus dominant during module reset.

title: Bus fault reporting
body: 397 v4 Bus fault reporting Version history:(4): Change the Verification Method to AnalysisPurpose:Source:Verification Method: AnalysisLegacy ID: 53885v2At least one module on each bus must be able to detect and report faults on the physical bus. Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU The faults and their respective fault codes are specified in [CAN DL 6] . The SRD Diagnostics and ECU Platform for the specific vehicle program specifies which module should perform this fault monitoring.4.3.2.1.1.1.1 Resynchronisation and bit sampling

title: ECU Conformance
body: 403 v1 ECU Conformance Version history:(1): Purpose: To ensure that the ECU is conformant to the 100BASE-T1 standard. The ECU supplier will have to provide test results of the applicable test cases. Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU Source: ETH DL 16Verification Method: AnalysisLegacy ID: 435344v0The ECU shall prove conformance to 100BASE-T1 by passing all layer 2 test cases in [ETH DL 16].The test suites shall be performed by an external test house approved by the base technology team (PSS333).All test results must be provided and will be kept confidential.

title: Link Establishment Time
body: 404 v5 Link Establishment Time Version history:(5):Purpose: To set the time allowed for link establishment.Source: Not availableVerification Method: TestLegacy ID: 353337v4The time to establish a link shall be less than 100 msec. The time starts when at least one of the following occurs:The ECU is powered.A wake up signal that implies that the link is needed is received by the ECU. A wake up signal can be, but is not limited to a wake up signal received via other networks like CAN and FlexRay, a button that is pressed, wake up via a cellular network or wake up via a WiFi Network.

title: Link speed and duplex
body: 405 v3 Link speed and duplex Version history:(3):Purpose: In order to optimize the startup time Auto negotiation shall not be used.Instead the link speed and duplex of each port connected to a PHY will be set statically.Source: ETH DL 4Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 347357v2The link speed and duplex for each port that is connected to an internal or external PHY shall be set according to [ETH DL 4].

title: MTU

Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU Source:Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 412631v1The default MTU size of Ethernet packets shall be set to 1500 bytes.MTU size shall be configurable.

title: Multicast support

One way to optimize the throughput is to change the border between the static and dynamic segment. For example when there is need to transmit a lot of data from only one node, the dynamic segment shall be larger than the static. This use case is applicable for Software Download. In order to determine which schedule is active a new parameter named NetworkStatus has been defined. This parameter is sent in the first slot of the static segment. There is one node on each FlexRay network which is responsible to transmit the NetworkStatus parameter. This node has the responsibility to be a FlexRay Schedule Coordinator. There are different requirements on the FlexRay Schedule Coordinator depending if the node is master on the Backbone or a Sub network. When the schedule is changed there is only a limited number of FlexRay parameters which need to be changed. These parameters are defined in chapter Global cluster parameters for Application Schedules and Global cluster parameters for Bootloader Schedules. The NetworkStatus parameter defines which FlexRay schedule is active at each moment. title: NetworkStatus Parameter
body: 452 v3 NetworkStatus Parameter Version history:(3):Purpose: In order for each node to detect which FlexRay Schedule is active.Source: -Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 56850v2The NetworkStatus parameter shall be two bytes long and shall be sent by the FlexRay Schedule Coordinator in the first slot of the static segment in all cycles and for all schedules.The name of the parameter as a signal on the bus is FRNetworkStatus. The byte order on the bus is: the most significant shall be transmitted first and then the least significant byte.

title: NetworkStatus parameter - Fault conditions
body: 456 v3 NetworkStatus parameter - Fault conditions Version history:(3):Purpose: To define the fault behaviour if a node receives an unexpected value of the NetworkStatus parameter.Source:Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 236796v2If a node receives a value of the NetworkStatus parameter which is not one of the defined values Normal, Boot or Undefined, the node is then not allowed to transmit any data. If a node receives the value Undefined of the NetworkStatus parameter when the Normal FlexRay schedule is active, the node is then allowed to both receive and transmit data. A node shall always listen on the NetworkStatus parameter (signal FRNetworkStatus) to be able to recover from a fault condition and start communicate again when the status is changed to Normal, Boot or Undefined. The frame containing the NetworkStatus must be a valid non-null frame received without errors for any further evaluation of NetworkStatus.Note: For example: The FlexRay Schedule Coordinator have been updated with a new schedule and one node have only an old schedule defined. It's then possible that this node is disturbing the communication. 4.3.4.1.2.2 FlexRay schedule changeThe purpose of a schedule change is in this context to change the partitioning between static and dynamic segment. The main use case for this is to have an optimized application schedule and an optimized bootloader schedule, by increasing the gNumberOfStaticSlots and reducing gNumberOfMinistolts defined in chapter 3.2 and 3.3 or vice versa in a well coordinated way that ensures that the length of a cycle remains unchanged. It is possible to have partial communication running even though different nodes use different schedules. To make this possible must the schedules have common slots in the static segment and the payload must be the same. Once the first node enters its dynamic part, communication between the nodes is impossible. The receiving node will compare the received slot number of the frame with its internally calculated slot number. If they do not match the frame will be regarded as erroneous and discarded. This is automatically handled by the FlexRay controller. To be able to have a GEELYGeely Automotive Research Institute(Ningbo)Co.Ltd Document TypeNote-SWRS Document Release StatusRELEASED Document No Revision005 Volume No01 Page No203(1572) Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU safe way for a node to join a running cluster without knowing the currently active schedule, all schedules must have a common static part, preferably small, that is guaranteed to be static in all schedule configurations. This part must contain all sync slots. If all nodes are configured with the parameter pSingleSlotEnabled set to true they will startup with SlotMode equal to SINGLE and only transmit their configured sync frames until the FlexRay controller is reconfigured to extend transmissions to all frames (SlotMode equal to ALL), by issuing an ALL_SLOTS command. A non Sync node will not transmit anything in SlodMode SINGLE. The name pSingleSlotEnabled is changed to pKeySlotOnlyEnabled in later versions of the specification than FlexRay Communication System Protocol Specification, FlexRay Data Link Layer – External publications.After joining a cluster, a node must use the data received in the first slot of the common static part of the cycle to determine the currently active FlexRay schedule. The first word of the data is named the NetworkStatus parameter. If the received NetworkStatus parameter differs from the nodes current FlexRay schedule it has to restart the controller and reconfigure the schedule and re-perform the integration procedure. If the node determines that it has the correct schedule it will issue the ALL_SLOTS command and resume full operation. An ALL_SLOTS command only takes effect at the start of the following cycle, assuming that the application can receive and evaluate the current active schedule within the first cycle received. The single slot mode logic delays full operation one cycle. If the node starts with the correct schedule it is possible to start full operation in the first cycle. Defined in [FR_DL_6] Notes to the table above:See [FR_DL_6] FlexRay Communication System Protocol Specification for details.4.3.5 Guideline for quality factor signals4.3.5.1 Guideline for quality factor signals4.3.5.1.1 Introduction4.3.5.1.1 What is the purpose of this documentThe purpose of this guideline is to inform about a mechanism for providing subscribers to a signal with information about failures which will reduce the accuracy of the signal. This mechanism can be used by subscribers to mitigate customer symptoms and/or improve the ability to diagnose and rectify the vehicle. This guide line defines a method for publishers to define a Quality Factor, and subscribers to reacts to it to ensure that the QF provides the intended benefits. Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU 4.3.5.1.1.2 RisksIn the past, misunderstanding and therefore inappropriate use of this and similar mechanisms has sometimes had the opposite effect i.e. it has aggravated symptoms and made it harder to diagnose and rectify the vehicle with in some cases some severe costs as a consequence of the errenous hanling. Therefore it is of absolute importance that all affected participants agree upon and document when and how to behave on the different levels of quality factor values. There have been many problems caused by the functions in publishing ECUs calculating QFs wrongly and the functions in subscribing ECUs reacting wrongly to QFs even where they have been calculated correctly. It is vital therefore that designers of subscribing functions carefully check the behaviour of the publishing function and do NOT rely on them meeting this guide line. The level of accuracy or tolerances of a signal value is not of interest in this document and must be documented in another document, see section Who should read this document?.4.3.5.1.1.3 Who should read this documentThis document should be read by the system integrators, the component developers, the test engineers, and the function owners which are using or will use quality factor signals. They together must agree upon a strategy how to handle different levels of quality factor values and manually document it properly in the SWRS so all future users (senders and receivers) of a quality factor signal always know how a certain quality factor value must be treated.4.3.5.1.1.4 Definitions and Abbreviations Definition/Abbreviation Description ECU Electronic Control Unit DTC Diagnostic Trouble Code ERC Emission Related Component, FMEA Failure Modes and effects analysis NOS Network Operating Software. The standard software package which includes a component to handle network communications. Operating Cycle The Operating Cycle consists of the time between Power Up (alt. Wake Up) and Power Down (alt. Enter Sleep Mode) as specified by each node specification. E.g. the engine Operating (Driving) Cycle consists of engine start-up, and engine shutoff ('Engine start' is defined as the point at which normal, synchronized spark and fuel control is obtained or when the engine reaches a speed of 150 rpm below the normal, warmed-up idle speed (as determined in the drive position for vehicles equipped with an automatic transmission)) QF (or Q-factor) Quality Factor SWRS Software Requirement Specification 4.3.5.1.2 Software Component RecommendationsIn a distributed system where data is sent between different nodes over a network, normally the node generating/producing the data is the only node knowing the quality of the data (through a diagnostic function). To be able to inform the node using the data about the data quality, a 'quality factor' value (Q-factor) can be linked to the signal containing the data and sent over the network at the same time. The 'quality factor' indicates some status information about the data signal, e.g. if the value is inaccurate because of a faulty sensor, and can be used to make decision about replacement values/reconfiguration. Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU 4.3.5.1.2.1 QF values definition and use4.3.5.1.2.1.1 Value 3 - 11b OKThis value indicates that the signal is accurate and that the data it contains is truly representative of the real state.The accuracy of the transmitted signal under this normal operating condition should be stated in the signal definition in the SWRS.4.3.5.1.2.1.2 Value 2 - 10b Not within specificationThis value indicates that although the signal still contains data that is representative of the real state of the vehicle, a fault has been detected which indicates that the accuracy has been affected to an extent which may affect the performance or durability of exceptional subscribers. Which nodes that are typical subscribers, exceptional subscribers and the tolerance for the value 2 must be agreed in advance and the expected behaviour of subscribers must be well known and documented. The reduction in accuracy from that achieved with normal operation must be well documented. It is expected that only a small minority of subscribers to QFs will react to the value 2.Example: Engine torque calculation - if the primary input of mass air flow fails it is possible to determine engine torque using manifold pressure, but with a notable reduction in accuracy. Most users of the Torque signal will not be affected but the reduced accuracy may not be adequate to allow the optimum shift quality / durability compromise to be maintained in the transmission. In this case the transmission can change to a slightly jerkier, but still functional, shift behaviour with minimal effect on the customer4.3.5.1.2.1.3 Value 1 - 01b No data existsThis value indicates that the signal is set to its initial value because it has not yet been possible to measure or calculate real data. This situation may persist until the node power up sequence is fully completed (all applications have been executed at least once). The expected delay until real data is provided should be specified by the publishing node and/or function owner.The QF must change to a new appropriate value as soon as the application program has started to write fully valid information (this means that the real measurements and/or calculations are complete and enough time has elapsed for any filter function to have a valid output value) to the NOS.The receiving function must be designed to function correctly with no data for up to the maximum time defined above. After this time it should treat a QF value of 1 as identically equal to a QF value of 3 unless there is a clear and documented customer benefit for it to do otherwise. (This is to support legacy and minimise the customer impact)There must be no undocumented assumptions or interpretations of the QF! Example: receiving functions should not assume that they will always receive the value of 1 and should NOT attempt to use it as a reset marker. Some transmitting functions may be able to transmit valid data fast enough to catch the first transmission by the NOS.If there is a need for a more extensive information exchange for a specific feature, then this must be solved with a unique defined signal between the concerned functions, and shall not be solved by a undocumented interpretation of the standard QF.4.3.5.1.2.1.4 Value 0 - 00b FaultyThis value indicates that there is a serious fault which prevents the signal being correctly generated by the publisher. The publisher may store a DTC to indicate this. Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU Where there is ANY useful data potentially left in the signal under these conditions, this should be stated in the SWRS to allow subscribers to make an optimum judgement as to whether customer functionality can be preserved.Subscribers which can no longer provide safe and/or reliable customer function must default to a safe condition and if required store a DTC indicating what has happened. Note, as with the publisher, the subscriber must give careful consideration to whether it is actually necessary to remove customer function, particularly when the received signal is a secondary input to the function. It is not generally recommended that subscribers use the data when QF = 0 and extra care should be taken if the option is used.4.3.5.1.2.2 QF values definition and use summary tableThe following table summarises the specified behaviour of publishers and subscribers, but it is essential that the detailed definitions above are studied in addition. QF Publisher Typical Subscriber Exceptional subscriber Behaviour DTC Behaviour DTC Behaviour DTC 3 OK". The corresponding data signal is calculated within the stated accuracy. No Function works normally no reaction. No Function works normally no reaction. No 2 "Not within Specification". Signal subscribers should assume the corresponding data signal is calculated within a stated additional percentage of the stated accuracy. MC* Gracefully degraded performance specifically agreed and documented MC* 1 "No data exists" No data has yet been written to the NOS. No Function works normally no reaction. Normal operation must include any special measures needed to cope with initial delay to receive valid data No 0 "Faulty". The accuracy of the corresponding data signal is undefined. MC* Degraded or no performance. MC* Table: Summary of possible publisher/subscriber behaviour*Invalid data DTC:s are conditionally mandatory. The Base Technology Specification UDS Data specifies during what conditions DTC:s shall be set based on invalid data.4.3.5.1.2.3 Supporting information and clarifications from lessons learned4.3.5.1.2.3.1 DTCsIn the above notes DTCs are mentioned a number of times. These recommendations do not override the diagnostics requirements for the vehicle (typically specified by the UDS Data Specification) for example that a DTC should only be set in the subscriber where there is a Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU noticeable customer symptom, which might not occur if a QF <> 3 value only persisted for a short time. The publisher shall set a DTC if it has transmitted even a single value of 2 or 0. The reason is that the publisher cannot know how fast the subscribers will set DTCs and it is vital that if any subscriber has an DTC there is a corresponding publisher DTC to allow the root cause to be identified and rectified.Accuracy(after the initial period when QF might be 1 has expired)Define: True value of data: dt (i.e. as would be measured by lab instrumentation)Published value of data: dp (i.e. the value which appears on the bus)Normal error: Δn (i.e. the range of error possible with the publisher working correctly)Additional error: Δa (i.e. the error added by the faults which have been detected)if (dt - Δn ≤ dp ≤ dt + Δn) then QF = 3elseif (dt - (Δn + Δa) ≤ dp ≤ dt + (Δn + Δa)) then QF = 2else QF = 0Note: Δn and Δa to be defined and documented to the fullest extent possible4.3.5.1.2.3.2 Temporary errors and filteringIt is beyond the scope of this guideline to define how short duration faults should be handled in all cases. The basic question is "what if a disturbance of typically short duration occurs such as a voltage spike?". In this case the publisher may be temporarily unable to provide accurate data. If it is determined that the module must report a problem with the data due to low or high supply voltage, an appropriate QF value must be chosen depending on the accuracy of the data as for any other fault.4.3.5.1.2.3.3 Engine crankingA very important special case of a temporary inability to transmit correct data is during engine cranking, or more generally during changes of vehicle power states. There is a generally agreed principle that ECUs should detect cranking, and not react to problems of any sort, including unexpected QF values, or set DTCs until a suitable time has elapsed after the engine has started to be sure that full function of the electrical system has been restored. Of course the exception to this is ECU functions which are needed to enable the cranking process. Unfortunately there is not yet an agreed standard for all brands and vehicles as to how this should work and it also depends on the vehicle architecture.4.3.5.1.2.3.4 Detecting missing dataThe QF is just like any other signal as far as its transmission around the network is concerned. It is NOT modified in any way by passing through a gateway, nor changed if missing frames are detected. Other mechanisms exist to deal with these issues, and QFs should NOT be used for this purpose. The QF shall not and can not be used by the subscriber, to get information on whether or not the publisher function is reporting any data to the network transport layer. This shall be taken care of by an UB (UpdateBit) or other mechanism such as a message counter.4.3.5.1.2.3.5 Multiple variants of a nodeIn case different variants of one node exist (e.g. Engine Control Modules, Brake Control Modules...), these nodes shall ensure that they apply the same rules for generating QFs they send out across their variants. In this case, the receiver can always react in the same way on a specific QF signal received from different node variants, i.e. has a common interface to the variants. Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU 4.3.5.1.2.3.6 Data valueThe corresponding data signal to the QF signal shall always contain the actual measured/calculated value for the transmitted data. This is valid for all possible QF values. Only during initialization, this data signal may contain the init value defined in the signal SWRS.4.3.5.1.2.3.7 Philosophy and development of the QF conceptThis section is not formally part of the definition, but attempts to explain the logic for WHY the guideline has been written as it has, and the history of problems which have lead to this logic. It is vital to understand that the QF is a mechanism to assist the mitigation of faults for the benefit of the vehicle user only. It only has meaning as part of the design of a distributed function in which sharing of data contributes to delivering a customer feature. In the past the generation and use of quality factors have been done in isolation which has lead to publishing nodes setting low quality factor values too readily, and subscribing nodes having needlessly severe reactions. This combination produces a situation where the symptoms experienced by the customer in the vehicle may be far more severe than is actually justified by the fault which has occurred.The QF guideline can't cover all possible needs of data quality information, but is rather a generalized standard method that will fit the majority of needs. If there are exceptions that can't be handled within the framework defined in this spec, then the subscriber and publisher must agree upon a specific solution for their specific need.It is essential that each user of a QF checks that their reaction is appropriate to the behaviour of the publisher. It is expected that the FMEA of the function should indicate the effect on that function of an error in its incoming signals. This should inform whether a QF is needed at all, and what the correct reaction should be.In theory of course it may be that different users of a signal might have different accuracy thresholds where reactions were required. For this reason there may be cases where quality indication mechanisms not covered by this framework are needed. This spec does not forbid these. So far no case has been found where defining more than two different states of degradation produce additional benefit.4.3.5.1.2.3.8 History of QF 1The QF value of 1 requires some specific explanation, as it has caused confusion and debate in the past. This value was used in earlier versions of this specification as the initial value AND to indicate that although no fault had been detected, some diagnostic evaluation was still ongoing. The classic example of this is the coolant temperature. OBD legislation requires that this is monitored to make sure the engine is genuinely warming up correctly. This evaluation inevitably takes many minutes, and there may indeed be usage patterns of the vehicle where the evaluation is never completed.There is no conceivable customer function on the vehicle which could not operate for several minutes after start, and in some usage patterns not operate at all. Therefore there was no useful way in which a subscriber could react in any other way to the value of 1 than to treat it exactly the same as 3. Unfortunately many subscribers followed a wrong but understandable logic that because 2 was worse than 3 and 0 was worse than 2; then 1 must also be worse than 2. This created fundamentally wrong behaviour in the vehicle which required software changes to correct it.The definition of QF 1 now should eliminate this doubt, but subscribing functions should be designed where possible to work correctly with publishing functions with the earlier behaviour to avoid the cost and risk of changing the publishing function.If there is a need for a more extensive information exchange for a specific feature, then this Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU must be solved with a unique defined signal between the concerned functions, and shall not be solved by a undocumented use of the standard QF.An example of this has been raised in the late stages of development of this version of the specification. This occurs in vehicles where the steering angle sensor can only detect movement of the steering wheel and not its absolute position. An absolute position is established by learning the straight ahead position by correlating with wheel speeds and yaw rate. This takes some time and clearly can only happen with the vehicle moving. The straight ahead position is remembered when the power is off, but if the steering wheel is moved with power off, there will be an error until a new straight ahead position is learned. None of the defined QF values in this spec allow for this, so a further signal indicating completion of the learning process had to be added to the vehicle4.3.5.1.2.4 Recommendations for creation of QF:sThe Quality Factor (QF) should handle and carry the quality number (value) of the data transmitted on the vehicle network.The Quality Factor should be a 2-bit signal.The Quality Factor signal should be transmitted in a signal group with the corresponding data signal. Note: The Quality Factor should be written by the application at the same time as the corresponding data signal without any interruption in between.The Quality Factor signal value should reflect the status of its corresponding data by using the following values, these are universally defined in section QF values definition and use:11b "OK"10b "Not within Specification"01b "No data exists"00b "Faulty"The initial value of the Quality Factor signal should be 01b.The conditions for the Quality Factor states and state transitions must be specified and documented (through state-transition diagrams and/or text in the SWRS document). It is the responsibility of the person owning the specification of how a particular data signal is calculated to document a complete and unambiguous specification of how the associated QF is to be calculated.It is not allowed to use QF data as the cause of setting an OBD (and thus ERC classified) DTC.4.3.6 LIN Data Link Layer4.3.6.1 LIN Data Link Layer - Generic Requirements4.3.6.1.1 Data Link Layer Requirements

title: Low Battery Voltage Operation
body: 483 v3 Low Battery Voltage OperationVersion history: ![](images/9617d3b99625324fff5a01f2a96f1985c20f17ebaf0c5dadc23b01dd25d27928.jpg) GEELY Geely Automotive Research Institute (Ningbo)Co.Ltd Document Type Note-SWRS Document Release Status RELEASED Document No Revision 005 Volume No 01 Page No 218(1572) Document Name Base Tech SWRS DHU (3): Change the Verification Method to Test Purpose: Source: Verification Method: Test Legacy ID: 53535v1 For 0 < Vbatt ECU < 8.0 volts the bus may operate in either the normal or the passive mode.
