A network may consist of several busses, electrically isolated from each other. Dominant/Recessive The bus can have one of two complementary logical values: “dominant” or “recessive”. See LIN Specification Package Revision 2.1, LIN Datalink Layer - Requisite documents, for the definition of dominant and recessive. During simultaneous transmission of “dominant” and “recessive” bits, the resulting bus value will be “dominant”. Network A set of electronic and cabling devices facilitating the multidirectional exchange of information encoded in serial form. Each electronic device (in this case: ECU) is equipped with a specific, standardized electronic interface in order to guarantee compatibility between exchanged binary items of information. Normal mode LIN node communication during operational voltages ranges and non faulty conditions. (100 ms at 30 fps).4.3.7.1.2 LVDS Data Link Layer - GMSL2This section describes how the video links using Maxim Integrated GMSL2 chipset shall be implemented.4.3.7.1.2.1 GMSL2 chipset selectionFor each LVDS network using GMSL2 there shall be one serializer and one deserializer. The serializer is located in the ECU containing the video source and the deserializer is located in the ECU containing the video sink. E.g. A camera will generate a video stream (video source) and a display will receive a video stream (video sink), hence the camera will contain a serializer and the display will contain a deserializer. A gateway node will be both a video sink and video source depending on which of the connected video links are referred.The choice of GMSL2 chipset shall be dependent on the needs of the application in the connected ECUs (e.g. resolution, video interfaces etc.) and is not specified in this specification. The chipset selection shall be verified and approved by the responsible authority appointed by the OEM, but Maxim Integrated needs to verify the compatibility of the chosen GMSL2 chips.Requirements from this section are defined in section “Requirements from section GMSL2 chipset selection”. Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU 4.3.7.1.2.2 LINoverLVDS datalink layer on GMSL2The Datalink Layer for a LINoverLVDS implementation using GMSL2 (Gigabit Multimedia Serial Link) shall be implemented as specified in this section.The implementation defined in this section shall be compliant to the datasheets from Maxim Integrated for the chosen chipset. The requirements described in this section defines how the datalink layer for the OEM shall be implemented on top of Maxim Integrated GMSL2.The ECU is not allowed to modify the concept unless it is approved by the responsible authority appointed by the OEM.4.3.7.1.2.2.1 Software component descriptionThis section describes how the LINoverLVDS on GMSL2 software component shall be implemented.LINoverLVDS on GMSL2 specifies a concept for communicate data over the UART control channel integrated in the Maxim Integrated chipset. The GMSL2 chipset interleave a half-duplex control channel together with the high-speed video stream sent from the video source to the video sink (see figure LINoverLVDS on GMSL2 Link Concept overview). The control channel can be used both for reading registers in the GMSL2 chipset and communication between the MCUs integrated in the ECUs. The control channel requires a higher-level protocol implementation in order to avoid collisions on the link etc. which is described in this specification. This is further described in Section: LINoverLVDS on GMSL2 protocol.The LINoverLVDS on GMSL2 is based on LIN, but has a different characteristic. Hence, the LIN specification is applicable as long as this specification does not specify otherwise. This is further described in Section: LIN inheritance for LINoverLVDS.The LINoverLVDS on GMSL2 datalink layer needs to be implemented as a part of the ECU Software. The GMSL2 physical interface needs low level drivers in combination with higher level functionality to make full use of the built-in functionality of the GMSL2 chipset (e.g. settings for equalization, pre-emphasis, video format etc.).The protocol is a point-to-point network and defines one diagnostic master, and one diagnostic slave. The diagnostic master is the ECU in charge of the communication on the control channel. The diagnostic slave will only communicate on the control channel when data is requested by the diagnostic master. This is further described in Section: Diagnostic master and diagnostic slave.A concept overview is given in Figure: LINoverLVDS on GMSL2 Link Concept overview. This section describes the OEM’s additions to that protocol. The speed on the UART channel shall be decided by the nodes of the GMSL2 network in order to meet the system requirements for software download and the requirements of the application. A minimum of 416kbps shall be used. When a node is active on the LVDS network it shall not fail to read frames, and identify and respond to headers on the bus, regardless of the internal processes of the ECU. Requirements from this section are defined in section “LINoverLVDS on GMSL2 protocol”. ## 4.3.7.1.2.2.2.1 Diagnostic master and diagnostic slave For each LVDS network there will be one diagnostic master and one diagnostic slave. A diagnostic master can have either a serializer or a deserializer and the same goes for a diagnostic slave. This is dependent on the application and is decided by the responsible authority appointed by the OEM. GEELYGeely Automotive Research Institute(Ningbo)Co.Ltd Document TypeNote-SWRS Document Release StatusRELEASED Document No Revision005 Volume No01 Page No249(1572) Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU The diagnostic master is responsible for initiation of the communication on the control channel. This also includes readout and writing data to the registers in the GMSL2 chipset, both on the local side and the remote side.If the communication on the control channel is lost, it is the diagnostic master which is responsible for reinitiating the communication. This also incorporates a loss of the complete video link.4.3.7.1.2.2.2.2 Power-up and power-downWhen power is supplied the GMSL2 link shall boot-up and establish the link fast. The diagnostic master shall be able to send first header within 250ms after power has been supplied or a hardware reset has been performed. If this is the case the LVDS link PLL shall be locked within 100ms. The diagnostic slave node shall be able to transmit valid data within 100ms after power has been supplied or a hardware reset has been performed. The slave shall not answer until it has valid data to transmit.If the above scenario cannot be met, the OEM appointed authority shall approve a scenario where the master node shall be able to transmit the first header 150ms after the PLL for the LVDS link is locked.4.3.7.1.2.2.2.3 Configuration of registers in the GMSL2 chipsetIn order to have a way of changing the default register settings in the GMSL2 chipset a configuration module shall be included in the diagnostic master. When the GMSL2 link is powered up the diagnostic master shall, after the diagnostic slave has set all its default register settings, set all registers specified in the configuration module, in the specific order. The configuration module may include register settings for both the serializer and the deserializer and the diagnostic master shall implement a way to handle this. It shall be possible to update the configuration module separately using software download. An overview can be found in Figure: Generic overview of a diagnostic master and diagnostic slave and the configuration module placement.The Diagnostic slave shall minimize the need of setting registers from the Diagnostic master by using the hardware interface of the GMSL2 chip in the slave ECU, to boot-up with the correct register settings. The timing restrictions for the interval between header and data in a frame are defined in Figure: time between the header and data of type 1 and type 2 messages. ![](images/08b4d99b7130baf7fafc4482c2366a30c18d7d2583743bcd8cb22857a826453c.jpg) Figure: interval time between in each data byte in type 1 messages Document TypeNote-SWRS Document Release StatusRELEASED Document No Revision005 Volume No01 Page No257(1572) Geely Automotive Research Institute (Ningbo)Co.Ltd ![](images/8eecd30976a318047cfbf293ca5a3f9714c05606a2c1fc9d65b4e9999d6d6c5a.jpg) Figure: interval time between in each data byte in type 2 messages Type 1 message ![](images/7118d3ef111f12fa239d446cb125019b63a90152ff0f944bbdfa8ae802808d77.jpg) Type 2 message ![](images/7df249fdba4b8f514592caaa6ac66ce1d0880b4d5e366aeb28f26bc894253b8c.jpg) Figure: time between the header and data of type 1 and type 2 messages GEELYGeely Automotive Research Institute(Ningbo)Co.Ltd Document TypeNote-SWRS Document Release StatusRELEASED Document No Revision005 Volume No01 Page No258(1572) Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU 4.3.7.1.2.2.3.4 Message definitionThe messages that shall be sent over the GMSL2 link in default session shall be defined in a .ldf file.At least the following messages shall be implemented and sent over the GMSL2 link in default session:VehCfgPrmDiag command request and Diag command response4.3.7.1.2.2.4 Sleep and wake up strategiesThe behavior of an ECU connected to a GMSL2 link where sleep and wakeup are supported is specified in this section.To reduce the power consumption of the GMSL2 chipset, a sleep mode can be entered. In the sleep mode, all register settings keep their programmed values and all functions in the chipset are powered down, except for the wakeup detectors on the local control interface, and the serial link. Any activity seen by the wakeup detectors temporarily turns on the control channel. During this time, a microcontroller can command the chipset to exit sleep mode.A request for setting the GMSL2 link into sleep mode will not necessarily enforce the slave node into a low-power mode. The application of the slave node may still be active after the go to sleep command has been received. This behavior is application specific.A sleep command shall be defined in the message definition file for the LVDS link (.ldf file). This command shall be sent before the GMSL2 chipset is set into sleep mode.The wakeup scenario is shown in Figure: Diagnostic master sends wake up request. When a diagnostic master sends a wakeup request (first header) due to a local event. The debouncing time is not included in the figure. The first header is sent within a specific time (mwt). After being woken up the slave node is ready to transmit valid data within a specific time (sd). The diagnostic slave shall not respond until the data is valid. The diagnostic master shall take this delay into account. Specific subsystems that require a faster wakeup response time can be defined in the subsystem application requirements. local event at t=0, mwt<100ms, sd<100msmwt is the master wake up timesd is the slave wake up delay Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU Figure: Diagnostic master sends wake up requestRequirements from this section are defined in section “Requirements from section Sleep and Wakeup strategies”.4.3.7.1.2.2.5 Access to GMSL2 parametersThe GMSL2 chipset includes a set of built-in parameters, used for monitoring the status of the link. These parameters need to be accessed from the upper layer software in the diagnostic master, but the slave GMSL2 chip needs to provide the status registers over the link.Requirements from this section are defined in section “Requirements from section Access to GMSL2 parameters”.4.3.7.1.2.2.6 LIN inheritance for LINoverLVDSThe LINoverLVDS for GMSL2 is inheriting some concepts from LIN (see [ LIN_DL_2]), hence the name LINoverLVDS. The concepts which have been inherited are described in this section.4.3.7.1.2.2.6.1 Request response protocolLINoverLVDS is a request response protocol in the same way as LIN protocol. The master shall send data using type 1 messages, and request data using the type 2 messages (See section LINoverLVDS on GMSL2 messages). The slave is never allowed to initiate communication on the control channel, due to risk of collisions.4.3.7.1.2.2.6.2 Message scheduling on LINoverLVDSLINoverLVDS messages are scheduled in the same way as LIN protocol. To specify the application message schedule an .ldf-file should be used. In PBL and SBL the diagnostics shall be gatewayed as fast as possible.Each event triggered signal shall have a heartbeat, which means that the signal shall be re-sent every 1 second.The diagnostic commands can consist of more data than 255 bytes, which is the maximum amount to fit into one LINoverLVDS on GMSL2 message. Therefore, Diagnostic message (MSG ID:0x00 3C and 0x00 3D) shall use the transport layer defined in the specification GMSL2 Control Transport Layer Specification [ GMSL2_TP ]. Diagnostic messages shall always have “Number of bytes (N)” set to 0xFF, since the payload length will be of different sizes. If not all bytes in the LINoverLVDS on GMSL2 message are used, the remaining bytes Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU shall be set to 0xFF.A message including the vehicle speed needs to be implemented, in order to meet the “Check programming pre-condition” routine control defined on a UDS level.A generic example of a message table is defined below: MSG ID Message Name Message Type Consumer Loop Time Note 0x00 20 Interrupt Status Information Type 1 Event triggered by INT = High 0x00 3C Diag Command Request Type 1 Slave ECU Event, no cyclic time1 0x00 3D Diag Command Response Type 2 Master ECU Event, no cyclic time1 0x00 06 ProfPenSts1 Type 1 Slave ECU Event, no cyclic time1 0x00 07 SaveSetgToMem Prmnt Type 1 Slave ECU Event, no cyclic time1 0x00 09 VehCfgPrm Type 1 Slave ECU Cyclic2 1 Event triggered signals shall have a heartbeat signal to enable detection of lost communication, see requirement Req31 Event triggered signals heartbeat2 Shall be cyclic only during first 30 seconds at the beginning of every driving cycle, and then not sent anymore. Period time shall be the same as incoming CC signal to Master ECU.A generic ECU example belowAn event is defined as any change of the signal value.Event driven messages except Interrupt Status Information are sent to message interval of cyclic messages, and cyclic time is kept for cyclic messages.Valid messageWhen PBL is activated and Programming Session is in progress MSG ID Message Name Valid/Invalid 0x00 09 VehCfgPrm Invalid 0x00 20 Interrupt Status Information Valid 0x00 3C Diag Command Request Valid 0x00 3D Diag Command Response Valid Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU When application is activated (no matter when Default Session or Extended Session is in progress) MSG ID Message Name Valid/Invalid 0x00 09 VehCfgPrm Valid 0x00 20 Interrupt StatusInformation Valid 0x003C Diag CommandRequest Valid 0x003D Diag CommandResponse Valid Requirements from this section are defined in section “Requirements from section Message scheduling on LINoverLVDS”.4.3.7.1.2.3 IPoverLVDS datalink layer on GMSL2The Datalink Layer for an IPoverLVDS implementation using GMSL2 (Gigabit Multimedia Serial Link) shall be implemented as specified in this section.The implementation defined in this section shall be compliant to the datasheets from Maxim Integrated for the chosen chipset. The requirements described in this section defines how the datalink layer for the OEM shall be implemented on top of Maxim Integrated GMSL2.The ECU is not allowed to modify the concept unless it is approved by the responsible authority appointed by the OEM.4.3.7.1.2.3.1 Software component descriptionThis section describes how the IPoverLVDS on GMSL2 software component shall be implemented.IPoverLVDS on GMSL2 specifies a concept for communicate data over the RGMII (Reduced gigabit media-independent interface) control channel integrated in the Maxim Integrated chipset. The GMSL2 chipset allows for adding an Ethernet bridge (full duplex) over the high-speed video stream sent from the video source to the video sink (see figure IPoverLVDS on GMSL2 Link Concept overview).The bridge can be used for application communication between the MCUs integrated in the ECUs connected to the link. The ethernet bridge requires a higher-level protocol implementation which is described in this specification. The protocol to implement on top of the ethernet bridge is IP communication (Network layer in the OSI-model and above).Since the media independent interface (MII) on the GMSL2 chipset allows for connecting any PHY to the MAC, the communication link can be seen as a regular DoIP connection. Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU NOTE: This concept is only applicable for some of the display links. Since it is only a subset of the GMSL2 chipset that have the RGMII interface, this need to be taken into consideration when choosing chipset for the ECUs. This will also require more of the MCUs in the ECUs, since a DoIP stack needs to be implemented. So, this concept shall only be used if the transferring speed of the application data sent together with the video stream requires it.In order to access the built-in functionality in the GMSL2 chipset the diagnostic master needs to be connected to the UART channel. The Diagnostic master will handle all register settings and link diagnostics. If some link diagnostics can only be performed on the Diagnostic slave side, the information will be sent over the Ethernet bridge. This is further described in Section:Diagnostic master and diagnostic slave.The IPoverLVDS on GMSL2 datalink layer needs to be implemented as a part of the ECU Software. The GMSL2 physical interface needs low level drivers in combination with higher level functionality to make full use of the built-in functionality of the GMSL2 chipset (e.g. settings for equalization, pre-emphasis, video format etc.).A concept overview is given in Figure: IPoverLVDS on GMSL2 Link Concept overview. Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU 4.3.7.1.2.3.2 IPoverLVDS on GMSL2 protocolWhen the control channel data is sent over the ethernet bridge, the communication shall be transparent, thus the endpoint sources and sinks are defining what actual protocol to use. The default shall however be to use UDP for one-way traffic and TCP/IP if two-way traffic termination is needed. As control channel protocol the IP Command Protocol shall be used when Ethernet protocol handles application, diagnostics and SWDL functionality.Design Rule: If proprietary the OEM applications intend to communicate internally within the vehicle network between IP based ECU's and when there is a need of a control channel, the IP Command Protocol specification shall be used. The IP Command Protocol specification provides requirements and guidelines how the data shall be exchanged between the ECU's. If the application under development is based on a known protocol (standardized framework), this should be stated in the corresponding IP Signal Content specification (SWRS) and does not need to use the IP Command Protocol. Example: the usage of FTP (RFC-959) would mean that this specification is not needed. The OEM delivers a set of specification which shall be used together. The IP Command Protocol which contains requirements and design guidelines which must be used for the implementations.The usage of Ethernet in automotive applications are defined in the Ethernet specifications, Internetwork specification and IP Routing specification.4.3.7.1.2.3.2.1 Diagnostic master and diagnostic slaveFor each GMSL2 network there will be one diagnostic master and one diagnostic slave. A diagnostic master can have either a serializer or a deserializer and the same goes for a diagnostic slave. This is dependent on the application and is decided by the responsible authority appointed by the OEM.The diagnostic master is responsible for the communication on the UART control channel. This includes readout and writing data to the registers in the GMSL2 chipset, both on the local side and the remote side.If the communication on the control channel is lost, it is the diagnostic master which is responsible for reinitiating the communication. This also incorporates a loss of the complete video link.The diagnostic slave shall not be connected to the UART channel of its GMSL2 chip.4.3.7.1.2.3.2.2 Configuration of registers in GMSL2 chipsetIn order to have a way of changing the default register settings in the GMSL2 chipset a configuration module shall be included in the diagnostic master. When the GMSL2 link is powered up the diagnostic master shall set all registers specified in the configuration module, in the specific order. The configuration module may include register settings for both the serializer and the deserializer and the diagnostic master shall implement a way to handle this. It shall be possible to update the configuration module separately using software download. An overview can be found in Figure: Generic overview of a diagnostic master and diagnostic slave and the Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU local configuration placement.The Diagnostic slave shall minimize the need of setting registers from the Diagnostic master by using the hardware interface of the GMSL2 chip in the slave ECU, to boot-up with the correct register settings. Figure: Generic overview of a diagnostic master and diagnostic slave and the local configuration placement.4.3.7.1.2.3.3 Sleep and wake up strategiesThe behavior of an ECU connected to an GMSL2 link where sleep and wakeup are supported is specified in this section.To reduce the power consumption of the GMSL2 chipset, a sleep mode can be entered. In the sleep mode, all register settings keep their programmed values and all functions in the chipset are powered down, except for the wakeup detectors on the local control interface, and the serial link. Any activity seen by the wakeup detectors temporarily turns on the control channel. During this time, a microcontroller can command the chipset to exit sleep mode.A request for setting the GMSL2 link into sleep mode will not necessarily enforce the slave node into a low-power mode. The application of the slave node may still be active after the go to sleep command has been received. This behavior is application specific.If the diagnostic slave application shall be set into sleep mode, the diagnostic master needs to send a sleep command to notify the slave before the GMSL2 chipset is set in sleep mode. The sleep command shall be defined by the tier1s of the ECUs connected to the link.The wakeup scenario is shown in Figure: Diagnostic master sends wake up request. When a diagnostic master sends a wakeup request (first header) due to a local event. The debouncing Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU time is not included in the figure. The first header is sent within a specific time (mwt). After being woken up the slave node is ready to transmit valid data within a specific time (sd). The diagnostic slave shall not respond until the data is valid. The diagnostic master shall take this delay into account. Specific subsystems that require a faster wakeup response time can be defined in the subsystem application requirements. Figure: Diagnostic master sends wake up requestRequirements from this section are defined in section “Requirements from section Sleep and Wakeup strategies”.4.3.7.1.2.3.4 Access to GMSL2 parametersThe GMSL2 chipset includes a set of built-in parameters, used for monitoring the status of the link. These parameters need to be accessed from the upper layer software in the diagnostic master, but the slave GMSL2 chip needs to provide the status registers.Requirements from this section are defined in section “Requirements from section Access to GMSL2 parameters”.4.3.7.1.2.4 ECU (Computer) Resource4.3.7.1.2.4.1 Power supply and resetThis section describes how power supply and reset should be handled.The power supply voltage level at the node shall be measured continuously. HW and SW inaccuracy in the monitoring of the supply voltage level must be considered when the ECU is designed. The ECU must meet this operating voltage range requirement also in a worst-case condition.Network communication is permitted outside the specified voltage range, provided that the ECU can correctly read and write messages and not cause any disturbance on the network. Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU There must be margins in both ends of the operating voltage range in regard to the voltage level where communication becomes unreliable or is no longer possible due hardware constraints. See Figure: Power supply range. Figure: Power supply rangeRequirements from this section are defined in section “Requirements from section Power supply and reset”.4.3.7.1.2.4.2 System level resourceThis section describes the requirements set for the system level resources of the GMSL2 system.Requirements from this section are defined in section “Requirements from section System level resource”.4.3.7.1.2.4.2.1 Internal propagation delayThis section is applicable for gateway nodes. Connected to GMSL2 networks.When the video traffic is handled the internal propagation delay (measured between controller input/output and ECU connector) shall be kept to a minimum.For the video traffic the delay is measured in frame delays. A maximum of three video frames Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU are allowed when rescale, rotate, resample, coding/decoding of video frame are performed. Otherwise the internal propagation delay is maximum two video frames.For data traffic over the UART control channel, the internal propagation delay shall be less than the serialization time of 10 bytes.For data traffic sent over the ethernet bridge, the internal propagation delay shall be less than the serialization time for 256 bytes.To enable full duplex Ethernet two-way traffic response, when the ECU act as ethernet repeater, the Round-Trip Propagation Delay shall be less than 140 Bit Times. If the ECU act as a transparent cable the Round-Trip delay shall be less than 11.1 Bit Times, 1/10th of maximum cable segment length (111.2 (Bit Times) = 100 Meters cable), and shall allow up to 5 units and 50 meters of cable in series in the Ethernet network.4.3.7.1.2.4.2.2 Start up timeIn order to have a responsive system, the startup time between two nodes shall be set to be maximum 64ms from system power-on until the link is established.4.3.7.1.2.4.3 Hardware componentsThe hardware components in the nodes connected to the GMSL2 link shall allow for premium video to be sent over the link.The bit error rate for the video link shall be less than 10-9/s. It is allowed to measure the bit error rate over 8 selected bits per pixel.The deserializer shall be robust against bursts of bit errors. It should be able to handle up to three pixels of bit errors. The burst must not cause any column displacements of the pixels, comprising a line.4.3.7.1.2.5 Hardware resource utilizationIf a GMSL2 gateway node has a long boot-up time, it is required to implement a by-pass mode which gateways video prior to it being fully booted. In this by-pass mode, the UART control channel is not mandatory.Requirements from this section are defined in section “Requirements from section Hardware resource utilization”.4.3.7.1.3 Requisite documents Reference Document [LIN_DL_2] LIN Specification Package Revision 2.1 [GMSL2_TP] GMSL2 Control Transport Layer Specification 4.3.7.1.4 Definitions and Abbreviations Definition Description Figure: IPoverLVDS on GMSL2 Link Concept overview GEELYGeely Automotive Research Institute(Ningbo)Co.Ltd Document TypeNote-SWRS Document Release StatusRELEASED Document No Revision005 Volume No01 Page No268(1572) Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU LVDS Low-Voltage Differential Signaling. This term is used in the present document in a wider sense, which is to say that it includes several technologies which utilize a differential signaling scheme with a low-voltage swing; such as Current-Mode Logic (CML, ±800mV), Low-Voltage Positive-Emitter-Coupled Logic (LVPECL, ±800mV), B-LVDS (Bus-LVDS, ±550mV), GMSL (Gigabit Multimedia Serial Link, ±350mV), LDI (LVDS Display Interface, ±350mV), openLDI (±350mV) as well as “pure LVDS” in its original sense with referral to the TIA/EIA-644 standard (±350mV). Serializer A single shift register that receives the parallel data once per parallel clock, and shifts it out to the higher serial clock rate (Parallel in Serial out). Deserializer A device divides the incoming clock down to the parallel rate. There are two registers connected as a double buffer: one is used to clock in the serial stream, and the other is used to hold the data for the slower, parallel side. Source A device which produce a collection of data including text, graphics, images, audio and video. Sink A device which process and present data. Node Electronic Control Module. In this context is a node the same as an ECU. Device In this context a device is the same as an electronic component. Abbreviation Description N/A Not Applicable IP Internet Protocol. The IP is the principal communications protocol used for relaying datagrams (packets) across an internetwork using the Internet Protocol Suite. SW SoftWare ECU Electronic Control Unit. Electronic control unit with a computer/microcontroller. TCP Transmission Control Protocol. TCP is one of the core protocols of the Internet Protocol Suite. TCP is one of the two original components of the suite, complementing the IP, and therefore the entire suite is commonly referred to as TCP/IP. LIN Local Interconnect Network. Low speed single wire network TBD To Be Defined 4.3.7.2 LVDS Data Link Layer - 1-wire reqs4.3.7.2.1 Compatibility

title: Bus speed
body: 1110 v2 Bus speed Version history:(2): Change the Verification Method from Test to Analysis+TestPurpose: To be able to use .ldf files, according to LIN standardSource:Verification Method: Analysis AND TestLegacy ID: 433901v0All modules shall be capable of operating at the nominal bus speeds of 9.6kbps or 19.2kbps, forbackward compatibility. The operating speed shall be defined on a bus by bus basis. The bus speed shall be 400 kbps (I2C fast-mode) in high speed mode, but the virtual bus speed shall be possible to limit to 19.2kbps. The virtual bus speed shall be implemented by adding a delay, on the Master side, between two consecutive messages sent on the bus. The delay shall be calculated based upon last message length, in bits, using preset bus speed and the requested nominal bus speeds of 9.6kbps or 19.2kbps, in the way that the average actual bus speeds will become 9.6kbps or 19.2kbps (setting dependent). Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU The Host I2C bitrate shall be set to 400kbit/s and the Remote I2C bitrate shall be 400kbit/s. The communication speed is set in the LVDS chipset registers by Master ECU, and is controlled by using different frequencies for SCL.

title: Built-in monitoring of link quality
body: 1126 v3 Built-in monitoring of link qualityVersion history:(3):Purpose: To monitor the link quality in a simple way.Source: DPR-LVDS-NETWORK-005:Req23v1Verification Method: Test + AnalysisLegacy ID: 345436v2It shall be possible to monitor the quality of the forward video channel on the deserializer side through a dedicated error counter. It shall also be possible to clear the error counter. The deserializer shall indicate the link status in terms of the existence, or absence, of a successful synchronization to the clock of the transmitted stream.It shall be possible to read out and clear the error counter, as well as to read out the link status, by means of standard diagnostic commands over standard vehicle networks, such as LIN, CAN or Flexray. If the ECU does not have such a connection, it shall be possible to do this over the control channel of the LVDS link.Implementation: Deserializer, Accessed from the Diagnostics master, over the LVDS link, optionally other access.Qualification method: Analysis, documentation of test results.

Status Code (3 byte) Name Description Byte 0[0..6] Don't Care Don't Care Byte 0[7] Lock Lock data status register Byte 1 AshellComm Error Ashell Communication Error register Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU Byte 2[0..7] Reserved Reserved Other control channel protocol implementations can be approved, if agreed between the OEM and both suppliers of the transceiver and the receiver side have agreed about the control channel implementation.Qualification method:Analysis, documentation of test results.4.3.7.3.1.4 Protocol over Ethernet Link (4-wire Eth)When the control channel is handled over the Ethernet communication protocol, the communication shall be transparent, thus the endpoint sources and sinks are defining what actualprotocol to use. The default shall however be the suggestion to use UDP for one way traffic and TCP/IP if two way traffic termination is needed. As Control Channel protocol the IP Command Protocol shall be used when Ethernet protocol handles application, diagnostics and SWDL functionality.The LVDS control channel over Ethernet must be able to perform diagnostics over the LVDS link.The methods for diagnostics must be compliant to the [LVDS_Generic:11]UDS Services and [LVDS_GENERIC:13]UDSonIP.Overall requirement of SWDL for private nodes in “General Software Download” [LVDS_GENERIC:5] shall be followed when the LVDS control channel over Ethernet is used.The Internetwork specification [LVDS_APIX_Eth:2] and IP Routing specification [LVDS_APIX_Eth:3] defines a set of rules that must be considered and fulfilled when designing/using the IP Command Protocol [LVDS_APIX_Eth:3] and the control signals used by the applications (which is handled in separate documents).Design Rule: If applications (proprietary) intend to communicate internally within the vehicle network between IP based ECU's and when there is a need of a control channel, this specification (IP Command Protocol) shall be used. The IP Command Protocol specification provides requirements and guidelines how the data shall be exchanged between the ECU's. If the application under development is based on a known protocol (standardized framework), this should be stated in the corresponding IP Signal Content specification (SWRS) and does not need to use the IP Command Protocol). Example the usage of FTP (RFC-959) would mean that this specification is not needed. The Base Tech SWRS includes a set of specification which shall be used together. The IP Command Protocol that contains requirements and design guidelines which must be used for the implementations.The IP Command Bus which defines services which is offered by servers.

title: HDCP support
body: 1094 v3 HDCP support Version history:(3):Purpose: Playback of high-resolution Blu-ray video requires encryption of all links between different nodes by means of HDCP.Source:Verification Method: Test + AnalysisLegacy ID: 345421v2In case the LVDS link is used to transfer HDCP-encrypted video, e.g. Blu-ray, then both the serializer and deserializer of the link shall have built-in HDCP-support.Implementation: One wire, Two wire and Four wire LVDS link with HD video contents over the video link.Qualification method: Analysis, documentation of test results.

title: Link Package Format
body: 1098 v2 Link Package Format Version history:(2):Purpose: In order to support pixel level interleaving, bit coding is needed.Source:Verification Method: Test + AnalysisLegacy ID: 345422v1Each package shall contain 30-bits: Bit position Field name Description 0-7 R Color data RGB, red 8-15 G Color data RGB, green 16-23 B Color data RGB, blue 24 V Toggling bit for line 25 H Toggling bit for frame 26 E Image enable 27*-28* ID* Source ID* 29* F* Function bit* GEELYGeely Automotive Research Institute(Ningbo)Co.Ltd Document TypeNote-SWRS Document Release StatusRELEASED Document No Revision005 Volume No01 Page No319(1572) Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU Figure: Line formatR[0:7] G[8:15] B[16:23] V[24] H[25] E[26] ID[27:28]* F[29]** For non-interleaved links, these bits are not used.In presence of I2S, these bits can be used only for non-interleaved links.Other format of video link package can be approved, if agreed between the OEM and both suppliers of the transceiver and the receiver side have agreed about the common link video packet format . (RGB 888, YCbCr 4:4:4, YCbCr 4:2:2, YCbCr 4:2:0, etc.)However at any time, the transceiver/receiver supplier requirements for the packet format must be fulfilled.Qualification method: Analysis, Documentation of test results.

title: Video stream multiplex
body: 1101 v3 Video stream multiplex Version history:(3):Purpose: Some links may require multiple video streams to be transmitted simultaneously. This will require time division multiplex.Source:Verification Method: Test + AnalysisLegacy ID: 345423v2If multiple video streams need to be transmitted over a single LVDS-link then they shall be multiplexed at the pixel level. The pixels at the sending side enter FIFO-buffers. A prioritizer monitors the occupancy level of the buffers and allows the most critical buffer to transmit. Since each pixel is tagged with an ID-code the receiver can separate the streams as necessary.The demultiplexer shall regenerate the original pixel clock for each demultiplexed video stream, in accordance with the pixel clock of the respective source. The information about the pixel clocks of the sources shall be transmitted over the control channel.Hsync and Vsync shall be regenerated on the receiver side in accordance with the VESA-CVT-R standard for timing with reduced blanking. Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU Implementation: Interleaved links on two-wire LVDS. Optionally for four-wire LVDS, see below addition.Other format of interleaved video link package can be approved, if agreed between the OEM and both suppliers of the transceiver and the receiver side have agreed about the common interleaved link video packet format.For four-wire LVDS the selected transceiver and receiver can have HW supported video streams interleaving, in that case the preferred solution shall use the present multiple HW video stream implementation.However at any time, the transceiver/receiver manufacturer requirements for the packet format must be fulfilled.Qualification method: Documentation, Documentation of test results.There may be a need to send more than one video stream simultaneously over one and the same link, i.e., to multiplex these streams. Should this be needed, multiplexing for the two different LVDS solutions is described in the present specification as part of the general concept of LVDS in vehicles.If multiple video streams need to be transmitted over a single LVDS-link then they shall be multiplexed at the pixel level. The pixels at the sending side enter FIFO-buffers. A prioritizer monitors the occupancy level of the buffers and allows the most critical buffer to transmit. Since each pixel is tagged with an ID-code the receiver can separate the streams as necessary.The demultiplexer shall regenerate the original pixel clock for each demultiplexed video stream, in accordance with the pixel clock of the respective source. The information about the pixel clocks of the sources shall be transmitted over the control channel.Hsync and Vsync shall be regenerated on the receiver side in accordance with the VESA-CVT-R standard for timing with reduced blanking.For two wire LVDS physical interfaces shall optionally allow transfer of up to 2 video streams, by over time multiplex or pixel merging within the same physical end interfaces – Both sides Tx and Rx must be capable to maintain the same pixel interleaving (time or wire multiplexing).Example: Channel 1 has a pixel-clock with 56MHz and Channel 2 has 16MHz this gives that Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU the LVDS link clock has to be at least 72MHz (LVDS is made for maximum 78MHz).In the case of four-wire LVDS with Ethernet support, the chipset already has a built-in function for multiplexing video streams, should there be a need for this use case. This chipset allows multiplex on video frame basis, and must be enabled by using the LVDS video interface on the chipset.Implementation: Interleaved links on two-wire LVDS. Optionally for four-wire LVDS, see below addition.Other format of interleaved video link package can be approved, if agreed between the OEM and both suppliers of the transceiver and the receiver side have agreed about the common interleaved link video packet format.For four-wire LVDS the selected transceiver and receiver can have HW supported video streams interleaving, in that case the preferred solution shall use the present multiple HW video stream implementation.However at any time, the transceiver/receiver manufacturer requirements for the packet format must be fulfilled.Qualification method: Documentation, Documentation of test results.

title: Toggle on Sync Bits
body: 1100 v3 Toggle on Sync Bits Version history:(3):Purpose: To avoid losing line- or frame-sync bits due to a bit error.Source:Verification Method: Test + AnalysisLegacy ID: 345424v2In case of a bit error the line- or frame- sync shall be delayed by only one pixel. Sync information shall generate a toggle on the line- and frame-bits.Implementation: Interleaved links on one-wire, two-wire and four-wire LVDS.Other format of interleaved video link package can be approved, if agreed between OEM and both suppliers of the transceiver and the receiver side have agreed about the line- or frame-sync bits.For four-wire LVDS the selected transceiver and receiver can have HW supported video streams interleaving, in that case the preferred solution shall use the multiple HW implementations of the line- or frame-sync bits.However at any time, the transceiver/receiver manufacturer requirements for the line- or frame-sync must be fulfilled.Qualification method:Analysis, documentation of test results.

title: Pixel Overhead Reduction
body: 1099 v3 Pixel Overhead Reduction Version history:(3):Purpose: To minimize overhead in the pixel data.Source: Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU Verification Method: Test + AnalysisLegacy ID: 345425v2All source information that does not need to be pixel synchronized may be sent through the control channel. The timing and the reduction of blanking may be compatible with the VESA-CVT-R standard for reduced blanking.Implementation: Non-interleaved links, one-wire, two-wire and four-wire LVDSQualification method: Analysis, documentation of test results.4.3.7.4.1.3 State management of control channel

title: State management of LVDS link(1wire)
body: 1095 v1 State management of LVDS link(1wire) Version history:(i):Purpose: The Serializer shall be responsible to set up the control channel.Source:Verification Method: Test + AnalysisLegacy ID: 433907v0The Serializer is responsible to set up the control channel, also after a loss of link.If communication over the control channel is lost, re-initialization will be handled by the serializer.The change of the selected method for utilize the control channel over the LVDS link shall be compliant to the below implementation.Implementation: Control channels over one-wire LVDS link.Other control channel implementations can be approved, if agree between the OEM and both suppliers of the transceiver and the receiver side have agreed about the control channel implementation.However at any time, the transceiver/receiver manufacturer requirements for the control channel implementation must be fulfilled. Document Name Base Tech SWRS DHU Serializer Deserializer I2C Master I2C Slave I2C Master I2C Slave Init Init Off Off Initialization (1wire) The Serializer is responsible to set up the control channel, also after a loss of link. If communication over the control channel is lost, re initialization will be handled by the serializer. See manufactory LVDS specification [LVDS_COAX:0] and [I2C_FPD-link_III:0]. I2C (1wire) The Serializer and Deserializer establish I2C communication over the link. This is managed by the Master of the communication (default serializer). See manufactory LVDS specification for details [LVDS_COAX:0] and [I2C_FPD-link_III:0]. This mode can be superseded if no Control channel is used Depending of the vehicle network architecture, it is possible to set the Deserializer to Master of the communication. This can be applicable for video sources without a CAN/LIN/Flexray connection. In this case, the Serializer sets itself to slave mode and handover the master functionality.

The Control channel State management shall follow the scheme below.Source:Verification Method: Test + AnalysisLegacy ID: 361990v0The Serializer is responsible to set up the control channel, also after a loss of link.If communication over the control channel is lost, re initialization will be handled by the serializer.The change of the selected method for utilize the control channel over the LVDS link shall be compliant to the below implementation.Implementation: Control channels over four-wire LVDS link.Other control channel implementations can be approved, if agreed between the OEM and both suppliers of the transceiver and the receiver side have agreed about the control channel implementation.However at any time, the transceiver/receiver manufacture requirements for the control channel implementation must be fulfilled.Qualification method: Analysis, documentation of test results. Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU Serializer Deserializer Ethernet Channel established Ctrl Channel established Video Link established Initialization (4wire ctrl)The Serializer is shall be responsible to set up the control channel, also after a loss of link.If communication over the control channel is lost, re initialization will be handled by the serializer.See APIX2 LVDS specification [LVDS_APIX2:2] SPI I2C boot (4wire ctrl)The Serializer and Deserializer establish local configuration via SPI/I2C, SPI communication can override deserializer configuration over the link. This is shall be managed by the Serializer.See APIX2 LVDS specification [LVDS_APIX2:2].This mode can be superseded if no Control channel is used. SPI Slave - I2C Master Mode (4wire ctrl)The Serializer and Deserializer establish SPI communication over the link and the deserializer shall be possible to be enabled as I2C host. This shall be managed by the Serializer.The Serializer sets the communication mode to SPI Slave - I2C Master. The communication speed shall be set through configuration of the Serializer. See APIX2 LVDS specification [LVDS_APIX2:2].This mode can be superseded if no Control channel or remote I2C master is used. SPI Master Slave Mode (4wire ctrl) Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU The Serializer sets the communication mode to SPI Master/Slave. The communication speed is set through configuration of the Serializer. See APIX2 LVDS specification [LVDS_APIX2:2]. This mode can be superseded if no Control channel or Ethernet Control channel is used.SPI Master Slave configuration (4wire ctrl)In SPI M/S mode the Serializer is by default the Master of the network. In SPI M/S mode an extension of the LIN protocol is used, see ref [LVDS_Generic:3] for communication protocol. Depending of the vehicle network architecture, it is possible to set the Deserializer to Master for the communication. This can be applicable for video sources without a CAN/LIN/Flexray connection. The Serializer set itself to slave mode and handover the master functionality. This mode can be superseded if no Control channel or Ethernet Control channel is used.Ethernet Master-Slave Configuration (4wire ctrl)The Serializer shall set the communication mode to Ethernet to enter this mode.The communication speed is set through the in band protocol. The default speed is 100 Mbps full duplex.Ethernet IP address management Host/slave is set up by application. See APIX2 LVDS specification [LVDS_APIX2:2]This mode can be superseded if no Control channel or SPI Master/Slave Control channels is used.In Ethernet mode the Serializer shall default be the Master of the network. In this mode the protocol depends on the application specific selection, see chapter Protocol, Ethernet in Vehicle Applicability.The minimum aggregated bandwidth shall exceed 200 Mbps. title: LVDS support of LIN Go to Sleep HANDLING
body: 1049 v1 LVDS support of LIN Go to Sleep HANDLING Version history:(1):Purpose:Source:Verification Method:Legacy ID: 391211v0The master sets the cluster into bus sleep mode by transmitting a go to sleep command.The request will not necessarily enforce the slave nodes into a low-power mode. The slave node application may still be active after the go to sleep command has been received. This behaviour is application specific.The go to sleep command is a master request frame with the first data field set to 0 and rest set to 0xFF, see Table 2.1. The slave nodes shall ignore the data fields 2 to 8 and interpret only the first data field. data1 data2 data3 data4 data5 data6 data7 data8 0 0xFF 0xFF 0xFF 0xFF 0xFF 0xFF 0xFF Table 2.1: Go to sleep commandThe normal way for setting the cluster to sleep is that the master node transmits the go to sleep command.4.3.7.4.1.4.1.2 Referred LIN Physical Layer Added or Modified Requirements

body: 1050 v1 Ability to disregard other headers and frames Version history:(1):Purpose:Source:Verification Method:Legacy ID: 391196v0The node shall respond to each header that is issued by the master, header that it is not programmed to handle and incorrect headers or frames on the bus, shall be acknowledge with an error response, to avoid blockage or starvation of the message buffers in the Master. body: 1055 v1 Communications protocol Version history:(1):Purpose: Define interface protocol which communicates between Master ECU and Slave ECU via LVDS.Source:Verification Method: Test Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU Legacy ID: 391215v0The Master ECU is normally the originator of the communication to Slave ECU by UART/I2C Protocol.Once handed over, the Slave ECU communicate by UART/I2C Protocol towards Master ECU.

title: Master and slave configuration
body: 1057 v1 Master and slave configuration Version history:(1):Purpose: Define master/slave setup on UART/I2C communication between Master ECU and Slave ECU via LVDS.Source:Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 391218v0Master ECU shall be Master and Slave ECU shall be Slave.Remark: The Serializer can both be the Master ECU or the Slave ECU.Remark: The Deserializer can both be the Master ECU or the Slave ECU.

title: Mode setting of transceiver device
body: 1058 v1 Mode setting of transceiver device Version history: Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU (1):Purpose:Define control mode in interface device(s).Source:Verification Method:Legacy ID:391214v0 Deserializer and Serializer are set with Base Mode of control mode in each device.

title: Node address of Slave ECU for SWDL
body: 1059 v1Node address of Slave ECU for SWDL Version history:(1):Purpose:Node device addresses of Slave ECU need to be converted to device address on LVDS by Master ECU.Source:Verification Method:TestLegacy ID:391217v0 When Slave ECU receives request message (Service, DID, RoutineID) for Diagnostic/SWDL between Tester and Master ECU, the Node Address used should be 0xCD.Master ECU converts Functional Address and Node Address to Device address on LVDS communication if needed – the Master shall route regardless of Node Address, as the Slave ECU is the only device that shall be connected to the Master ECU, per LVDS network.The Node Address is set to 0xABCD in VBF creation tool when VBF file is created for Slave ECU.

title: UART characteristics
body: 1060 v1UART characteristics Version history:(1):Purpose:Source:Verification Method:TestLegacy ID:391212v0 UART characteristics shall be according to LIN Specification Package Revision 2.1, LIN Physical Layer – Requisite documents, with nominal bus speeds of 9.6kbps or 19.2kbps.As a deviation from LIN standard above, the UART shall also support a high speed mode at 400 Kbps. 4.3.7.4.1.4.2 LIN Datalink Layer compatibility

title: Ability to read every frame instance
body: 1061 v1Ability to read every frame instance Version history:(1):Purpose:Source: Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU Verification Method:Legacy ID: 390936v0When the node is active on the bus it must not fail to read frames and to identify and respond to headers on the bus, regardless of any competing internal processes.

title: Application timing requirements
body: 1062 v1 Application timing requirements Version history:(1):Purpose:Source:Verification Method:Legacy ID: 390938v0The node application must be designed according to functional timing requirements, not according to the timing properties of a specific LIN bus implementation (i.e. a specific .ldf-file or similar).The high speed mode, at the full Bus speed, needs to be taken into account – virtual bus speed shall be retimed. In case of using virtual bus speeds on a specific LIN bus implementation (i.e. a specific .ldf-file or similar) the timing properties shall be recalculated to meet functional timing.

title: Bus speed
body: 1063 v1 Bus speed Version history:(1):Purpose:Source:Verification Method:Legacy ID: 390935v0All modules shall be capable of operating at the nominal bus speeds of 9.6kbps or 19.2kbps, forbackward compatibility. The operating speed shall be defined on a bus by bus basis. The bus speed shall be less than 416 kbps in high speed mode, but the virtual bus speed shall be possible to limit to 19.2kbps. The virtual bus speed shall be implemented by adding a delay, on the Master side, between two consecutive messages sent on the bus. The delay shall be calculated based upon last message length, in bits, using preset bus speed and the requested nominal bus speeds of 9.6kbps or 19.2kbps, in the way that the average actual bus speeds will become 9.6kbps or 19.2kbps (setting dependent).

title: Format of the part number data record
body: 1064 v1 Format of the part number data record Version history:(1):Purpose:Source:Verification Method: Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU Legacy ID: 390940v0When a part number for a LIN slave is to be transmitted from the slave to the master node, the format of the data shall be as follows:Part number data records used by VCC shall have 8 digits for part number + 3 characters (version suffix).Part number data records used by Geely shall have 10 digits for part number + 3 characters (version suffix).The part number digits shall be coded in BCD and the 3 characters (version suffix) shall be coded in ASCII, right justified, with any unused digit filled with 0H. In total 7 bytes (VCC) or in total 8 bytes (Geely).If version suffix contains one character, there shall be two space between part number and version suffix.If version suffix contains two characters, there shall be one space between part number and version suffix.Example:1234567<space><space>A -> (hex) 01 23 45 67 20 20 4112345678<space><space>A -> (hex) 12 34 56 78 20 20 411234567AB -> (hex) 01 23 45 67 20 41 4212345678<space>AB -> (hex) 12 34 56 78 20 41 421234567ABC -> (hex) 01 23 45 67 41 42 4312345678ABC -> (hex) 12 34 56 78 41 42 43

title: Format of the serial number
body: 1065 v1 Format of the serial numberVersion history:(1):Purpose:Source:Verification Method:Legacy ID: 390941v0When a serial number for a LIN slave is to be transmitted from the slave to the master node, the format of the data shall be as follows (see LIN Specification Package Revision 2.1, LIN Datalink Layer - Requisite documents):8 digits for serial number. All coded in BCD, right justified with any unused digit filled with 0H in total 4 bytes.Example:12345678 -> (hex) 12 34 56 78123456 -> (hex) 00 12 34 56

title: LIN signal frames may appear arbitrarily
body: 1066 v1 LIN signal frames may appear arbitrarilyVersion history:(1):Purpose:Source: Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU Verification Method:Legacy ID: 390939v0The node must not assume that headers in the range 0x00 to 0x3B appear in a specific relative order.

title: Wakeup strategy
body: 1067 v1 Wakeup strategy Version history:(1):Purpose:Source:Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 390937v0All nodes shall follow the strategy specified in LIN Specification Package Revision 2.1, LIN Datalink Layer – Requisite documents. title: Header jitter
body: 1068 v1 Header jitter Version history:(1):Purpose:Source:Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 390948v0The transmission of headers must follow the time schedule given by the schedule table. There will normally be a jitter in the transmission of headers [LVDS_GENERIC:3] LIN SpecificationPackage Revision 2.1, caused by internal processes inside the master ECU. The worst case Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU jitter and the THader_Maximum must be calculated by the supplier of the master ECU and reported to the OEM design team responsible for the ECU. The worst case jitter must not exceed 1 ms.

title: Local event - master sends the first header
body: 1069 v1 Local event - master sends the first header Version history:(1):Purpose:Source:Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 390944v0A master node shall transmit the first header within 100 ms after a local event.

title: Network event - wake up request to slave ready to communicate
body: 1070 v1 Network event - wake up request to slave ready to communicate Version history:(1):Purpose:Source:Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 390946v0The LIN slave node shall detect the wake up request and be able to transmit valid data within 100ms. Slaves shall not respond until their data is valid.Diagnostic supervision in the master shall take this delay into account. Specific subsystems that require a faster wakeup response time can be defined in the subsystem application requirements.

title: Power on - master sends the first header
body: 1071 v1 Power on - master sends the first header Version history:(1):Purpose:Source:Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 390945v0A master node shall be able to transmit the first header within 250 ms after power is applied or after a hardware reset. The LVDS link PLL shall be locked within 100 ms under conditions above, otherwise the master node shall be able to transmit the first header within 150 ms after LVDS link PLL is locked.

title: Power on - slave sends the first response
body: 1072 v1 Power on - slave sends the first response Version history:(1):Purpose:Source:Verification Method: Test Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU Legacy ID: 390947v0A slave node shall be able to transmit valid data within 100 ms after power is applied or after a hardware reset. Slaves shall not respond until their data is valid. The LVDS link PLL shall be locked within 100 ms under conditions above, otherwise the master node shall be able to able to transmit the first header within 150 ms after LVDS link PLL is locked. Diagnostic supervision in the master shall take this delay into account.

title: Timeout and sleep commands
body: 1073 v1 Timeout and sleep commands Version history:(1):Purpose:Source:Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 390943v0The master shall always issue a sleep command when power down of the bus is required, LIN Specification Package Revision 2.1, LIN Datalink Layer - Requisite documents.4.3.7.4.1.4.4 LIN Datalink Layer compatibility - SW Slave reqs

title: Timeout and sleep commands
body: 1074 v1 Timeout and sleep commands Version history:(1):Purpose:Source:Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 390950v0All slaves must implement both the timeout and sleep command, LIN Specification Package Revision 2.1, LIN Datalink Layer - Requisite documents.

title: Transmission time
body: 1075 v1 Transmission time Version history:(1):Purpose:Source:Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 390949v0The true T Response Maximum value, in which a node can complete its response, shall be stated in the free text section of the Node Capability File. In the event a value is not provided, the communication schedule (defined in the .ldf-file or equivalent) shall presume a value of T Response Maximum as defined in LIN Specification Package Revision 2.1, LIN Datalink Layer - Requisite documents. The high speed mode, at the full Bus speed, needs to be taken into account – virtual bus speed shall be retimed. In case of using virtual bus speeds on a specific Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU LIN bus implementation (i.e. a specific .ldf-file or similar) the timing properties shall be recalculated to meet functional timing.4.3.7.4.1.4.5 LIN Physical Layer compatibility

title: Remote Register access LVDS Slave ECU LVDS command
body: 1087 v1 Remote Register access LVDS Slave ECU LVDS commandVersion history:(1):Purpose: Define message format on UART/I2C communication to Slave ECU LVDS Registers.Source:Verification Method: Test + AnalysisLegacy ID: 391221v0Slave ECU LVDS Chipset registers shall access via Master ECU via the control channel over LVDS link.Access from Master ECU to remote Slave ECU register addresses shall only handle by Master ECU as local error management.Gateway accesses to Remote Slave ECU registers write access shall handle CRC error management, offloading the CRC from the message before perform the remote Slave ECU LVDS register access.For Gateway accesses to Remote Slave ECU LVDS registers read access, the Master ECU shall calculate CRC and add the CRC field to the message before responding to remote Slave Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU register access. Signal definitions:SYNC: 1 byte and fixed value as 0x79.DEV ADDR: 1 byte and the value specified in Device address requirement.REG ADDR: 1 byte and the value specified in Message list requirement.NUMBER OF BYTES: 1 byte and the value is data length of all BYTE.BYTE(): Valid parameter data DEV ADDR addresses Ref [LVDS_GMSL:2] Device Serializer Read Serializer Write Deserializer Read Deserializer Write Maxim9259(Serializer) - - 0x91 (remote config address) 0x90 (remote config address) Maxim9260(Deserializer) 0x81 (remote config address) 0x80 (remote config address) - - There are two types of signals:Type1Data sent from Master (Master ECU) to Slave ECU LVDS chipset registersType2Data sent from Slave ECU LVDS chipset registers to Master (Master ECU) Message type1SYNCDEV ADDR + W0x790x6CNUMBER OF BYTESN Message type2SYNCDEV ADDR + W0x790x6CNUMBER OF BYTESN Qualification method: Analysis, documentation of test results.

title: By-Pass Latency
body: 1043 v3 By-Pass Latency Version history:(3):Purpose: To fullfil early-HMI requirements and park-assistance performance.Source:Verification Method: DemonstrationLegacy ID: 345430v2The gateway shall allow a live video image on the sinks display after maximum three (3) video frames latency. (100 ms at 30 fps).Implementation: Two_wire and Fourwire LVDS link.Qualification method: Demonstration, documentation of test results.

title: By-Pass Mode
body: 1044 v2 By-Pass Mode Version history:(2):Purpose: To be able to show a PAC image on the CSD before the IHU has been fully booted.Source:Verification Method: AnalysisLegacy ID: 345426v1Traffic through the gateway shall be able to transfer video direct after startup, according to startup requirements.If not possible to fulfill normal video within six (6) video frames latency, a By-Pass mode shall be provided, until the ECU is completely booted. The by-pass mode shall be able to produce a video stream that follows the VESA video timing definition of all the supported sinks. The Control channel, via Ethernet or SPI/I2C/UART are not mandatory in bypass mode.Implementation: Two wire and Four wire LVDS link.Qualification method: Analysis (Documentation).

title: By-Pass Start Up Time
body: 1045 v3 By-Pass Start Up Time Version history:(3):Purpose: To be able to show a video image on the sink before the gateway has been fully booted.Source:Verification Method: Test + AnalysisLegacy ID: 345429v2If an By-Pass mode is needed at the gateway, the video traffic shall be up and running within six (6) video frames latency. (200 ms at 30 fps). Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU Implementation: Two wire and Fourwire LVDS link.Qualification method: Analysis, Documentation of test results.

title: Pixel Queue
body: 1046 v3Pixel Queue Version history:(3):Purpose: To be able to mix and multiplex-demultiplex with minimum delay of image data.Source:Verification Method: Test + AnalysisLegacy ID: 345432v2 If a link has more than one source, then the pixels of each source shall be placed in a queue.Implementation: One-wire, Two-wire LVDS, four-wire LVDSOther format of Pixel queue for interleaved video link package can be approved, if agreed between the OEM and both suppliers of the transceiver and the receiver side have agreed about interleaved video link package.For four-wire LVDS the selected transceiver and receiver can have HW supported video streams interleaving, in that case the preferred solution shall use the multiple HW implementations of the line- or frame-sync bits.However at any time, the transceiver/ receiver manufacture requirements for the line- or frame-sync must be fulfilled.Qualification method: Analysis, documentation of test results.

title: Pixel Queue Delay
body: 1047 v4Pixel Queue Delay Version history:(4):Purpose: Minimize memory depth of receiving FIFO.Source:Verification Method: Test + AnalysisLegacy ID: 345433v3 If a link has more than one source, then the pixels of each source shall be placed in a queue.Implementation: One-wire, Two-wire LVDS, four-wire LVDSOther format of Pixel queue for interleaved video link package can be approved, if agreed between the OEM and both suppliers of the transceiver and the receiver side have agreed about interleaved video link package.For four-wire LVDS the selected transceiver and receiver can achieve HW supported video streams interleaving, in that case the preferred solution shall use the multiple HW implementations of the line- or frame-sync bits.However at any time, the transceiver/ receiver manufacture requirements for the line- or frame-sync must be fulfilled.Qualification method: Analysis, documentation of test results. title: Bidirectional Control Channel on four-wire LVDS with Ethernet
body: 1025 v2 Bidirectional Control Channel on four-wire LVDS with Ethernet Version history:(2):Purpose: To define a bidirectional control channel in order to control the high-speed LVDS video link as well as to exchange various types of data between the nodes.Source: DPR-LVDS-NETWORK-005:Req5v1Verification Method: DemonstrationLegacy ID: 345397v1The control channel shall support bidirectional transfer of data. The type and speed of transfer shall be software configurable, and can be either I2C (400 kbps) or SPI (400 kbps - 1 Mbps). The SPI mode for external access on the remote side shall only be active if the Ethernet MII mode is disabled. On the local side the SPI interface shall be used for accessing the local and remote registers, as well as the external I2C host controller. The types of data to be exchanged shall include event-driven application data, diagnostics data, validation of link quality, remote-side configuration data and software download. It shall be possible to initiate transfer of data as well as to be initiated remotely by the remote side.The control channel shall be functional independently of the state of the high-speed forward video channel.Implementation: Four-wire LVDS with EthernetQualification method: Demonstration.Note: Details of the implementation of the bidirectional control channel are decided through agreement between the OEM and the supplier.

body: 1026 v1 Bidirectional Control Channel on one-wire LVDS Version history:(1):Purpose: To define a bidirectional control channel in order to control the high-speed LVDS video link as well as to exchange various types of data between the nodes.Source: DPR-LVDS-NETWORK-005:Req4v1, [LVDS_Netw:6]Verification Method: DemonstrationLegacy ID: 433930v0The control channel shall support bidirectional transfer of data. The type and speed of transfer shall be I2C High speed mode (400 kbps). The types of data to be exchanged shall include event-driven application data, diagnostics data validation of link quality, remote-side configuration data and software download. It shall be possible to initiate transfer of data as well Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU as to be initiated remotely by the remote side.The control channel shall be functional independently of the state of the high-speed video channel.

title: Bidirectional Control Channel on two-wire LVDS
body: 1027 v3 Bidirectional Control Channel on two-wire LVDS Version history:(3):Purpose: To define a bidirectional control channel in order to control the high-speed LVDS video link as well as to exchange various types of data between the nodes.Source: DPR-LVDS-NETWORK-005:Req4v1, [LVDS_Netw:6]Verification Method: DemonstrationLegacy ID: 345396v2The control channel shall support bidirectional transfer of data. The type and speed of transfer shall be software configurable, and can be either I2C (400 kbps) or UART (400 kbps - 1 Mbps). The types of data to be exchanged shall include event-driven application data, diagnostics data validation of link quality, remote-side configuration data and software download. It shall be possible to initiate transfer of data as well as to be initiated remotely by the remote side.The control channel shall be functional independently of the state of the high-speed forward channel.Implementation: Two-Wire LVDSQualification method: Demonstration.Note: Details of the implementation of the bidirectional control channel are decided through agreement between the OEM and the supplier.

title: Bidirectional High-Speed Control Channel on four-wire LVDS with Ethernet
body: 1028 v2 Bidirectional High-Speed Control Channel on four-wire LVDS with Ethernet Version history:(2):Purpose: To define a high-speed bidirectional control channel in order to control the high-speed LVDS video link as well as to exchange various types of data between the nodes.Source: DPR-LVDS-NETWORK-005Req6v1Verification Method: DemonstrationLegacy ID: 345416v1The high-speed control channel shall support bidirectional transfer of data. The type and speed of transfer shall be software configurable. The Ethernet MII mode will need to disable the external SPI interface on the remote side, but the I2C master shall still be allowed to use. With the high-speed MII there is no access to the local and remote registers, neither to the external I2C via the I2C host controller; for this function the SPI interface must be supported as well, in addition to the Ethernet MII interface. Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU The types of data to be exchanged shall depend on the overlaying protocol only,the chipset shall act as MII-connected PHYs on both sides of the link.If the chipset does not support auto negotiation, then a fixed mode of 100 Mbps, full-duplex,shall be used.The control channel shall be functional independently of the state of the high-speed forwardvideo channel, but the correct mode must be set to enable the needed Ethernet bandwidth.Implementation: Four-wire LVDS with EthernetQualification method: Demonstration.Note: Details of the implementation of the high-speed bidirectional control channel are decidedthrough agreement between the OEM and the supplier.HDCP is used for secured transmissions over LVDS and is initiated by the Serializer. TheHDCP functionality is available in DCP enabled variants of LVDS chipset.

title: Bit error rate
body: 1029 v3 Bit error rate Version history:(3):Purpose: To establish premium video quality including robustness of video link.Source: DPR-LVDS-NETWORK-005:Req1v1, [LVDS_GMSL:2, [LVDS_APIX2:2]Verification Method: Test + AnalysisLegacy ID: 345393v2 Allowed bit error rate is 10 -10/s. It is allowed to measure the bit error rate over 24 or 32 selectedbits for each pixel.The selection of 32 bits shall be used if 32 bits (40 bits 8b10b encoded) link format is used.Implementation: AllQualification method: Analsis, documentation of test results: Reading of measurements, see[ LVDS_GMSL:2 ] and [ LVDS_APIX2:2 ]

title: Deserializer Robustness against Bit Errors Four-Wire LVDS with Ethernet
body: 1030 v2 Deserializer Robustness against Bit Errors Four-Wire LVDS with Ethernet Version history:(2):Purpose: To establish robustness of the deserializer against a burst of bit errors andthus premium video quality.Source: DPR-LVDS-NETWORK-005:Req3v1Verification Method: Test + AnalysisLegacy ID: 345395v1 The deserializer shall be able to handle a length of a burst due to bit errors of up to three pixelswithin each video source. The burst must not cause any column displacements of the pixelscomprising a line; it must not corrupt the video timing generator on the receiving side; it mustnot cause an interchange of source-destination order in the case of dual video streams. Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU Implementation: Deserializer side, four-wire LVDS with EthernetQualification method: Analysis, documentation of test results.

title: Battery voltage above normal operating range
body: 1032 v1 Battery voltage above normal operating range Version history:(1):Purpose: To guarantee deterministic behavior of the LVDS Link, it is desired that: above normal operating range, the Serializer shall determine the state of the link, i.e. by forcing inactive mode.Source:Verification Method: Test + AnalysisLegacy ID: 362119v0The LVDS network shall only be fully functional over an operating range of 8 to 16 volts, above normal range the ECU shall detect and can possible disrupt the transmission. The same disruption shall be during partial or complete ECU startup, shutdown, reset, brownout or comparable events.To guarantee deterministic behavior of the LVDS Link, it is desired that above normal operating range, the Serializer shall determine the state of the link, i.e. by forcing the bus to go to inactive mode, in which communicating shall be disrupted. Note: Bolded part is relevant to the SW-requirement.Implementation: AllQualification method: Analysis, documentation of test results.

title: Communication voltage range
body: 1033 v1 Communication voltage range Version history:(1):Purpose: To require the ECU to not disturb the LVDS link, neither video nor control channel, shall operate outside the operating voltage range.Source:Verification Method: Test + AnalysisLegacy ID: 362117v0The LVDS network shall be fully functional over an operating range of 8 to 16 volts. ECUs shall not interfere with the LVDS link, or disrupt the transmission of the other ECU outside of its specified voltage operating range, during partial or complete ECU startup, shutdown, reset, brownout or comparable events.The LVDS communication links shall continue to communicate outside the voltage operating range as long as they have a correct behavior but shall be disabled in case the operating voltage is out-of-range and correct communication cannot be provided.Implementation: AllQualification method: Analysis, documentation of test results.

title: ECU Power Loss
body: 1034 v1 ECU Power Loss Version history:(1): Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU Purpose: LVDS link ECUs shall not interfere with normal communication during a loss of power (or low voltage) condition.Source:Verification Method: Test + AnalysisLegacy ID: 362120v0LVDS link ECUs shall not interfere with normal communication during a loss of power (or low voltage) condition. Upon return of power, normal operation shall resume without any operator intervention within a time determined by the vehicle manufacturer.Implementation: AllQualification method: Analysis, documentation of test results.

title: ECU Internal Data Propagation Delay (1wire)
body: 1037 v1 ECU Internal Data Propagation Delay (1wire) Version history:(1):Purpose: To require the ECU to not add unnecessary internal propagation delay.Source:Verification Method: Test + AnalysisLegacy ID: 433929v0The internal propagation delay, measured between controller input/output and ECU connector, shall not exceed measures below:For I 2C control channel modes, the latency shall be less than 250 us.Implementation: AllQualification method: Analysis, documentation of test results.

title: ECU Internal Data Propagation Delay (2wire)
body: 1038 v1 ECU Internal Data Propagation Delay (2wire) Version history:(1):Purpose: To require the ECU to not add unnecessary internal propagation delay. For data traffic the gateway delay shall be measured by the serialization time of 10 bytesSource:Verification Method: Test + AnalysisLegacy ID: 362124v0The internal propagation delay, measured between controller input/output and ECU connector, shall not exceed measures below:For SPI/I2C and UART control channel modes, the latency shall be less than the serialization time for 10 bytes messages.Implementation: AllQualification method: Analysis, documentation of test results.

title: ECU Internal Data Propagation Delay (4wire)
body: 1039 v1 ECU Internal Data Propagation Delay (4wire) Version history:(1):Purpose: To require the ECU to not add unnecessary internal propagation delay. For data traffic the gateway delay shall be measured by the serialization time of 10 bytes, for fast ethernet maximum of the serialization time of 256 bytesSource:Verification Method: Test + AnalysisLegacy ID: 362125v0 Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU The internal propagation delay, measured between controller input/output and ECU connector, shall not exceed measures below:For full duplex 100Mbps Ethernet data traffic the gateway latency shall be less than 25 microseconds.(100Mbps Ethernet and max 1000 bytes/packets)To enable full duplex 100Mbps Ethernet two way traffic response, when ECU act as ethernet repeater, the Round-Trip Propagation Delay shall be less than 140 (in Bit Times). If ECU act as a transparent cable, the Round-Trip delay shall be less that 11.1 (Bit Times), 1/10th of maximum cable segment length (111.2 (Bit Times) = 100 Meters cable), and shall allow upto 5 units and 50 meters of cable in series in the Ethernet network.For SPI/I2C and UART control channel modes, the latency shall be less than the serialization time for 10 bytes messages.Implementation: AllQualification method: Analysis, documentation of test results.

title: ECU Internal Video Propagation Delay
body: 1040 v2 ECU Internal Video Propagation Delay Version history:(2):Purpose: To require the ECU to not add unnecessary internal propagation delay. For video traffic delay is measured in frame delays.Source: DPR-LVDS-NETWORK-005:Req9v1Verification Method: Test + AnalysisLegacy ID: 345419v1The internal propagation delay, measured between controller input/output and ECU connector, shall not exceed measures below:If LVDS links transfer video traffic, maximum three (3) video frames (corresponding to 100 ms at 30 fps) are allowed, when rescale, rotate, resample, coding/decoding of video frame are performed otherwise maximum two video frames.Implementation: AllQualification method: Analysis, documentation of test results.

title: LVDS Single Chipset
body: 1041 v1 LVDS Single Chipset Version history:(1):Purpose: To secure compatibility of LVDS communication, both Serilizer and Deserializer must belong to compatible chipset family.Source: REQPROD 344966, REQPROD 344559Verification Method: AnalysisLegacy ID: 362122v0All LVDS serializers and deserializers in the LVDS network shall belong to the same chipset family of compatible chips. If compatible chipset is used, Tier1 must make sure that all SW Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU access to physical level functionality, as well as the SW accessibility of the companion side is supported.If low level SW compatibility cannot be assured, appropriate SW API/Drivers shall be supplied by Teir1.For 4-wire only:If the high speed control channel additionally supports 100 Mbps full-duplex Ethernet interface over LVDS link, SW level requirement is to apply the corresponding level of Ethernet SW layers support that is used over the link.Qualification method: Analysis (documentation).
