This is applicable for legacy ECUs not supporting CheckMemory.The Software Authentication concept includes a list of specifications that has a tight relation to each other, the "Figure - Software Authentication specification component structure", shows the overview and their relation. ![](images/4a671cf9ebf6d13d59a3cea8dd2b207aea75165ea8fd70f06cd702da6c1e9c4f.jpg) GEELYGeely Automotive Research Institute(Ningbo)Co.Ltd Document TypeNote-SWRS Document Release StatusRELEASED Document No Revision005 Volume No01 Page No748(1572) Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU CheckMemory), where the complete set of software parts are signed and the single signature is transferred (downloaded) to the ECU in a dedicated software part. Added here for reference only.3 and 4 - The "Software Download and Upload sequences" and "General Bootloader requirements" includes the default software authentication method requirements for the client and server respectively, where each software part is independently signed and the signature is transferred in a CheckMemory routine control. Introduced together with the data file format version VBF 2.6. Note: There is a dedicated " General Bootloader requirements" version for ECUs not supporting CheckMemory.5 - The "Software Authentication for file based systems", defines the requirements when code signing certificates are used in the ECU.6 - The "VBF (Versatile Binary Format)" data file format. VBF 2.6 is required when signing methods using CheckMemory are applied.4.4.4.1.6 IntroductionThe purpose of Software Authentication is to provide the following security services in order to protect the software in the vehicle:Authentication (proof of origin): the recipient ECU of the downloaded software shall be confident that the software originates from a legitimate source.Integrity: the recipient ECU shall be able to verify that the original software has not been altered (e.g. manipulated by an unauthorized user) in transit.Copy Protection: it is used to prevent unauthorized feature activation, by e.g. copying a software from one ECU to another. This is not the same as encryption, for confidentiality. Copy protection is realized by key management.The two first terms, Authentication (proof of origin) and Integrity, are commonly referred to as Authenticity. It is accomplished by the use of public-key algorithms (asymmetric algorithms), where the key (private key) used to encrypt the software is separated from the key used to decrypt it (public key). The private ( secret) key is exclusively known to the originator of the software, thus this key is used for signing (generating a digital signature). The recipient(s) having access to the public key is able to verify the downloadable parts. The software together with the signature shall be sent to the recipient ECU. Standard code signing technology relies on asymmetric cryptography in the form of public key infrastructure (PKI) and provides a well proven quality history.To summarize: Software Authentication concept is applied to ensure that the software being executed in the vehicle is authentic by:Secure download/flushing (prevent "malware" software by verifying the downloaded software part). Focus of this specification.Secure boot (prevent from booting modified and unauthorized software)It does however NOT cover e.g. a secure delivery process of complete file from software supplier to the OEM but describes how to sign the data blocks of a software part once those criteria(s) for signing it are fulfilled. Hence, conditions to ensure that a software part is valid and trusted prior to it is stored in software archives, distributed to e.g. cloud etc. or for performing the actual signing of the data blocks are to be specified elsewhere. Figure - General Signing model1. The software is developed and released.2. The software is sent to the trust centre for signing.3. The software is signed using a private key and by that a signature (signed software) is generated by the trust centre.4. The software including signature is stored and transferred (software download) to the ECU.5. The software stored in the ECU is being verified by using the public key. In order to perform SWDL, authentication of the tester tool is required using Security Access.In a vehicle the ECU capabilities differs, i.e. some are "high-performance" ECUs but some are having less capabilities. Based on that, the Software Authentication concept has currently only support for a simplified key structure for signing/verifying a software part:One layer of keys ("raw private/public key pairs") is applied, where only the raw public key data with minimum metadata is used for verification, i.e. no key chain verification as for a more standardized certificate verification of multiple levels (root, policy and issuer authorities). Still, certificates could be used for key management purposes (storage, distribution) and when signing. GEELYGeely Automotive Research Institute(Ningbo)Co.Ltd Document TypeNote-SWRS Document Release StatusRELEASED Document No Revision005 Volume No01 Page No750(1572) Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU Software , Figure - One-Layer key structureThe figure below gives a brief overview of concerned systems for the Software Authentication concept. Document Name Base Tech SWRS DHU Off-Board Systems ECU Software Supplier Develop software parts s19, .hex ECU Config Vehicle Software Configuration Software approval and release Check documentation (tests, change orders, etc.) Verify software part OK? Release. Trust Centre Software Signing Protected key storage Sign software using dedicated private key Distribute public key Workshop Systems Software storage and Software Download Store software part in sw repository Store Public Key SWDL (and signature transfer) Manufacturing Systems Local Software storage and Software Download Store Public Key SWDL (and signature transfer) On-Board Systems On-Board Systems Vehicle ECU Software validation and execution Verify software stored at target memory Only start application upon successful verification PublicKey SW Part (.vbf) Figure - Software Authentication concerned systems Figure - Software Authentication concerned systems is a simplified view, where details are omitted (e.g. temporarily software repositories at manufacturing). But, the figures does however illustrate that there are several systems involved which will result in the fact that several interfaces must be defined. A typical software signing function is described in Figure - Software signing function overview. The data that is signed together with the methods (hash function and signing algorithm) must be known to both the signer (Trust Centre) and verifier (ECU). A hash value (digest) is calculated on the data and that hash is being encrypted with the signer's private (secret) key. This encrypted hash is called a signature. The software part together with the signature forms the signed data that is transferred to the ECU. Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU Figure - Software signing function overviewThe secret private key is kept protected by the trust centre and must not be exposed, i.e. the data to be signed is an input to the signing function where the private key is stored as shown in Figure - Trust Centre signing. Figure - Trust Centre signingThe software authentication concept must support different signing methods, e.g. for future Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU growth (change of key lengths, algorithms, etc.) but also for legacy reasons. This variability must be handled in a controlled manner at theoff-boardsystems and because of that the term Signing Methodis introduced. See chapterSigning Methodsfor further details.4.4.5 Hardware Security Module4.4.5.1 Hardware security module4.4.5.1.1 IntroductionThis is a software requirement specification for the usage of hardware security modules. The intent of the hardware security module is to provide tamper resistance and enable cryptographic operations:1. Control access to key usage2. Secure storage (keys)3. Generate true random numbers4. Accelerate cryptographic operationsThe purpose of a hardware security module is to increase the security level by adding logical and physical tamper protection to key material or other sensitive information. The scope of this document does not include performance requirement since that is part of the specific implementation.Depending on the required level of protection for each implementation the following parameters need to be decided:Security functional requirements (security mechanisms)Security assurance requirements (quality assurance formalism)These are typically expressed by reference to established certification schemes like FIPS security levels or Common Criteria protection profiles or an industry de-facto standard like HIS/SHE.4.4.5.1.2 Requirements

title: Privacy Regulations
body: 6436 v1 Privacy Regulations Version history:(1):Purpose: Privacy Regulations shall be followedSource:Verification Method: DocumentationLegacy ID:All systems storing any personal data shall adhere to privacy regulations or policies applicable (e.g. GDPR, China laws or NHTSA) on the targeted markets.

title: Privacy as Default
body: 6437 v2 Privacy as Default Version history:(2):Purpose: Prevent personal data to be exposedSource:Verification Method: InspectionLegacy ID:The main guidelines when developing systems are “privacy as default” and “privacy by design” to prevent data exfiltration and ensure the privacy and integrity of sensitive information.Whenever it is possible, personal data shall be anonymized or de-identified and encrypted.It shall not be possible to access other person’s personal data and it shall be possible to erase all personal data on request to eliminate any footprints e.g. when a car is sold or shared.Any administrator access to personal data shall be restricted to a minimum and actions logged.

title: Purpose and Consent
body: 6438 v2 Purpose and Consent Version history:(2):Purpose: Only necessary data collected, consent given and right to be forgottenSource:Verification Method: DocumentationLegacy ID:A basic principle is that only necessary personal data shall be stored and the purpose for collecting the data must be clearly expressed.The contractor shall be able to present a list of what data is collected and the purpose must be Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU clearly expressed.Consent for data collection as well as the possibility to erase personal data from the system is mandatory and shall be considered in the system design.4.4.7 Cyber Security4.4.7.1 Cyber Security Requirements for Security Level 1 ECUs4.4.7.1.1 Cyber Security Related Information SharingEffective defense against cyberattacks requires a high level of collaboration among multiple suppliers, information sharing is essential for many reasons. It can help to:1) Build trust between stakeholders (OEM, component manufacturers, aftermarket operators, etc.)2) Collaborate and contribute to making industry-wide standards;3) Improve integration through commonly accepted practices;4) Collaborate with industry actors to find countermeasures and challenge the relevance of their security mechanisms;5) Provide a mechanism to challenge and develop security teams' skills;6) Support the detection and mediation of security issues.Therefore, vehicle manufacturers are committed to engaging with public authorities as well as other stakeholders, from every sector of the industry. Equally, they are ready to engage with third parties to share and discuss new cybersecurity threats in order to help the whole community to find countermeasures.4.4.7.1.2 Privacy 116138 v1User Data Protection Version history:(1):Purpose:Source:Verification Method:Legacy ID: Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU The integrity, confidentiality and authenticity of the user's data must be ensured.Confidentiality protection requirements must be defined with regards to privacy issues.Techniques to anonymize and pseudo-anonymized personal data are adopted when necessary.Applicable data privacy rules will depend on the laws and standards to which Geely Automotive group is subject. 116139 v1 Privacy as default Version history:(1):Purpose:Source:Verification Method:Legacy ID:Privacy is a growing concern and with the introduction of new regulations (such as EU GDPR and China's new privacy law 2018), it is vital to make sure that privacy is part of the design.The protection of personal data is of great concern for GRI, and applicable for any system/component using or storing personal information. "Personal data" means any information relating to an identifiable natural person. Which can be directly or indirectly used to identified a person, information such as name, identification number, location data or factors specific to the physical, physiological, genetic, mental, economic, cultural or social identity of that person.The main guidelines when developing systems are “privacy as default” and “privacy by design” to prevent data exfiltration and ensure the privacy and integrity of sensitive information. When it is possible, data shall be anonymized or de-identified and when applicable encrypted. 116140 v1 Purpose and consent Version history:(1):Purpose:Source:Verification Method:Legacy ID:Another basic principle is that only necessary personal data shall be stored. The contractor shall be able to present a list of what data is collected and the purpose must be clearly expressed. Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU Consent for data collection as well as the possibility to erase personal data from the system shall be considered in the system design.4.4.7.1.3 Security Testing 20884 v3 Continuous Security Testing Version history:(3):Purpose:Source:Verification Method: DocumentationLegacy ID:An appropriate test methodology according to industry best practices shall be used and described. The test methodology must be suitable for the target.Security testing of new or modified software that introduce a security risk shall be done continuously during the development and life cycle.Static code analysis tools as part of the Software Development Life-cycleCode review (manual/automatic)Code review is a systematic examination of program source code. It is intended to find mistakes overlooked in software development, improving the overall quality of software. Reviews are done in various forms, such as pair programming, informal walk throughs and formal inspections.Static code analysis is the process of detecting errors and defects in software source code. And static code analysis is done without executing any of the code, while dynamic code analysis relies on studying how the code behaves during execution.4.4.7.1.4 Reviews

title: Handling Anomalies
body: 6453 v4 Handling Anomalies Version history:(4):Purpose: Handling of anomaliesSource:Verification Method: DocumentationLegacy ID:System anomalies, such as misuse, unexpected system events or buffer overflow, that can endanger system security shall be logged, detected and acted upon to prevent any information loss or system breach.The system shall be designed with a proper error handling to be able to withstand unexpected events or inputs. Input validation shall be performed to reject any malformed or out of band input to avoid unexpected behavior or execution that can endanger system security.The input validation shall cover all code injection attacks.In the case there is a local ECU event log, all unexpected events shall be recorded.

title: Incident and Patch Management
body: 6464 v3 Incident and Patch Management Version history:(3):Purpose: Manage life cycle of productSource:Verification Method: DocumentationLegacy ID:During the entire ECU life cycle, any discovered security risks or incidents shall be promptly reported to Geely/CEVT. The supplier is responsible to continuously and actively find and analyze any cyber security vulnerabilities or risks affecting the integrity of the delivered system.Any highly critical patch shall be in place within one week after being discovered or published.A security patch process and strategy shall be presented by the supplier.

title: Password Protection
body: 6522 v4 Password Protection Version history: Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU (4):Purpose: Protect any passwords storedSource:Verification Method: InspectionLegacy ID:Any passwords stored in the ECU must be safeguarded in accordance with security best-practices so they cannot be retrieved or guessed.If available, the preferred way is to protect passwords in a protected environment such as a HTA. If HTA is not available then any saved password data must be one way encrypted according to SHA-2 (SHA 512). The password hash must also be protected by salt. Salt is additional randomized seed data appended or prepended to a one-way hash function input utilized to prevent dictionary/rainbow attacks.Passwords must be at least twelve (12) characters in length. Highly sensitive passwords shall have a minimum length of twenty (20) characters.A password should include both lower-case and capital letters as well as one digit and special characters such as ! " # $ % & ' () * + , - . / : ; <= > ? @ [ \ ] ^ { | } ~All default passwords for services, users or software must immediately be changed. Mechanisms to prevent brute force password guessing shall be implemented. 90439 v2 Minimize Attack Surfaces Version history:(2):Purpose: Remove unused functionalitySource:Verification Method:Legacy ID:To reduce possible attack vectors, the number of exposed services and interfaces shall be kept to a minimum and any unused functionalities and ports shall be turned off.Operating systems, application functionality, user accounts and communication protocols used shall be limited to only provide the features needed to meet specified business needs, removing unused functionality. For example:1. Don't give more access to users/services that they absolutely need. Just enough to accomplish their tasks (following the principle of least privilege) Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU 2. Storage of confidential and or Personal Identifiable data must be kept to a minimum and data must be deleted when not needed.3. Turn off (remove or disable) functionality that is not required or being used.4. Remove features that are not being used.5. Remove previous versions of software and unused code.Reduce entry points into the ECU by eliminating unnecessary service requests.

title: System Hardening
body: 6448 v4 System Hardening Version history:(4):Purpose: Ensure a secure configurationSource:Verification Method: InspectionLegacy ID:Operating systems, application functionality, user accounts and communication protocols used shall be hardened to only allow the features or access rights needed for the demanded functionality.Hardening shall also consider an attacker that may already has gained access to a system and make it more difficult to get any further access to the compromised system and thereby provide a second line of defense.Hardening process shall include:Configuration of access rights and configuration files of operation systems and applications shall be reviewed and if necessary modified to ensure they support a secure system and application setup. Default installations often comes with embedded weaknesses and special attention shall be given to any default configuration files and access rights that may provide excessive access to system assets.When applicable, common industry recommendations for hardening (e.g. NIST SCAP, SANS SCORE or NSA guidelines) shall be followed.The chosen hardening method shall be documented and communicated.
