Timing Parameter SWDL DIAG Max Value Max Value GW_CAN_IP_L1 See [*] and Formula(1) See [*] and Formula(1) GW_CAN_IP_L2 5 ms 5 ms Formula(1):unsegmented messages: C_Assegmented messages: C_As + C_Bs + ((Message size) – (L-SDU size))/(L-SDU size) * C_CrTable: Vehicle GW: FlexRay to IP response timing parameters*: [VCC - DoCAN] 118334 v1 Latency CAN to IP, GW_CAN-IP_L2Version history: Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU (1):Purpose: Clarify and define a maximum latency time.Source:Verification Method: TestLegacy ID:Req:If a communication channel can be allocated, time between receiving complete response from CAN network until DoIP response shall be triggered shall be max 5ms.4.5.1.8.2 Gateway allocation of communication channelsThis section describes the allocation of communication channels for physical request and responses.Note: Functional requests, including TesterPresent, should not be delayed in the gateway due to e.g. queued or parallel requests in the gateway. Functional requests need to have separate communication channel, so that TesterPresent can be sent though the gateways and keep ECUs in non-default session.4.5.1.8.2.1 Sub Network (CAN) - Client sideThis section will describe and give grounds for the following requirements:REQPROD 118147 Transmit(Tx) CCs on Sub NetworkREQPROD 118151 Receive(Rx) CCs on Sub NetworkThe in-vehicle gateway should not do any re-sending of messages, e.g. if time-out due to no flow control frames is received.It should always be guaranteed when allocating a transmit (Tx) communication channel (CC) on the sender side, the receiver side should be able to allocate a receive (Rx) communication channel (CC), so that no data (first frame) will be lost.There is no handshake mechanism when allocating a Tx CC on the sender side with the allocation of an Rx CC on the receiver side, hence it must always be assured that a Rx CC can be allocated to receive at least the first frame so that no data will be lost.Allocation of transmit (Tx) communication channels (CCs)Vehicle GW for requests to Sub Network (CAN):The Vehicle Network GW should have three(3) communication channels (CCs) for sending physical request to the ECUs on each Sub Network. Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU Allocation of receive (Rx) communication channels (CCs)Vehicle GW for responses from Sub Network (CAN):The Vehicle Network GW should have same number of receive (Rx) communication channels (CCs) as transmit (Tx) communication channels (CCs) on the Sub Network (Note: The number of Rx CCs are project specific, e.g. same number as ECUs connected on the Sub Network).The Vehicle GW must be able to receive and handle first frame from all ECUs.If there is no buffer in the buffer pool available for receiving the complete response on the CC, the Vehicle GW should send flow control WAIT until a buffer that fits the response is available. When a buffer is available, the Vehicle GW should send a flow control CTS for receiving the remaining part of the response.Note: When dimension the system with number of supported communication channels and number of messages that can be allocated from the buffer pool, it must be assured that flow control WAIT frames can be sent long enough time so that the sending side does not time-out.See Figure: "Allocation communication channels (CCs) for physical request on Sub Network (CAN) - Client side". title: Parallel requests on LIN
body: 6284 v3Parallel requests on LIN Version history:(3):Purpose:The tester shall not need to consider limitations on LIN.Source:Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 82084v3The LIN master shall be able to handle parallel physical addressed diagnostic requests to a LIN network.On one LIN network there shall only be one ongoing physical address diagnostic request, the LIN master needs to wait until response is received or time out before next request is sent on the LIN network.Rationale:The LIN master shall serialize incoming parallel request to one LIN network. Next request(s) need be stored in buffer(s) in the LIN master until previous message is completed then take next parallel request in the queue and send on LIN etc.Similar behaviour is also valid for queued request in bootloader, i.e. a physical addressed diagnostic request on LIN shall always be completed before next physical addressed diagnostic request can be sent.

This means the LIN master shall be able to be re-programmed during the same time as the LIN slave.4.5.1.11.2 LIN master time out

To ensure a minimum performance requirement for parallel communication and optimize SWDL performance.Source:Verification Method: Test Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU Legacy ID: 442653v0For each LIN network behind the LIN master: In bootloader mode, the LIN master shall be able to reserve at least a 324 bytes RAM buffer pool only for responses.The buffers for each LIN network shall be structured as: Buffers size Number of Buffers Memory need Total Memory need 100 3 300 8 3 24 # of buffers 6 324 4.5.2 UDS Data4.5.2.1 UDS Data4.5.2.1.1 APPENDIX4.5.2.1.1.1 Appendix AData records requested and reported via diagnostic services shall fit into one of the data classifications as described below.Where multi-byte data records are specified and the byte order is not already specified in [Data_4] Global Master Reference Database then the order shall be that the most significant byte of the multi-byte record shall be placed in the data byte with the lowest number according to the data byte numbering convention used in [Data_50] Road vehicles – Diagnostics systems – Diagnostic services.Data type 1- ASCII (American Standard Code for Information Interchange)The ASCII data type contains one character per byte with a value between 0x00 and 0x7F using the standard ASCII code. ASCII parameters shall always be left justified (i.e., the most significant byte represents the first character) with any unused bytes filled with 0x00.Data type 2- BCD (Binary Coded Decimal)The BCD data type contains two numbers per byte with a value between 0 and 9 using the standard 4 bit hex value for each number. BCD parameters shall always be left justified (i.e., the most significant bit represents the first number) with any unused nibbles filled with 0xF.Data type 3- State EncodedThe state encoded data type is used when hexadecimal values represent unique states (e.g., using different values to represent the states of the ignition switch). State encoded parameters shall be limited to a maximum size of 1 byte (i.e., 256 unique states).Data type 4- Bit-MappedThe bit-mapped data type contains the binary state (0/1) of a parameter in a single bit (e.g., the discrete state of an ECU output may be represented as "0" for "Off" and "1" for "On"). If a particular bit-mapped parameter is not supported within a data record that is being reported by the ECU, the value of this bit shall be set to zero. Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU Data type 5- Unsigned NumericThe unsigned numeric data type is used to represent data that has a defined range of values and a specific resolution that can be represented through hexadecimal encoding. Each unsigned numeric parameter consists of a size in bits (n), a resolution (r), and an offset. The minimum value of the unsigned parameter is equal to the offset. The maximum value of the unsigned parameter is equal to ((2 n-1) * r) + offset). The maximum value of n is 32. Data type 6- Signed NumericThe signed numeric data type is used to represent data that has a defined range of values and a specific resolution that can be represented through 2's complement encoding. Each signed numeric parameter consists of a size in bits (n) and a resolution (r). The minimum value of the signed parameter is equal to - (2 (n-1) * r). The maximum value of the signed parameter is equal to ((2 (n-1) - 1) * r). The maximum value of n is 32. Data type 7- Binary floating pointThe binary floating point data type is used to represent data that has a defined range of values and a specific resolution that can be represented through the IEEE 754 single precision standard for binary floating point arithmetic. Each binary floating point parameter consists of a sign bit, exponent, and mantissa that is stored in accordance with single precision IEEE 754. Data type 8 - HexadecimalThe hexadecimal data type contains two characters per byte with a value between 0 and 9 and between A and F using the standard 4 bit hex value for each character. 4.5.2.1.2 Requirements 4.5.2.1.2.1 Requirements from section Diagnostic Data

title: Compliance to ISO14229-1
body: 2093 v2 Compliance to ISO14229-1 Version history:(2): Purpose: The diagnostic strategy is to comply with the general ISO diagnostic specifications.Source: Section "Diagnostic Data"Verification Method: AnalysisLegacy ID: 67741v1 All diagnostic data supported by the ECU shall be compliant to [Data_50] Road vehicles – Diagnostics systems – Diagnostic services , UDS - Data - External publications . The ECU is not allowed to support other diagnostic data than specified in section 4 and in each implementation specification for the respective network (e.g. UDSonCAN, UDSonFR and UDSonIP) and by reference [Data_53] Road vehicles — End-of-life activation of on-board pyrotechnic devices — Part 1: General information , UDS - Data - External publications and [Data_54] Road vehicles — End-of-life activation of on-board pyrotechnic devices — Part 2: Communication requirements , UDS - Data - External publications unless it is approved by the responsible authority appointed by OEM.

title: Diagnostic data for private ECUs Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU
body: 2096 v2 Diagnostic data for private ECUs Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU Version history:(2): Change the Verification Method from Test to AnalysisPurpose: Specify that also private ECUs shall support diagnostic dataSource: Section 4 - DIAGNOSTIC DATA REQUIREMENTSVerification Method: AnalysisLegacy ID: 174453v0Private ECUs shall, from a diagnostic point of view, be regarded as if they were internally connected units (e.g. internal I/O-units reading sensors and controlling actuators) within the public ECU master itself. The public ECU master shall, on behalf of the private ECUs, support all the diagnostic data required by this document and that are applicable for the private ECUs.

title: Compliance to ISO26262
body: 2095 v1 Compliance to ISO26262 Version history:(1):Purpose: Implementation of diagnostics on safety related ECUs must comply with ISO 26262.Source:Verification Method: AnalysisLegacy ID: 67743v0For all ECUs implementing safety requirements with an ASIL higher than QM, it shall be ensured that the diagnostic functions required in this specification cannot violate any of those safety requirements, i.e. to demonstrate independence as required by [Data_55] Road vehicles - Functional safety , International Organization for Standardization, 2011 , UDS - Data - External publications . Exception to this requirement is allowed only when approved by the responsible authority appointed by OEM and will require that the diagnostic functions required in this specification are developed according to Road vehicles - Functional safety , International Organization for Standardization, 2011 , UDS - Data - External publications and the allocated ASIL of those safety requirement for wich independence cannot be demonstrated. title: Customer setting parameters data record
body: 2236 v2 Customer setting parameters data record Version history:(2):Purpose: The purpose is to support the ECU replacement process at workshopSource: Table "Requirements for definition of ECU/Vehicle status in data records"Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 344378v1A data record with identifier 0xDED0 shall be implemented if the ECU stores customer setting parameter.The data record shall only consist of record data that contain information of customer settings stored by the ECU. The data record is used for restoring customer settings in the ECU replacement process at a workshop.A customer setting is defined as:A function that is open for alteration by the customer and/or tester tool it will be possible to change and adapt behavior of the functionality in the car to suit the customer.A long term alteration that only is initiated by the customer himself. The ECU is not allowed to change the customer setting parameter. Short term adjustments that, due to safety or other reasons, only are valid in one driving cycle or less and will revert to a predefined value are not to be considered as customer setting parameter.A setting that can be done by the customer himself and by the tester tool or only by a tester tool (at workshop or remote).

title: Complete ECU PartSerial Number data record
body: 2210 v8 Complete ECU PartSerial Number data record Version history:(8): Clarification about the usage of Geely part numbers. Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU The data records shall be implemented exactly as defined in [Data_4] Global Master Reference Database.The data records (called "composite" data record) shall contain several data items in an arbitrary order. Each data item shall consist of a data identifier followed by the record data that is identified by the data identifier.The "composite" data record with identifier 0xEDA0 shall contain the following data items (the data items is depending of the currently active executing software):F120 or F121 or F122, Application- or PBL- or SBL Diagnostic Database Part numberF12A, ECU Core Assembly Part NumberF12B, ECU Delivery Assembly Part NumberF18C, ECU Serial NumberF12E or F125 or F124, ECU- or PBL Software Part Number(s) or SBL Software Version NumberF13F, Private ECU(s) or component(s) Serial Number.The "composite" data record with identifier 0xED20 shall contain the following data items (the data items is depending of the currently active executing software):F1A0 or F1A1 or F1A2, Application- or PBL- or SBL Diagnostic Database Part numberF1AA, ECU Core Assembly Part NumberF1AB, ECU Delivery Assembly Part NumberF18C, ECU Serial NumberF1AE or F1A5 or F124, ECU- or PBL Software Part Number(s) or SBL Software Version NumberF13F, Private ECU(s) or component(s) Serial Number.

title: ECU Software Extended Part Numbers data record
body: 2214 v4 ECU Software Extended Part Numbers data recordVersion history:(4): Clarification about the usage of Geely format part numbers.Purpose: To enable readout of the extended part numbers for the ECU softwaresSource: Section "ECU/Vehicle identification"Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 114062v2If required by the project responsible OEM, data records shall be implemented according to the following:A data record with identifier 0xF12F shall be implemented containing Volvo Cars format Part number.A data record with identifier 0xF1AF shall be implemented containing Geely format Part number.Both data records shall be implemented in all ECU:s independently of what car brand they shall be used in.The data records shall be implemented exactly as defined in [Data_4] Global Master Reference Database.The content of the dataRecord with dataldentifier 0xF12F shall be the following: Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU Byte Description #1 Total number of ECU Software Part Numbers #2 - 8 ECU Software #1 Part Number #9 - 15 ECU Software #2 Part Number . . . . #N - (N+6) ECU Software #X Part Number The content of the dataRecord with dataldentifier 0xF1AF shall be the following: Byte Description #1 Total number of ECU Software Part Numbers #2 - 9 ECU Software #1 Part Number #10 - 17 ECU Software #2 Part Number . . . . #N - (N+7) ECU Software #X Part Number The Part Number(s) is only allowed to be used for item(s) that can not be separately downloaded to the ECU according.

title: ECU Software Part Number data record
body: 2215 v6 ECU Software Part Number data record Version history:(6): Clarification about the usage of Geely part numbers. Purpose: To enable readout of the part number for the ECU software.Source: Section "ECU/Vehicle identification"Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 68207v4 A data record with identifier 0xF12E shall be implemented containing Volvo Cars format Part numbers.A data record with identifier 0xF1AE shall be implemented containing Geely format Part numbers.Both data records shall be implemented in all ECU:s independently of what car brand they shall be used in.The data records shall be implemented exactly as defined in [Data_4] Global Master Reference Database.The content of the dataRecord shall be the following: The content of the dataRecord with identifier 0xF12E shall be the following: Byte Description #1 Total number of ECU Software Part Numbers #2 - 8 ECU Software #1 Part Number #9 - 15 ECU Software #2 Part Number . . . . #N - (N+6) ECU Software #X Part Number The content of the dataRecord with identifier 0xF1AE shall be the following: Byte Description #1 Total number of ECU Software Part Numbers #2 - 9 ECU Software #1 Part Number GEELYGeely Automotive Research Institute(Ningbo)Co.Ltd Document TypeNote-SWRS Document Release StatusRELEASED Document No Revision005 Volume No01 Page No900(1572) Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU #10 - 17 ECU Software #2 Part Number. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . GEELYGeely Automotive Research Institute(Ningbo)Co.Ltd Document TypeNote-SWRS Document Release StatusRELEASED Document No Revision005 Volume No01 Page No901(1572) Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU

title: One time write of the Security Constant data record
body: 2218 v2One time write of the Security Constant data record Version history:(2):Purpose: To limit the possibility to change the value of the security constant to a one time writing of the value.Source: Section "ECU/Vehicle identification"Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 68183v1If it is possible to change the value of the data record with identifier 0xF102, by diagnostic service defined in [Data_1] UDS Services, the value is allowed to be changed only one single time. Once the value has been changed, it shall not be possible to change the value again. Change of the value is optional only when the ECU is executing the secondary bootloader - programming session .

title: Part number data records coding
body: 2219 v6Part number data records coding Version history:(6): Change the Verification Method from Analysis to TestPurpose: N/ASource: Section "ECU/Vehicle identification"Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 68214v4Part number data records used by VCC shall have 8 digits for part number + 3 characters (version suffix).Part number data records used by Geely shall have 10 digits for part number + 3 characters (version suffix).T he part number digits shall be coded in BCD and the 3 characters shall be coded in ASCII.The data record used by VCC shall have a fixed length of 7 bytes and the data record used by Geely shall have a fixed length of 8 bytes, be right justified with any unused digit(s) filled with 0.If version suffix contains one character, there shall be two space characters between the part number digits and the version suffix.If version suffix contains two characters, there shall be one space character between the part number digits and the version suffix.This requirement applies to all data records with the following identifiers used by VCC:F120, F121, F122, F125, F12A, F12B, F12C, F12E, F12F.This requirement applies to all data records with the following identifiers used by Geely:F1A0, F1A1, F1A2, F1A5, F1AA, F1AB, F1AC, F1AE, F1AF.

title: Primary Bootloader Software Part Number data record
body: 2221 v4 Primary Bootloader Software Part Number data record Version history:(4): Clarification about the usage of Geely format part numbers. Purpose: To enable readout of the part number of the Primary Bootloader SW.Source: Section "ECU/Vehicle identification"Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 68225v2A data record with identifier 0xF125 shall be implemented containing Volvo Cars format Part number.A data record with identifier 0xF1A5 shall be implemented containing Geely format Part number.Both data records shall be implemented in all ECU:s independently of what car brand they shall be used in.The data records shall be implemented exactly as defined in [Data_4] Global Master Reference Database.

title: Private ECU(s) or component(s) Serial Number data record
body: 2222 v1 Private ECU(s) or component(s) Serial Number data record Version history:(1):Purpose: To support read out of serial numbers for private ECUs or components that are required by legislation to have additional documentation and where the case is that the private ECUs / components does not support to be addressed directly by a tester.Source:Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 442733v0A data record with identifier 0xF13F shall be implemented only if the following conditions are fulfilled:• The ECU is a Public ECU master for Private ECU(s) or component(s) which has Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHUadditional documentation requirements.The Public ECU master does not support gateway functionality for the private ECU(s) / component(s) in question, meaning that a tester can not read the serial number from the Private ECU(s) or component(s) by addressing it directly.The content of the data record shall only consist of serial number(s) for Private ECU(s) or component(s) that are subject to additional documentation requirements. The decision if a Private ECU or component will be subject for additional documentation is made by responsible authority at OEM.The content of the data record shall only consist of serial number(s) for those Private ECU(s) or component(s) that can not be directly addressed by a tester.The length of the serial number for a private ECU / component shall be maximum 12 digits.The coding of the serial number shall be alphanumeric.The serial number shall be right justified with any unused digits filled with 0, in total 12 bytes.If a private ECU / component, that is supposed to be present according to the ECU master, fails to answer when the public ECU master collect private ECUs / components part & serial numbers, this shall be shown by filling all bytes in the missing number with 0xFF.If the configuration of a vehicle excludes a private ECU / component (i.e certain private ECU / component are not mounted in the vehicle) this shall be shown by having all bytes in the serial number for that specific private ECU / component filled with 0x00.The content of the data record shall be the following:Byte Description#1 Total number of Private ECU(s) / component(s) Serial Numbers#2 -13 Private ECU / component #1 Serial Number#14 - 26 Private ECU / component #2 Serial Number.. ..#N - (N+12) Private ECU / component #X Serial Number

title: Secondary Bootloader Diagnostic Database Part Number
body: 2223 v4 Secondary Bootloader Diagnostic Database Part NumberVersion history:(4): Clarification about the usage of Geely part numbers.Purpose: To enable readout of a database key for the diagnostic database used by the ECU's secondary bootloader SW.Source: Section "ECU/Vehicle identification"Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 68194v2A data record with identifier 0xF122 shall be implemented containing Volvo Cars format Part number.A data record with identifier 0xF1A2 shall be implemented containing Geely format Part number.Both data records shall be implemented in all ECU:s independently of what car brand they shall be used in.The data records shall be implemented exactly as defined in [Data_4] Global Master Reference Database.

title: Secondary Bootloader Software Version Number data record
body: 2224 v1 Secondary Bootloader Software Version Number data recordVersion history: Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU (1):Purpose: To enable readout of the version number of the Secondary Bootloader SW.Source: Section: ECU/Vehicle identificationVerification Method: TestLegacy ID: 129845v0A data record with identifier 0xF124 shall be implemented exactly as defined in reference [Data_4] Global Master Reference Database.

title: Secondary Bootloader Software Version Number data record coding
body: 2225 v2 Secondary Bootloader Software Version Number data record coding Version history:(2):Purpose: To enable correct interpretation of the Secondary Bootloader Software Version Number.Source: Section: ECU/Vehicle identificationVerification Method: InspectionLegacy ID: 129842v1The Secondary Bootloader Software Version Number 0xF124 shall be BCD encoded, right justified, all unused digit shall be filled with 0 in total 7 bytes.

title: Vehicle Configuration Parameters data record
body: 2226 v1 Vehicle Configuration Parameters data record Version history:(1):Purpose: To enable readout of the Vehicle Configuration Parameters.Source: Section "ECU/Vehicle identification"Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 68185v0A data record with identifier 0xF106 shall be implemented, exactly as defined in [Data_4] Global Master Reference Database, in the Car Configuration Domain Master, on networks with ECU configuration controlled by an on-board master configuration file.

title: Vehicle Identification Number data record
body: 2227 v1 Vehicle Identification Number data record Version history:(1):Purpose: To enable readout of the standard 17 character VIN (as written on the vehicle identification plate).Source: Section "ECU/Vehicle identification"Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 68227v0If the ECU has a requirement to store VIN, a data record with identifier 0xF190 shall be implemented exactly as defined in [Data_4] Global Master Reference Database Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU

title: Vehicle Information Section data record
body: 2228 v2 Vehicle Information Section data record Version history:(2):Purpose: To enable readout of Vehicle Information Section.Source: Section "ECU/Vehicle identification"Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 68205v1A data record with identifier 0xF114 shall be implemented exactly as defined in reference [Data_4] Global Master Reference Database, in the Car Configuration Domain Master, on networks with ECU configuration controlled by an on-board master configuration file.

title: Write of the Public Key data record
body: 2229 v3 Write of the Public Key data record Version history:(3):Purpose: To enable programming of the Public Key, for ECUs supporting Software Authentication where only the key (and not certificates) is used to verify the authenticity of the software.Source: Section "ECU/Vehicle identification"Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 418471v1If the ECU is supporting the Software Authentication concept where the data file is verified using a Public Key only as defined in [Data_10] General Software Authentication the ECU shall implement to:Write the Public Key data record with identifier 0xD01C, by diagnostic service defined in [Data_1] UDS Services, it is to be supported when the ECU is executing the secondary bootloader - programming session.4.5.2.1.2.7 Requirements from section DTC information - General

title: DTC Failure Type Byte
body: 2100 v1 DTC Failure Type Byte Version history:(1):Purpose: A unified failure type description shall be used by all DTCs since it will be displayed by the tools.Source: Table "Requirements on implementation of DTCs"Verification Method: AnalysisLegacy ID: 68265v0DTCs supported by an ECU shall use Failure Type Byte as defined in [Data_51] Diagnostic trouble code definitions , UDS - Data - External publications.

title: DTCs defined by GMRDB
body: 2101 v3 DTCs defined by GMRDB Version history: Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU (3): Change the Verification Method from Test to Analysis Purpose: All DTC information shall be supported by OEM specific tools and must therefore be defined in GMRDB.Source: Table "Requirements on implementation of DTCs"Verification Method: AnalysisLegacy ID: 68264v1 DTCs supported by an ECU shall be implemented as defined in [Data_4] Global MasterReference Database. Development specific implementer specified DTCs are excluded from from this requirement.

title: DTCs for faults caused by the ECU operating environment or by customer
body: 2102 v1 DTCs for faults caused by the ECU operating environment or by customer Version history:(1): Purpose: DTCs identifying faults caused by the ECU operating environment or by customer actions shall be defined in a separate range in order for the tools to be able to mask them out if required.Source:Verification Method: InspectionLegacy ID: 115161v0 DTCs that identifies faults caused by the ECU operating environment or by customer actions shall be defined in the base DTC range U2E00 to U2EFF and according to section Detection of faults caused by the ECU operating environment or customer actions .

title: DTCs for secondary faults caused by data from other ECU indicated as invalid
body: 2103 v3 DTCs for secondary faults caused by data from other ECU indicated as invalid Version history:(3): Purpose: DTCs identifying secondary faults (i.e. not root cause9 shall be defined in a separate range in order for the tools to be able to mask them out if required.Source: Table "Requirements on implementation of DTCs" - item 2.3Verification Method: AnalysisLegacy ID: 68270v2 DTCs that identifies faults caused by signal or data value received from another ECU where the signal/data is indicated as invalid by the transmitting ECU, shall be defined in the base DTC range U2C00 to U2CFF and according to section Detection of faults caused by signals and data values received from other ECUs .

title: DTCs for secondary faults caused by data from other ECU not indicated as invalid
body: 2104 v3 DTCs for secondary faults caused by data from other ECU not indicated as invalid Version history:(3): Purpose: DTCs identifying secondary faults (i.e. not root cause9 shall be defined in a separate range in order for the tools to be able to mask them out if required.Source: Table "Requirements on implementation of DTCs" - item 2.4 Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU Verification Method: AnalysisLegacy ID: 68271v2 DTCs that identifies faults caused by signal or data value received from another ECU where the signal/data is not indicated as invalid by the transmitting ECU, shall be defined in the base DTC range U2D00 to U2DFF according to section Detection of faults caused by signals and data values received from other ECUs.

title: DTCs that are needed only during the development of the ECU
body: 2105 v1 DTCs that are needed only during the development of the ECU Version history:(1): Purpose: DTCs that are needed only during the development of the ECU shall be defined in a separate range in order for the tools to be able to mask them out if required.Source: Table "Requirements on implementation of DTCs" - item 2.7Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 392611v0 DTCs that are needed only during the development or quality tracking of the ECU shall be defined in the base DTC range U2BFF.The requirements on detection of the faults that shall be identified by DTCs in this range are specified in the following sections.The FDC10 shall increase with the value 1 when the test sample failed criteria is met for the DTCs in this range.The maximum value of the FDC10 shall be set to +126 (which means that the value DTC status bits, except the bits 4 and 6, will never be set, they will remain unchanged) for the DTCs in this range.

title: DTCs that are needed only during the development of the ECU - implementerspecified
body: 2106 v5 DTCs that are needed only during the development of the ECU - implementerspecified Version history:(5): Purpose: DTCs that are needed only during the development of the ECU shall be defined in a separate range in order for the tools to be able to mask them out if required.Source: Table "Requirements on implementation of DTCs" - item 2.6Verification Method: InspectionLegacy ID: 115163v4 DTCs specified by the implementer that are needed only during the development or quality tracking of the ECU shall be defined in the base DTC range U2F00 to U2FFF.The requirements on detection of the faults that shall be identified by DTCs in this range are specified in section Requirements on detection of faults caused by signal/data content received from other ECUs.The FDC10 shall increase with the value 1 when the test sample failed criteria is met for the DTCs in this range.The maximum value of the FDC10 shall be set to +126 (which means that the value DTC status bits, except the bits 4 and 6, will never be set, they will remain unchanged) for the DTCs Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU in this range.

title: ECU operation cycle
body: 2107 v3 ECU operation cycle Version history:(3): Change the Verification Method to Analysis Purpose: Reference to requirements on an operation cycle that shall be supported by the ECU.Source: Section "Definitions- Operation cycle"Verification Method: AnalysisLegacy ID: 392752v1Refer to REQPROD 391191 - ECU operation cycle and REQPROD 391192 - ECU start up time, in [Data_1] UDS Services, for definition of an operation cycle and requirements on the ECU to start and stop an operation cycle.

title: Emissions related DTCs defined by SAEJ2012
body: 2108 v1 Emissions related DTCs defined by SAEJ2012 Version history:(1): Purpose: Emission related DTCs are defined by SAEJ2012.Source: Table "Requirements on implementation of DTCs" - item 1.1Verification Method: AnalysisLegacy ID: 68266v0For all emissions related ECUs, DTCs with base DTC value in any of the ranges P0000 to P0FFF, P2000 to P2FFF or P3400 to P3FFF shall be implemented as defined in [Data_51] Diagnostic trouble code definitions , UDS - Data - External publications.

title: Non emissions related DTCs defined by SAEJ2012
body: 2109 v2 Non emissions related DTCs defined by SAEJ2012 Version history:(2): Purpose: Standardized DTCs defined in SAEJ2012 shall be used.Source: Table "Requirements on implementation of DTCs" - item 2.1Verification Method: AnalysisLegacy ID: 68267v1DTCs with base DTC value in any of the ranges B0000 to B0FFF, B3000 to B3FFF, C0000 to C0FFF, C3000 to C3FFF, U0000 to U0FFF or U3000 to U3FFF shall be implemented as defined in [Data_51] Diagnostic trouble code definitions , UDS - Data - External publications and in the sections Detection of faults in external electrical circuits to Detection of faults due to configuration errors and software incompatibility and DTCs associated with driver indications .

title: Reporting of DTC information
body: 2110 v2 Reporting of DTC information Version history:(2): Purpose: It must be possible to extract DTC information from the ECU by standardized Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU services.Source: Table "Requirements on implementation of DTCs"Verification Method: AnalysisLegacy ID: 68262v1DTCs supported by an ECU shall be reported on request of the diagnostic services specified in [Data_1] UDS Services, and be reported not more than once in any response.4.5.2.1.2.8 Requirements from section Calibration of DTCs

title: Calibration of agedDTCLimit
body: 1804 v2 Calibration of agedDTCLimit Version history:(2):Purpose: To ensure that DTCs is calibrated correctly.Source: Section Calibration of DTCs, item 7.Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 408301v0If not otherwise is specified by this document or is approved by CEVT Electrical Architecture, the AgedDTCLimit shall be calibrated in such a way that the following is met:· The DTC aging counter (OCC2 or OCC5) shall reach the agedDTCLimit when the fault has not been detected at such a long time that it probably will not occur and be detected again. Typically, it is likely that the detected fault has been self-healed or detected by mistake.Refer to [Data 12] General Diagnostic Guideline for recommendations and guidelines on how this requirement shall be met.

title: Calibration of confirmedDTCLimit
body: 1805 v2 Calibration of confirmedDTCLimit Version history:(2):Purpose: To ensure that DTCs is calibrated correctly.Source: Section Calibration of DTCs. item 6Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 408300v0If not otherwise is specified by this document or is approved by the responsible authority appointed by OEM, the confirmedDTCLimit shall be calibrated in such a way that the following is met:· Calibration of DTC test sample failed is equal to the confirmedDTCLimit when it is very likely that that the most customers observe a symptom (caused by the detected fault) and is bothered by the symptom in such extent that they require repair of the vehicle.Typically, it is very likely that the detected fault can be considered as permanent (lasting), i.e. repetitive and persistent, and that it occurs and causes customer symptom during the most vehicle operations and environmental conditions.Note that customer symptoms may be caused by actions (e.g. reconfigurations) taken by the ECU that tries mitigating the effect (e.g. on customer function, engine emissions or system safety) of the detected fault. If the detected fault causes a driver indication (e.g. telltale, text message, etc.), it shall be regarded as a customer symptom.Refer to [Data 12] General Diagnostic Guideline for recommendations and guidelines on how Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU this requirement shall be met.

title: Calibration of DTC test sample failed
body: 1806 v1 Calibration of DTC test sample failed Version history:(1):Purpose: To ensure that DTCs is calibrated correctly.Source: Section Calibration of DTCs, item 1.Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 408292v0If not otherwise is specified by this document or is approved by the responsible authority appointed by OEM, the DTC test sample failed criteria shall be calibrated in such a way that the following is met:• The DTC test sample shall fail when the monitored item does not meet the design requirements specified by the implementer.Examples:1. The DTC test monitors an external circuit connected to the ECU and it runs periodically each 100 ms. The DTC test sample fail when the circuit is short to ground.2. The DTC test monitors the maximum end-to-end timing of a signal sent on the in-vehicle network. The DTC test sample fail as soon as the maximum end-to-end timing of the received signal is exceeded.Refer to section Definitions and Abbreviations for definition of DTC test sample.

title: Calibration of DTC test sample passed
body: 1807 v1 Calibration of DTC test sample passed Version history:(1):Purpose: To ensure that DTCs is calibrated correctly.Source: Section Calibration of DTCs, item 2.Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 408293v0If not otherwise is specified by this document or is approved by the responsible authority appointed by OEM, the DTC test sample passed criteria shall be calibrated in such a way that the following is met:• The DTC test sample shall pass when the monitored item meet the design requirements specified by the implementer.Examples:1. The DTC test monitors an external circuit connected to the ECU and it runs periodically each 100 ms. The DTC test sample pass when the circuit is not short to ground.2. The DTC test monitors the maximum end-to-end timing of a signal sent on the in-vehicle network. The DTC test sample pass when the maximum end-to-end timing of the received signal is met.Refer to section Definitions and Abbreviations for definition of DTC test sample.

title: Calibration of DTCTestFailedLimit
body: 1808 v2 Calibration of DTCTestFailedLimit Version history:(2): Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU Purpose: To ensure that DTCs is calibrated correctly.Source: Setion Calibration of DTCs, item 4Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 408296v0If not otherwise is specified by this document or is approved by the responsible authority appointed by OEM, the DTCTestFailedLimit shall be calibrated, i.e. the size of the DTC fault detection counter (FDC 10) step-up (increase) value shall be adjusted, in such a way that the following is met:• The DTC fault detection counter (FDC10) shall reach a value that is equal to the DTCTestFailedLimit (i.e. +127) when it is very likely that the most customers observe a symptom (caused by the detected fault) but probably not all of them is bothered by the symptom in such extent that they require repair of the vehicle.Note that customer symptoms may be caused by actions (e.g. reconfigurations) taken by the ECU that tries mitigating the effect (e.g. on customer function, engine emissions or system safety) of the detected fault. If the detected fault causes a driver indication (e.g. telltale, text message, etc.), it shall be regarded as a customer symptom.Refer to [Data 12] General Diagnostic Guideline for recommendations and guidelines on how this requirement shall be met.

title: Calibration of DTCTestPassedLimit
body: 1809 v2 Calibration of DTCTestPassedLimitVersion history:(2):Purpose: To ensure that DTCs is calibrated correctly.Source: Setion Calibration of DTCs, item 5Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 408299v0If not otherwise is specified by this document or is approved by the responsible authority appointed by OEM, the DTCTestPassedLimit shall be calibrated, i.e. the size of the DTC fault detection counter (FDC 10) step-down (decrease) value shall be adjusted, in such a way that the following is met:• The DTC fault detection counter (FDC10) shall reach a value that is equal to the DTCTestPassedLimit (i.e. -128) when the fault has not been detected for a while and the monitored object can currently be considered free from the fault.Typically, the FDC 10 step-down value is equal or a bit less than the FDC 10 step-up value.Refer to [Data 12] General Diagnostic Guideline for recommendations and guidelines on how this requirement shall be met.

title: Calibration of unconfirmedDTCLimit
body: 1810 v2 Calibration of unconfirmedDTCLimitVersion history:(2):Purpose: To ensure that DTCs is calibrated correctly.Source: Section Calibration of DTCs, item 3Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 408294v0 Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU If not otherwise is specified by this document or is approved by the responsible authority appointed by OEM, the unconfirmedDTCLimit shall be calibrated in such a way that the following is met:· The DTC fault detection counter (FDC10) shall reach a value that is equal to or greater than the unconfirmedDTCLimit when it is likely that at least some customers observer a symptom (caused by the detected fault) but probably only some of them is bothered by the symptom in such extent that they require repair of the vehicle.Typically, it is very likely that the detected fault is intermittent (temporary), i.e. sporadic and transient, and that it occurs and causes customer symptom during only certain (perhaps unusual) vehicle operation and environment conditions.Note that customer symptoms may be caused by actions (e.g. reconfigurations) taken by the ECU that tries mitigating the effect (e.g. on customer function, engine emissions or system safety) of the detected fault. If the detected fault causes a driver indication (e.g. telltale, text message, etc.), it shall be regarded as a customer symptom.Refer to [Data 12] General Diagnostic Guideline for recommendations and guidelines on how this requirement shall be met.4.5.2.1.2.9 Requirements from section Detection of faults

title: DTC values
body: 1816 v2 DTC values Version history:(2):Purpose: To enable easy identification of specific faults.Source: Section "Detection of faults"Verification Method: AnalysisLegacy ID: 68892v1Unless otherwise specified in the following sections, one unique DTC value shall be used to identify each fault that can be detected by a DTC test in an ECU. Grouping of faults to use one single common DTC is not allowed unless explicitly approved by the responsible authority appointed by OEM, or where the tables within this specification already shows the use of the same DTC. Where faults are combined, all of the associated stored DTC information (e.g. the fault detection counter) is also combined and no more than one instance of the DTC shall be reported in any response to the services specified in reference [Data_1] UDS Services. Where the implementer identifies a requirement for separate repair action or fault confirmation process for DTCs that are shown with the same DTC then the responsible authority appointed by OEM may permit the use of different DTCs.

title: Failure type value for DTCs
body: 1817 v2 Failure type value for DTCs Version history:(2):Purpose: To enable easy identification of specific faults.Source: Section "Detection of faults"Verification Method: AnalysisLegacy ID: 68893v1Unless specifically defined in this document, DTCs shall use Failure Type values which are the Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU same as the DTCFailureTypeByte defined by [Data_51] Diagnostic trouble code definitions,UDS - Data - External publications, as appropriate depending on the type of fault.A failure type value of 0x00 may only be used if the Base DTC description includes the failure type and is approved in [Data_4] Global Master Reference Database. In such cases the Base DTC may not be combined with any other failure type values.

title: Generic Test Run Criteria - car mode transition inhibit criteria
body: 1818 v2 Generic Test Run Criteria - car mode transition inhibit criteria Version history:(2):Purpose: Changing car mode may cause transitional effects that may trigger a DTC test.This must be avoided in order not to set false DTCs.Source: Section "Detection of faults"Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 68889v1A II DTC tests shall be inhibited during 5 seconds from any transition from one car mode to another. The inhibition shall start at notational consumption of the 'car mode' signal when a change of car mode is requested and shall be active for 5 s ± 2s. Exception is allowed (e.g. due to safety reasons or legal requirements on emissionrelated faults) if the DTC test is able to detect faults in an accurate and reliable manner without use of these test run criteria but possibly other test run criteria, and if approved by the responsible authority appointed by OEM.

title: Generic Test Run Criteria - car modes inhibit criteria
body: 1819 v2 Generic Test Run Criteria - car modes inhibit criteria Version history:(2):Purpose: In some car modes vehicle functions may be inhibited which may cause other behaviour than normally expected by the DTC tests.Source: Section "Detection of faults"Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 68891v1A II DTC tests shall be inhibited when the vehicle is set in any of the car modes Factory,Transport or Crash.

title: Generic Test Run Criteria - enable criteria
body: 1820 v3 Generic Test Run Criteria - enable criteria Version history:(3):Purpose: A general rule is that all DTC tests shall run all the time that the ECU is "in operation".Source: Section "Detection of faults"Verification Method: AnalysisLegacy ID: 68886v2DTC tests shall be enabled all the time during an operation cycle provided that no inhibited criteria are met.If the ECU performs any action due to fault detected by the DTC test (e.g. in order to mitigate Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU the effect of the fault on customer functions or system safety), the DTC tests shall not be inhibited after the ECU has performed the action (e.g. has reduced or turned off the customer functions that are affected by the fault). However, if this is not appropriate and if approved by the responsible authority appointed by OEM, the DTC test may be inhibited in this case.The DTC tests shall not be inhibited (while the ECU is in operation) when the functionality, which can be affected by fault detected by the DTC test, is not active (e.g. is disabled when the functionality is not used). However, if this is not appropriate and if approved by the responsible authority appointed by OEM, the DTC test may be inhibited in this case.

title: Generic Test Run Criteria - low power inhibit criteria
body: 1821 v4 Generic Test Run Criteria - low power inhibit criteria Version history:(4):Purpose: DTC tests shall be regarded as unreliable when electrical power availability is limited, i.e. the tests shall be inhibited.Source: Section "Detection of faults"Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 68887v3If the ECU is power supplied from the 12 V system for which the EIPowerLevel signal is applicable, all DTC tests shall be inhibited when electrical power availability is limited, as indicated by EIPowerLevel 1. Exception: A test shall not be inhibited during engine cranking if the test can detect faults that can occur during cranking and that can prevent the transition to engine running. Other exception is allowed (e.g. due to safety reasons or legal requirements on emissionrelated faults) if the DTC test is able to detect faults in an accurate and reliable manner without use of these test run criteria but possibly other test run criteria, and if approved by the responsible authority appointed by OEM

title: Generic Test Run Criteria - low voltage inhibit criteria
body: 1822 v1 Generic Test Run Criteria - low voltage inhibit criteria Version history:(1):Purpose: DTC tests shall be regarded as unreliable when the ECU supply voltage is low, i.e. the tests shall be inhibited.Source: Section "Detection of faults"Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 68890v0A II DTC tests shall be inhibited when voltage supplied to the ECU is lower than required for ensuring correct fault monitoring. The low voltage limit shall be defined by the implementer but shall not be higher than the lower limit of the supply voltage range specified for the function(s) which includes the monitored component/system, unless otherwise defined in this document.

title: Generic Test Run Criteria - usage mode transition inhibit criteria
body: 1823 v4 Generic Test Run Criteria - usage mode transition inhibit criteria Version history:(4):Purpose: Changing usage mode may cause transitional effects that may trigger a DTC test. This must be avoided in order not to set false DTCs. Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU Source: Section "Detection of faults"Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 68888v3If not otherwise is specified, all DTC tests shall be inhibited during 5 seconds from any transition from one usage mode to another. The inhibition shall start at notational consumption of the 'usage mode' signal when a change of usage mode is requested and shall be active for 5 s ± 2s. Exception is allowed (e.g. due to safety reasons or legel requirements on emissionrelated faults) if the DTC test is able to detect faults in an accurate and reliable manner without use of these test run criteria but possibly other test run criteria, and if approved by the responsible authority appointed by OEM.

title: Test Run Criteria - Updating the DTC Fault Detection Counter
body: 1824 v3 Test Run Criteria - Updating the DTC Fault Detection Counter Version history:(3):Purpose: If a DTC test is stopped by an inhibit criteria the actual test may not be allowed to stop due to safety or other functional requirements. In order to stop updating the DTC information it is sufficient to stop updating FDC10. Note that if the actual test is not stopped and the ECU can take any action due to faults detected by the DTC test (e.g. reduce or shut off its functionality or request a warring indicator) that for sure can cause customer symptom the updating of the FDC10 should not be stopped (i.e. the test is not inhibited in this case).Source: Section "Detection of faults"Verification Method: AnalysisLegacy ID: 68885v2If a DTC test is inhibited it shall stop updating the DTC Fault Detection Counter (FDC10).4.5.2.1.2.10 Requirements from section Detection of faults in external electrical circuits

title: Base DTC value for detection of low supply voltage
body: 1959 v1 Base DTC value for detection of low supply voltage Version history:(1):Purpose: To enable easy identification of specific faults.Source: Table "Requirements on detection of faults in external electrical circuits connected to the ECU" - item 10.1Verification Method: AnalysisLegacy ID: 69021v0Detection of low supply voltage shall use base DTC value U3003 to identify the fault.

title: Base DTC value for faults in high side driver outputs
body: 1960 v1 Base DTC value for faults in high side driver outputs Version history:(1):Purpose: To enable easy identification of specific faults. Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU Source: Table "Requirements on detection of faults in external electrical circuits connected to the ECU" - items 6.1, 6.2 and 6.3Verification Method: AnalysisLegacy ID: 68961v0High side driver outputs circuits which has fault detection implemented shall have one unique base DTC value for each output circuit.

title: Base DTC value for low side driver outputs
body: 1961 v1 Base DTC value for low side driver outputs Version history:(1):Purpose: To enable easy identification of specific faults.Source: Table "Requirements on detection of faults in external electrical circuits connected to the ECU" - items 5.1, 5.2 and 5.3Verification Method: AnalysisLegacy ID: 68918v0Low side driver outputs circuits which has fault detection implemented shall have one unique base DTC value for each output circuit.

title: Base DTC value for short circuit and open circuit faults in FM, PCM, PWM...
body: 1962 v1 Base DTC value for short circuit and open circuit faults in FM, PCM, PWM... Version history:(1):Purpose: To enable easy identification of specific faults.Source: Table "Requirements on detection of faults in external electrical circuits connected to the ECU" - items 3.1, 3.2, 4.1 and 4.2Verification Method: AnalysisLegacy ID: 68910v0The ECU shall implement one unique base DTC value for each FM, PCM, PWM and similar input circuit for detection short circuit to ground faults, short circuit to battery and open circuit faults.

title: Base DTC value for short circuit to battery or open circuit faults in an...
body: 1963 v1 Base DTC value for short circuit to battery or open circuit faults in an... Version history:(1):Purpose: To enable easy identification of specific faults.Source: Table "Requirements on detection of faults in external electrical circuits connected to the ECU" - item 2.1 and 2.2Verification Method: AnalysisLegacy ID: 68903v0The ECU shall implement one unique base DTC value for each analog input circuit for detection short circuit to ground faults, short circuit to battery and open circuit faults. Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU

title: Base DTC value for switch inputs
body: 1964 v1 Base DTC value for switch inputs Version history:(1):Purpose: To enable easy identification of specific faults.Source: Table "Requirements on detection of faults in external electrical circuits connected to the ECU" - item 1.1 and 1.2Verification Method: AnalysisLegacy ID: 68899v0The ECU shall implement one unique base DTC value for each switch input circuit for which fault detection is implemented.

title: Detection of CS- or CRC-error on private ECU network
body: 1965 v1 Detection of CS- or CRC-error on private ECU network Version history:(1):Purpose: Basic requirement to enable detection of faults.Source: Table "Requirements on detection of faults in external electrical circuits connected to the ECU" - item 9.3Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 68988v0If the ECU is a Public ECU master on a network and it is able to detect CS- or CRC-error on received messages on that network as part of the ECU functional requirements (i.e. where the primary reason for the fault monitor is another than to support generation of DTC information) this fault shall also be identified by an appropriate DTC.Otherwise, the ECU shall be able to detect this fault as defined by a feasibility study performed by the implementer. (The feasibility study is required to decide if a technical solution is available and its cost is justified for the fault detection to be implemented. The implementer is responsible for the feasibility study. The feasibility study shall be approved by the responsible authority appointed by OEM).

(The feasibility study is required to decide if a technical solution is Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU available and its cost is justified for the fault detection to be implemented. The implementer is responsible for the feasibility study. The feasibility study shall be approved by the responsible authority appointed by OEM).

title: Failure type value for short circuit and open circuit faults in FM, PCM,...
body: 1990 v1Failure type value for short circuit and open circuit faults in FM, PCM,... Version history:(1):Purpose: To enable easy identification of specific faults.Source: Table "Requirements on detection of faults in external electrical circuits connected to the ECU" - items 3.1, 3.2, 4.1 and 4.2Verification Method: AnalysisLegacy ID: 68911v0DTCs for faults in FM, PCM, PWM and similar input circuits shall use Failure Type value according to one of the following alternativesAlternative 1: Input circuits which have fault detection for short circuit to battery or open circuit faults implemented that can differentiate between the two faults shall use Failure Type value 0x12 and 0x13, as appropriate depending on the type of fault. If the fault detection can not differentiate between the two faults then Failure Type value 0x33 or 0x34, as appropriate depending on the type of fault, shall be used for both faults.DTCs for short circuit to ground faults shall use Failure Type value 0x11.Alternative 2: Input circuits which have fault detection for short circuit to ground or open circuit faults implemented that can differentiate between the two faults shall use Failure Type value 0x11 and 0x13, as appropriate depending on the type of fault. If the fault detection can not differentiate between the two faults then Failure Type value 0x33 or 0x34, as appropriate depending on the type of fault, shall be used for both faults.DTCs for short circuit to battery faults shall use Failure Type value 0x12.

Source: Table "Requirements on detection of faults inferred from system behaviour" - item 2.1 Verification Method: Analysis Legacy ID: 69647v0 If the ECU is able to detect if the measured behaviour of a component or system do not follow the predictions of a simulation of expected behaviour which is being run by the ECU, as part of the ECU functional requirements (i.e. where the primary reason for the fault monitor is another than to support generation of DTC information) each such fault shall also be identified by an appropriate DTC. title: Detection of corrupt data received from other ECU by end-to-end checksum
body: 1831 v1 Detection of corrupt data received from other ECU by end-to-end checksum Version history:(1): Purpose: To handle the situation where there may be a customer complaint and a symptom associated with the ECU generating the DTC but the root cause is located on another ECU which may or may not be exhibiting any symptoms.Source: Table "Requirements on detection of faults caused by signal/data content received from other ECUs"Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 332533v0 If the ECU detects, by the data protection mechanism end-to-end checksum implemented at application level in the ECU, that a data value received from other ECU is corrupted each such fault shall also be identified by an appropriate DTC.

title: Detection of corrupt data received from other ECU by rolling counter
body: 1832 v2 Detection of corrupt data received from other ECU by rolling counter Version history:(2): Purpose: To handle the situation where there may be a customer complaint and a symptom associated with the ECU generating the DTC but the root cause is located on another ECU which may or may not be exhibiting any symptoms.Source: Table "Requirements on detection of faults caused by signal/data content received from other ECUs" - item 4.1Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 71752v1 If the ECU detects, by the data protection mechanism rolling counter implemented at application level in the ECU, that a data value received from other ECU is corrupted (the data is received without the corresponding rolling count value being properly updated e.g. incremented by the value 1 when expected), as part of the ECU functional requirements (i.e. where the Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU primary reason for the fault monitor is another than to support generation of DTC information)each such fault shall also be identified by an appropriate DTC.

title: Detection of corrupt data received from other ECU by up-date-bit
body: 1833 v3 Detection of corrupt data received from other ECU by up-date-bit Version history:(3): Purpose: To handle the situation where there may be a customer complaint and asymptom associated with the ECU generating the DTC but the root cause is located on another ECU which may or may not be exhibiting any symptoms.Source: able "Requirements on detection of faults caused by signal/data content received from other ECUs"Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 332551v2 If the ECU detects, by the data protection mechanism end-to-end checksum implemented at application level in the ECU (the data is received without the corresponding up-date bit value being properly set e.g. set to the value 1 when expected), that a data value received from other ECU is corrupted each such fault may also be identified by an appropriate DTC.Note: The DTC may be mandatory if the DTC is emission related but this is not specified by this document.Note: The faults are identified by DTCs that are known as "LostComDTCs".If the DTC is not emission related the DTC status indicator 30:5 (SI30:5) – warningIndicatorRequestedSinceLastClear is allowed to be set to 1 for these DTCs despite the FDC10 never reach +127 as the DTCs are development specific. Refer to Table: "Requirements on implementation of DTC status indicators" for requirements on set of DTC SI 30:5 to 1. It is up to the implementer to specify the criteria for set the DTC SI 30:5 to 1.

title: Detection of other ECU not operating normally
body: 1834 v1 Detection of other ECU not operating normally Version history:(1): Purpose: To handle the situation where there may be a customer complaint and asymptom associated with the ECU generating the DTC but the root cause is located on another ECU which may or may not be exhibiting any symptoms.Source: Table "Requirements on detection of faults caused by signal/data content received from other ECUs" - item 1.1Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 70867v0 If the ECU detects that another ECU sends data that indicates it has detected a fault which causes it to operate with reduced or not correct functionality, as part of the ECU functional requirements (i.e. where the primary reason for the fault monitor is another than to support generation of DTC information) each such fault shall also be identified by an appropriate DTC. (The feasibility study is required to decide if a technical solution is available and its cost is justified for the fault detection to be implemented. The implementer is responsible for the feasibility study. The feasibility study shall be approved by the responsible authority appointed by OEM). Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU

body: 1815 v2 Detected of events associated with driver indications Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU Version history:(2):Purpose: If a driver indication (e.g. telltale, text message, etc.) exists which, when activated, recommends (e.g. by a service book instruction, text message, etc.) the driver to bring the car to a workshop, the workshop may need to be able to find the root cause for this indication by a DTC.Source: Section "Detection of events associated with driver indications"Verification Method: AnalysisLegacy ID: 71801v1A DTC test indicating the cause of the event that triggers an activation of a driver indication (which when activated, recommends the driver to bring the car to a workshop) shall be implemented as required by a study performed by the implementer and approved by the responsible authority appointed by OEM.4.5.2.1.2.18 Requirements from section DTC status bits

title: Support for DTC status bit confirmedDTC
body: 2125 v4 Support for DTC status bit confirmedDTC Version history:(4):Purpose: To provide information about the status of an individual DTC to the test tool.Source: Table "Requirements on implementation of DTC status bits"Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 71827v3The DTC status bit no 3, confirmedDTC, shall be supported for all DTCs supported by the ECU, as defined in [Data_50] Road vehicles – Diagnostics systems – Diagnostic services , UDS - Data - External publications, with the following addition:The bit shall be set to 1 when the OCC6 reaches the confirmedDTCLimit.The value of the the confirmedDTCLimit shall be in the range of [1, +15].The bit shall be reset to 0 when the DTC is aged.The bit shall not be set 1 and it shall be set to 0, in case of the bit is already set to 1, if there are no aging counter (OCC2 or OCC5) allocated to the DTC due to the long term memory overflow.(The status bit number is the bit number of the DTC status byte associated with the DTC.)

title: Data records not included in local snapshot data
body: 2118 v1 Data records not included in local snapshot data Version history:(1):Purpose: To ensure consistent storage of data records in local DTC snapshot data records.Source: Section "DTC snapshot data identification"Verification Method: Analysis Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU Legacy ID: 71837v0Data records defined either as SystemSupplierSpecific or dynamically defined (as defined according to the table Requirements on implementation of data records) shall not be included in local DTC snapshot data.

title: Order of multiple samples of data records in global and local snapshot data records
body: 2119 v1 Order of multiple samples of data records in global and local snapshot data records Version history:(1):Purpose: To ensure consistent storage of data records in local DTC snapshot data recordsSource:Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 115401v0If data is sampled multiple times (record type = 'Multiple samples') before the sampling criteria is satisfied, then the sampled values shall be repeated a defined number of times in the snapshot data record. The order of the DTC snapshot data in the DTC snapshot record shall be such that the data which is sampled first is put at the start of the record (in bytes #1 to n) and the next data sample is appended to data from the first sample (bytes #n+1 to m), and so on.4.5.2.1.2.20 Requirements from section DTC snapshot sampling criteria

title: Sampling criteria for DTCSnapshotRecordNumber 0x20, single sample
body: 2120 v5 Sampling criteria for DTCSnapshotRecordNumber 0x20, single sample Version history:(5):Purpose: To define the criteria for sampling of snapshot data when the DTC has reached its unconfirmed limit.Source: Table "Requirements on implementation DTC snapshot sampling criteria"Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 72012v4When implementing with AUTOSAR 4.0.x:For all DTCs supported by the ECU DTC snapshot data shall be sampled and stored with DTCSnapshotRecordNumber 0x20 when the following criteria is satisfied for the data associated with the DTC:Each time the FDC10 reaches a value that is equal to or greater than its unconfirmedDTCLimit until the FDC10 reaches the value +127 (since DTC information was last cleared) and each time the FDC10 reaches the value +127 until the DTC staus bit 3 – confirmedDTC is set to 1 (since DTC information was last cleared).If FDC10 reaches a value that is equal to or greater than its unconfirmedDTCLimit and less than +127 more than once during an operation cycle then the sampling of data shall be triggered the first time only. If FDC10 reaches the value +127 more than once during an operation cycle then the sampling of data shall be triggered the first time only. GEELYGeely Automotive Research Institute(Ningbo)Co.Ltd Document TypeNote-SWRS Document Release StatusRELEASED Document No Revision005 Volume No01 Page No1001(1572) Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU Only the last sampled DTC snapshot data shall kept in the memory (the previously sampled DTC snapshot data is overwritten).When implementing with AUTOSAR 4.1 or newer:For all DTCs supported by the ECU DTC snapshot data shall be sampled and stored with DTCSnapshotRecordNumber 0x20 when the following criteria is satisfied for the data associated with the DTC:Each time the FDC10 reaches the value +127 until the DTC status bit 3 – confirmedDTC is set to 1 (since DTC information was last cleared).If FDC10 reaches the value +127 more than once during an operation cycle then the sampling of data shall be triggered the first time only.Only the last sampled DTC snapshot data shall kept in the memory (the previously sampled DTC snapshot data is overwritten).

title: Sampling criteria for DTCSnapshotRecordNumber 0x21, single sample
body: 2121 v3 Sampling criteria for DTCSnapshotRecordNumber 0x21, single sampleVersion history:(3): Change the Verification Method to TestPurpose:Source:Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 441094v0When implementing with AUTOSAR 4.0x:This requirement is Not ApplicableWhen implementing with AUTOSAR 4.1 or newer:For all DTCs supported by the ECU DTC snapshot data shall be sampled and stored with DTCSnapshotRecordNumber 0x21 when the following criteria is satisfied for the data associated with the DTC:Each time the FDC10 reaches a value that is equal to or greater than its unconfirmedDTCLimit and less than +127 (since DTC information was last cleared).If FDC10 reaches a value that is equal to or greater than its unconfirmedDTCLimit and less than +127 more than once during an operation cycle then the sampling of data shall be triggered the first time only.Only the last sampled DTC snapshot data shall kept in the memory (the previously sampled DTC snapshot data is overwritten).

title: Sampling criteria for DTCSnapshotRecordNumber 0x30 to 0x3F, multiple samples
body: 2122 v2 Sampling criteria for DTCSnapshotRecordNumber 0x30 to 0x3F, multiple samplesVersion history: Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU (2):Purpose: To define the criteria for sampling of snapshot data when the DTC has reached its unconfirmed limit.Source:Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 115421v1For DTCs supported by the ECU DTC snapshot data may be sampled and stored with DTCSnapshotRecordNumber in the range 0x30 to 0x3F according to the following:The DTC snapshot data shall be sampled periodically. A number of samplers before and/or after the criteria are satisfied shall be stored (the number of samples, and the periodicity, shall be defined by the implementer). The sampling criteria is specified by the implementer. The DTC snapshot record shall only consist of DTC snapshot data that is needed during the development of the ECU. The implementer shall not expect that CEVT tools support the DTC snapshot record.

title: Sampling criteria for DTCSnapshotRecordNumber 0x40 to 0x4F, single sample
body: 2123 v1 Sampling criteria for DTCSnapshotRecordNumber 0x40 to 0x4F, single sampleVersion history:(1):Purpose: To define the criteria for sampling of snapshot data.Source: Table: Requirements on implementation DTC snapshot sampling criteriaVerification Method: TestLegacy ID: 336996v0For DTCs supported by the ECU DTC snapshot data may be sampled and stored with DTCSnapshotRecordNumber in the range 0x40 to 0x4F according to the following:The DTC snapshot data shall be sampled (and stored) once when the criteria is satisfied. The sampling criteria is specified by the implementer. The DTC snapshot record shall only consist of DTC snapshot data that is needed during the development of the ECU. The implementer shall not expect that CEVT tools support the DTC snapshot record.

title: Definition of global real time data record
body: 2258 v2 Definition of global real time data record Version history:(2):Purpose: Ensure that the global real time data has a useful resolution and accuracy.Source: Table "Requirements on implementation of global DTC snapshot data"Verification Method: AnalysisLegacy ID: 72018v1The ECU responsible for maintaining and distributing the real time data shall maintain a global time data record with the following range, resolution and accuracy:range 0x00000000 to 0xFFFFFFFFeresolution 1 bit = 100 msaccuracy minimum ±10 minutes/week (±0.1%)correct value not available = 0xFFFFFFFFafter the global time have reached 0xFFFFFFFFFE it shall restart from 0x00000000

title: Definition of total distance data record
body: 2259 v3 Definition of total distance data record Version history:(3):Purpose: Ensure that the total distance data has a useful resolution and accuracy.Source: Table "Requirements on implementation of global DTC snapshot data"Verification Method: AnalysisLegacy ID: 72020v2The ECU responsible for maintaining and distributing the total distance data shall maintain a total distance data record with the following range, resolution and accuracy:range minimum 0x000000 to 0x0F4240.resolution 1 bit = 1 kmthe accuracy shall be the same as or better than the accuracy of the total distance displayed in the dash boardcorrect value not available = 0xFFFFFFFF

title: Definition of vehicle battery voltage data record
body: 2260 v2 Definition of vehicle battery voltage data record Version history:(2):Purpose: Ensure that the vehicle battery voltage data has a useful resolution and accuracy.Source: Table "Requirements on implementation of global DTC snapshot data"Verification Method: AnalysisLegacy ID: 72021v1The ECU responsible for maintaining and distributing the vehicle battery voltage data shall maintain a vehicle battery voltage data record with the following range, resolution and accuracy: Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU range minimum / 0x00 to 0x60r resolution 1 bit = 0.25 Voltthe accuracy shall be according to section Requirements for detection of low supply voltage.correct value not available = 0xFF

title: Distribution of global DTC snapshot data
body: 2261 v3 Distribution of global DTC snapshot data Version history:(3): Change the Verification Method from Test to Analysis Purpose: To ensure that global snapshots data that is sampled and stored in each ECU is not too old.Source: Section "Global DTC snapshot data"Verification Method: AnalysisLegacy ID: 72024v1 Global DTC snapshot data shall be transmitted to all public ECUs by an ECU (one or more) responsible for maintaining and distributing the data according to the following requirements:- The ECU shall transmit current values of the data periodically each second on the network except the data record 0xDD02 - "Vehicle battery voltage" which shall be sent faster according to the requirements specified in section Additional requirements for detection of low supply voltage.- The ECU shall transmit the data with a maximum age of 250 ms, except the data record 0xDD02 - "Vehicle battery voltage" which shall be sent with a lower maximim age according to the requirements specified in section Additional requirements for detection of low supply voltage.

title: Maintaining global real time after power loss
body: 2262 v3 Maintaining global real time after power loss Version history:(3): Change the Verification Method from Test to Analysis Purpose: To ensure consistency in the distributed global real time value after power loss.Source: Table "Requirements on implementation of global DTC snapshot data"Verification Method: AnalysisLegacy ID: 72019v1 The ECU responsible for maintaining and distributing the real time data shall store the current value of global real time in long.term memory at least once each operation cycle. If the ECU loses power supply then, following reconnection of the power supply, it shall continue to count the global real time beginning from the stored value.

title: Storage of global DTC snapshot data when not available
body: 2263 v4 Storage of global DTC snapshot data when not available Version history:(4): Change the Verification Method from Test to Analysis Purpose: If data received from the network is not availabel at the sampling moment the last received value will be the most useful to store.Source: Section "Global DTC snapshot data"Verification Method: Analysis Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU Legacy ID: 72026v2If global DTC snapshot data received from the vehicle network is not available when the sampling criteria is fulfilled, the latest received value shall be used and stored as DTC snapshot data.If no value has been received in the current operation cycle a value representing "correct value not available", according to specified in table: Requirements on implementation of global DTC snapshot data, shall be used and stored as DTC snapshot data.

title: Supported data records in global DTC snapshot data
body: 2264 v10 Supported data records in global DTC snapshot data Version history:(10): Change the Verification Method from Test to AnalysisPurpose: To enhance fault tracing and root cause analysis specific vehicle global data shall be stored with each DTC.Source: Table "Requirements on implementation of global DTC snapshot data"Verification Method: AnalysisLegacy ID: 72017v8For all DTCs supported by the ECU the global DTC snapshot data records shall include the following data records, as defined in reference [Data_4] Global Master Reference Database and the stored data records shall be reported on request of the diagnostic services specified in reference [Data_1] UDS Services:0xDD00 Global real time.0xDD01 Total distance.0xDD02 Vehicle battery voltage.0xDD0A Usage mode.0xDD0B Partial Network Cluster (PNC). See note 10xDD0C EIPowerLevel.Note 1:This DID is not mandatory for all ECU's. It shall only be included in the Global DTC snapshot data when the ECU is required to implement this DID.4.5.2.1.2.22 Requirements from section Local DTC snapshot data

title: Storage of local DTC snapshot data when not available
body: 2265 v2 Storage of local DTC snapshot data when not available Version history:(2): Change the Verification Method from Test to AnalysisPurpose: If data received from the network is not availabel at the sampling moment the last received value will be the most useful to store.Source: Section "Local DTC snapshot data"Verification Method: AnalysisLegacy ID: 72028v0If local DTC snapshot data received from the vehicle network is not available when the sampling criteria is fulfilled, the latest received value shall be used and stored as DTC snapshot data.
