title: Support for local DTC snapshot data
body: 2266 v2 Support for local DTC snapshot data Version history:(2):Purpose: To enhance fault tracing and root cause analysis specific ECU local data shall be stored with each DTC.Source: Table "Requirements on implementation of local DTC snapshot data"Verification Method: AnalysisLegacy ID: 72027v1For all DTCs supported by the ECU local DTC snapshot data shall be implemented as defined by a feasibility study performed by the implementer. (The feasibility study is required to decide if a technical solution is available and its cost is justified for the DTC snapshot data to be implemented. The implementer is responsible for the feasibility study. The feasibility study shall be approved by the responsible authority appointed by OEM). The stored local DTC snapshot data records shall be reported on request of the diagnostic services specified in reference [Data_1] UDS Services.4.5.2.1.2.23 Requirements from section DTC operation cycle counters

title: Support for Operation Cycle Counter #1
body: 2111 v4 Support for Operation Cycle Counter #1 Version history:(4):Purpose: To provide enhanced information about the occurrence of a DTC that may be useful in the analysis of the fault.Source: Table "Requirements on implementation of DTC operation cycle counters"Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 72030v3For all DTCs supported by the ECU a counter identified by DTCExtendedDataRecordNumber=1 shall be implemented according to the following:When implementing with AUTOSAR 4.0.x:Definition:Number of operation cycles (including the current operation cycle) since the DTC fault detection counter 10 last reached a value that is equal to or greater than its unconfirmedDTCLimit or more (since DTC information was last cleared). All operation cycles, including those during which the test was not passed shall be included.Increment/clear criteria:The counter shall be incremented at the beginning of each operation cycle.The counter shall be cleared as soon as FDC10 reaches a value that is equal to or greater than its unconfirmedDTCLimit.If any count operation occurs which would cause a counter to roll over past 0xFF then the count value shall instead be maintained at 0xFF. Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU Reporting:The stored counter shall be reported as a 1 byte unsigned numeric value on request of the diagnostic services specified in reference [Data_1] UDS Services.When implementing with AUTOSAR 4.1 or newer:Definition:Number of operation cycles (including the current operation cycle) since the DTC fault detection counter 10 last reached the value +127 (since DTC information was last cleared). All operation cycles, including those during which the test was not passed shall be included.Increment/clear criteria:The counter shall be incremented at the beginning of each operation cycle.The counter shall be cleared as soon as FDC10 reaches the value +127.If any count operation occurs which would cause a counter to roll over past 0xFF then the count value shall instead be maintained at 0xFF.Reporting:The stored counter shall be reported as a 1 byte unsigned numeric value on request of the diagnostic services specified in reference [Data_1] UDS Services.

title: Support for Operation Cycle Counter #2
body: 2112 v5 Support for Operation Cycle Counter #2 Version history:(5):Purpose: To provide enhanced information about the occurrence of a DTC that may be useful in the analysis of the fault.Source: Table "Requirements on implementation of DTC operation cycle counters"Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 72031v4For all DTCs supported by the ECU a counter identified by DTCExtendedDataRecordNumber=2 shall be implemented according to the following:When implementing with AUTOSAR 4.0.x:Definition:Number of operation cycles (including the current operation cycle) since the DTC fault detection counter 10 last reached a value that is equal to or greater than its unconfirmedDTCLimit (since DTC information was last cleared). The operation cycles during which the test was not passed shall be excluded.Increment/clear criteria:In each operation cycle the counter shall be incremented as soon as the FDC10 reaches the value -128, unless FDC10 has already reached a value that is equal to or greater than its unconfirmedDTCLimit in the current operation cycle.The counter shall be cleared as soon as FDC10 reaches a value that is equal to or greater than its unconfirmedDTCLimit.If any count operation occurs which would cause a couter to roll over past 0xFF then the count Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU value shall instead be maintained at 0xFF. Reporting:The stored counter shall be reported as a 1 byte unsigned numeric value on request of the diagnostic services specified in reference [Data_1] UDS Services. When implementing with AUTOSAR 4.1 or newer:Definition:Number of operation cycles (including the current operation cycle) since the DTC fault detection counter 10 last reached the value +127 (since DTC information was last cleared).The operation cycles during which the test was not passed shall be excluded. Increment/clear criteria:In each operation cycle the counter shall be incremented as soon as the FDC10 reaches the value -128, unless FDC10 has already reached the value +127 in the current operation cycle.The counter shall be cleared as soon as FDC10 reaches the value +127.If any count operation occurs which would cause a couter to roll over past 0xFF then the count value shall instead be maintained at 0xFF. Reporting:The stored counter shall be reported as a 1 byte unsigned numeric value on request of the diagnostic services specified in reference [Data_1] UDS Services.

title: Support for Operation Cycle Counter #3
body: 2113 v5 Support for Operation Cycle Counter #3 Version history:(5):Purpose: To provide enhanced information about the occurrence of a DTC that may be useful in the analysis of the fault.Source: Table "Requirements on implementation of DTC operation cycle counters"Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 72032v4For all DTCs supported by the ECU a counter identified by DTCExtendedDataRecordNumber=3 shall be implemented according to the following: When implementing with AUTOSAR 4.0.x:Definition:Number of operation cycles (including the current operation cycle) since the DTC fault detection counter 10 first reached a value that is equal to or greater than its unconfirmedDTCLimit (since DTC information was last cleared).All operation cycles, including those in which the test has not been passed or the DTC fault detection counter 10 has not reached a value that is equal to or greater than its unconfirmedDTCLimit shall be included. Increment/clear criteria:The counter shall be incremented at the beginning of each operation cycle following the operation cycle where FDC10 first reached a value that is equal to or greater than its unconfirmedDTCLimit. Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU If any count operation occurs which would cause a counter to roll over past 0xFF then the count value shall instead be maintained at 0xFF.Reporting:The stored counter shall be reported as a 1 byte unsigned numeric value on request of the diagnostic services specified in reference [Data_1] UDS Services.When implementing with AUTOSAR 4.1 or newer:Definition:Number of operation cycles (including the current operation cycle) since the DTC fault detection counter 10 first reached the value +127 (since DTC information was last cleared).All operation cycles, including those in which the test has not been passed or the DTC fault detection counter 10 has not reached the value +127 shall be included.Increment/clear criteria:The counter shall be incremented at the beginning of each operation cycle following the operation cycle where FDC10 first reached the value +127.If any count operation occurs which would cause a counter to roll over past 0xFF then the count value shall instead be maintained at 0xFF.Reporting:The stored counter shall be reported as a 1 byte unsigned numeric value on request of the diagnostic services specified in reference [Data_1] UDS Services.

title: Support for Operation Cycle Counter #4
body: 2114 v4 Support for Operation Cycle Counter #4 Version history:(4):Purpose: To provide enhanced information about the occurrence of a DTC that may be useful in the analysis of the fault.Source: Table "Requirements on implementation of DTC operation cycle counters"Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 72033v3For all DTCs supported by the ECU a counter identified by DTCExtendedDataRecordNumber=4 shall be implemented according to the following:When implementing with AUTOSAR 4.0.x:Definition:Number of operation cycles (including the current operation cycle) during which the DTC fault detection counter 10 reached a value that is equal to or greater than its unconfirmedDTCLimit (since DTC information was last cleared).Increment/clear criteria:In each operation cycle the counter shall be incremented as soon as FDC10 has reached a value that is equal to or greater than its unconfirmedDTCLimit for the first time.If any count operation occurs which would cause a counter to roll over past 0xFF then the count value shall instead be maintained at 0xFF. Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU Reporting:The stored counter shall be reported as a 1 byte unsigned numeric value on request of the diagnostic services specified in reference [Data_1] UDS Services.When implementing with AUTOSAR 4.1 or newer:Definition:Number of operation cycles (including the current operation cycle) during which the DTC fault detection counter 10 reached the value +127 (since DTC information was last cleared).Increment/clear criteria:In each operation cycle the counter shall be incremented as soon as FDC10 has reached the value +127 for the first time.If any count operation occurs which would cause a counter to roll over past 0xFF then the count value shall instead be maintained at 0xFF.Reporting:The stored counter shall be reported as a 1 byte unsigned numeric value on request of the diagnostic services specified in reference [Data_1] UDS Services.

title: Support for Operation Cycle Counter #5
body: 2115 v4 Support for Operation Cycle Counter #5 Version history:(4):Purpose: To provide enhanced information about the occurrence of a DTC that may be useful in the analysis of the fault.Source: Table "Requirements on implementation of DTC operation cycle counters"Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 72034v3For all emission related DTCs supported by the ECU a counter identified by DTCExtendedDataRecordNumber=5 shall be implemented according to the following:Definition:Number of warm-up cycles since the DTC commanded the MIL to switch off (since DTC information was last cleared).The warm-up cycle is defined in [Data_52] OBD II regulation, section 1968.2 of title 13, California Code of Regulations, UDS - Data - External publications.Increment/clear criteria:The counter shall be incremented when warm-up cycle changes from false to true.The counter shall be cleared when the DTC fault detection counter 10 reach the value of +127. If any count operation occurs which would cause a counter to roll over past 0xFF then the count value shall instead be maintained at 0xFF.Reporting:The stored counter shall be reported as a 1 byte unsigned numeric value on request of the diagnostic services specified in reference [Data_1] UDS Services. Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU

title: Support for Operation Cycle Counter #6
body: 2116 v7 Support for Operation Cycle Counter #6 Version history:(7):Purpose: To provide enhanced information about the occurrence of a DTC that may be useful in the analysis of the fault.Source: Table "Requirements on implementation of DTC operation cycle counters"Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 72035v6 For all DTCs supported by the ECU a counter identified by DTCExtendedDataRecordNumber=6 shall be implemented according to the following:Definition:The number of consecutive operation cycles (including the current operation cycle) during which the DTC fault detection counter 10 reached the value of +127 (since DTC information was last cleared). The operation cycles during which the test was not completed shall be excluded. The minimum range of the counter is 0-15.Increment/clear criteria:In each operation cycle the counter shall be incremented as soon as FDC10 has reached the value +127 for the first time.The counter shall be cleared in the beginning of the operation cycle following an operation cycle where FDC10 did not reach the value +127 at any time but -128 (the counter shall maintain its value if the FDC10 did not reach the value -128). The counter may also be cleared when the confirmedDTCLimit is reached.If any count operation occurs which would cause a counter to roll over past 0xFF, then the count value shall instead be maintained at 0xFF.Reporting:The stored counter shall be reported as a 1 byte value on request of the diagnostic services specified in reference [Data_1] UDS Services.

title: Support for Operation Cycle Counter #7
body: 2117 v6 Support for Operation Cycle Counter #7 Version history:(6):Purpose: To provide enhanced information about the occurrence of a DTC that may be useful in the analysis of the fault.Source:Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 115561v5 For all DTCs supported by the ECU a counter identified by DTCExtendedDataRecordNumber=7 shall be implemented according to the following:When implementing with AUTOSAR 4.0.x:Definition:Number of operation cycles (including the current operation cycle) since the DTC fault Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU detection counter 10 first reached a value that is equal to or greater than its unconfirmedDTCLimit (since DTC information was last cleared). The operation cycles during which the test was not passed or the DTC fault detection counter 10 did not reach a value that is equal to or greater than its unconfirmedDTCLimit shall be excluded.Increment/clear criteria:The counter shall be incremented in each operation cycle, following the operation cycle where FDC10 first reached a value that is equal to or greater than its unconfirmedDTCLimit, as soon as the following criteria is met: The FDC10 reach the value -128 or a value that is equal to or greater than its unconfirmedDTCLimit.If any count operation occurs which would cause a counter to roll over past 0xFF then the count value shall instead be maintained at 0xFF.Reporting:The stored counter shall be reported as a 1 byte unsigned numeric value on request of the diagnostic services specified in reference [Data_1] UDS Services.When implementing with AUTOSAR 4.1 or newer:This requirements is Not Applicable4.5.2.1.2.24 Requirements from section DTC fault detection counters

title: Support for Fault Detection Counter #10
body: 2097 v6 Support for Fault Detection Counter #10 Version history:(6):Purpose: To provide enhanced information about the occurrence of a fault, that may be useful in the analysis of the fault, and enables detailed calibration of the corresponding DTC.Source: Table "Requirements for the implementation DTC fault detection counters"Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 72036v5For all DTCs supported by the ECU a counter identified by DTCExtendedDataRecordNumber=10 shall be implemented as defined in [Data_50] Road vehicles – Diagnostics systems – Diagnostic services ( service 19 sub-function 14 and Appendix D.5), UDS - Data - External publications and according to the following additional definitions:1. At the start of a new operation cycle the count value shall be 0.2. The count value shall be maintained between test runs within one and same operation cycle, also when the test run is blocked due to the test run criteria is not satisfied3. The DTC test may be completed (i.e. the DTC status bit 4 and 6 is set to 0) before FDC10 reaches +127 or -128, and passed (i.e. the DTC status bit 0 is set to 0) before FDC10 reaches -128, where approved by the responsible authority appointed by OEM.4. The maximum value of the counter may be set to +126 (which means that the value DTC status bits, except the bits 4 and 6, will never be set, they will remain unchanged) where approved by the responsible authority appointed by OEM or shall be set to +126 if that is specified by this document. Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU 5. If a single test sample of a test returns a fail result, when the current value of the counter is negative, the new count value resulting from the fail result shall be set as if the current count value had been 0 (a test sample represents the fail result shall always causes fault detection counter to decrement above 0).6. If a single test sample of a test returns a pass result, when the current value of the counter is positive, the new count value resulting from the pass result shall be set as if the current count value had been 0 (a test sample represents the pass result shall always causes fault detection counter to decrement below 0).7. The count value shall be updated (increased or decreased) each time the DTC test runs and produce a test sample failed or passed result. If the number of consecutive test sample failed results is more than 127 to reach the testFailedLimit +127 (from the start value 0) or if the number of consecutive test sample passed results is more than 128 to reach the testPassedLimit -128 (from the start value 0), the count value cannot be updated (increased or decreased) each time the DTC test runs and produce a test sample failed or passed result. In this case, and only in this case, may a pre-counter or similar (specified by the implementer) be used in order to reduce the number of updates to 127 (at increases) and 128 (at decreases). Refer to section Definitions and Abbreviations for definition of a test sample. Exception to this requirement (e.g. due to legal requirements) is allowed but only when approved by the responsible authority appointed by OEM.The stored counter shall be reported as a 1 byte signed numeric value with a range of -128 to + 127 on request of the diagnostic services specified in reference [Data_1] UDS Services.

title: Support for Fault Detection Counter #11
body: 2098 v4 Support for Fault Detection Counter #11 Version history:(4):Purpose: To provide enhanced information about the occurrence of a fault, that may be useful in the analysis of the fault.Source: Table "Requirements for the implementation DTC fault detection counters"Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 72038v3For all DTCs supported by the ECU a counter identified by DTCExtendedDataRecordNumber=11 may be implemented and if it is implemented then shall be according to the following definition:The count value shall be equal to the maximum value the FDC10 has reached during current operation cycle.The stored counter shall be reported as a 1 byte signed numeric value on request of the diagnostic services specified in reference [Data_1] UDS Services.

body: 2099 v2 Support for Fault Detection Counter #12 Version history:(2):Purpose: To provide enhanced information about the occurrence of a fault, that may be useful in the analysis of the fault.Source: Table "Requirements for the implementation DTC fault detection counters"Verification Method: Test Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU Legacy ID: 72039v1For all DTCs supported by the ECU a counter identified byDTCExtendedDataRecordNumber=12 shall be implemented according to the following definition:The count value shall be equal to the maximum value, which is equal to or greater than unconfirmedDTCLimit, the FDC10 has reached since the last time DTC information was cleared.The stored counter shall be reported as a 1 byte signed numeric value on request of the diagnostic services specified in reference [Data_1] UDS Services.4.5.2.1.2.25 Requirements from section DTC time stamp

title: Support for DTC time stamp #20
body: 2142 v3 Support for DTC time stamp #20 Version history:(3):Purpose: To provide enhanced information about the occurrence of a fault, that may be useful in the analysis of the fault.Source: Table "Requirements on implementation of DTC time stamps"Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 72041v2 For all DTCs supported by the ECU a data record identified byDTCExtendedDataRecordNumber=20 shall be implemented according to the following definition:The record value shall be equal to the global real time (data record 0xDD00) that is taken the first time FDC10 reaches a value that is equal to or greater than unconfirmedDTCLimit, since DTC information was last cleared.The stored data record shall be reported as a 4 byte value on request of the diagnostic services specified in reference [Data_1] UDS Services.

The feasibility study shall be approvedby the responsible authority appointed by OEM).If implemented bit no 4 of SI30 shall indicate SymptomSinceLastClear according to thefollowing definition:The bit shall be set to 1 when FDC10 is in the range [unconfirmedDTCLimit, +127] and specificconditions specified by the implementer, that need to be fulfilled in order to generate customersymptom, are satisfied.

body: 2137 v2 Support for DTC status indicator #30, testFailedSinceLastClear/Aged Version history:(2):Purpose: To provide information about the DTC test failed since the DTC was last agedor, as long as the DTC have not been aged, since the DTC information waslast clear.Source: Table "Requirements on implementation of DTC status indicators"Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 72071v1 For all DTCs supported by the ECU, bit no 7 of SI30 shall indicatetestFailedSinceLastClear/Aged according to the following definition:The bit is set to set to 1 wthen DTC test is falied i.e. when the FDC10 reach the value +127.The bit is reset to 0 when DTC is aged i.e. the SI30:3 is set to1.

title: Support for DTC status indicator #30, UnconfirmedDTC
body: 2138 v4 Support for DTC status indicator #30, UnconfirmedDTC Version history:(4):Purpose: To provide an early indication that a fault may be currently present.Source: Table "Requirements on implementation of DTC status indicators";Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 72064v3 Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU When implementing with AUTOSAR 4.0.x:For all DTCs supported by the ECU, bit no 0 of SI30 shall indicate UnconfirmedDTC according to the following definition:The bit shall be set to 1 when FDC10 reaches a value in the range [unconfirmedDTCLimit,+127]The bit shall be reset to 0 when FDC10 reaches the value -128.The value of the unconfirmedDTCLimit is specified by the implementer according to the requirements specified in section Generic requirements on calibration of DTCs.The value shall be in the range of [+1, +127].When implementing with AUTOSAR 4.1 or newer:For all DTCs supported by the ECU, bit no 0 of SI30 shall be set to 0.

title: DTC storage time
body: 2303 v2 DTC storage time Version history:(2): Change the Verification Method from Test to Analysis Purpose: To ensure that DTC information is up to date when reported by diagnostic service.Source:Verification Method: AnalysisLegacy ID: 115623v0 The DTC information shall be stored within a maximum delay time of "DTC storage time" T1=400 ms. The parameter "DTC storage time" T1 is defined as the time from that an event occurs (e.g. a fault is detected) that cause DTC information to be stored (updated) until the DTC information is available for access by diagnostic service specified in reference [1]. If many events (e.g. 10 or more) occur within a time period of T1 then may the "DTC storage time" be increased but only if that is approved by the responsible authority appointed by OEM.

title: Transfer of DTC information to long term memory
body: 2335 v3 Transfer of DTC information to long term memory Version history:(3): Change the Verification Method from Test to AnalysisPurpose: To ensure that no DTC information is lost during normal vehicle operation.Source: Section "Transfer of DTC information to long term memory"Verification Method: AnalysisLegacy ID: 72141v1If the ECU temporarily stores DTC information in short-term memory before storing it in long-term memory, any DTC information that has been added, deleted or changed during the operation cycle shall be transferred from short-term memory to long-term memory at the end of the operation cycle, and whenever required before it is erased from the short term memory if the erase is caused by normal vehicle operation.Situations/events, which are not regarded as normal vehicle operation, are:1) Unexpected disconnection of the ECU power supply while the ECU is in operation, due to Vehicle battery removal, fuse blow, connector disconnection or other similar cause which does not occur as part of normal vehicle operation.2) ECU supply voltage below minimum specification due to e.g. weak battery or other vehicle related fault.3) Diagnostic service requests that results in an ECU reset. See [Data_1] UDS Services, for services which are allowed to reset the ECU.4) Additional events, not covered by items 1-3 above, which have been documented by the implementer and approved by the responsible authority by OEM.DTC information from previous operation cycle shall be retained if temporarily stores DTC information in short-term memory is lost, in the current operation cycle, due to vehicle operation that is not regarded as normal.4.5.2.1.2.29 Requirements from section Clear DTC information

title: Clear DTC information by diagnostic service
body: 1811 v3 Clear DTC information by diagnostic service Version history:(3): Change the Verification Method from Test to AnalysisPurpose: To allow all DTC information to be cleared by request from e.g. the service Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU technician.Source: Table "Requirements in implementation of clear of DTC information" - item 1Verification Method: AnalysisLegacy ID: 72146v1All stored DTC information for all DTCs supported by the ECU, with the exceptions defined in [Data_50] Road vehicles – Diagnostics systems – Diagnostic services, UDS - Data - External publications, shall be cleared when requested by diagnostic service specified in [Data_1] UDS Services.

title: Clear DTC information when a DTC is aged
body: 1812 v6 Clear DTC information when a DTC is aged Version history:(6): Change the Verification Method from Test to AnalysisPurpose: To allow the DTCCConfirmation status to be reset if a failure has not been detected for a defined time.Source: Table "Requirements in implementation of clear of DTC information" - item 3Verification Method: AnalysisLegacy ID: 72152v4When implementing with AUTOSAR 4.0.x:When the counter used for aging of a DTC reaches the value agedDTCLimit defined for the DTC, no DTC information shall be cleared with some exception (reset of a DTC status bit and some DTC status indicators) that is specified in the document.The agedDTCLimit shall be a value in the range of [1, 255]. The counter used for aging shall either be operation cycle counter 2 or 5. The implementer shall specify the value of the agedDTCLimit according to the requirements specified in section Generic requirements on calibration of DTCs and which of the two counters shall be used for aging. An addition to specified above is that emission related DTCs may use both counters for aging. I this case is the DTC aged when both counters have reached their agedDTCLimit.When implementing with AUTOSAR 4.1 or newer:When the counter used for aging of a DTC reaches the value agedDTCLimit defined for the DTC, all DRC Snapshot data and Extended data records shall be cleared. All DTC status bits shall be cleared as well, except fro status bit testFailedSinceLastClear, this bit will retain its status.The agedDTCLimit shall be a value in the range of [1, 255]. The counter used for aging shall either be operation cycle counter 2 or 5. The implementer shall specify the value of the agedDTCLimit according to the requirements specified in section Generic requirements on calibration of DTCs and which of the two counters shall be used for aging. An addition to specified above is that emission related DTCs may use both counters for aging. I thiscase is the DTC aged when both counters have reached their agedDTCLimit.

title: Clear DTC information when an aged DTC reoccurs
body: 1813 v3 Clear DTC information when an aged DTC reoccurs Version history:(3): Change the Verification Method from Test to Analysis Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU Purpose: To ensure that new DTC information is captured when an aged DTC reoccurs.Source: Table "Requirements in implementation of clear of DTC information" - item 4Verification Method: AnalysisLegacy ID: 72154v1When implementing with Autosar 4.0x:If FDC10 for a DTC reaches a value equal to or greater than unconfirmedDTCLimit, after the DTC has been aged (i.e. the counter used for aging of the DTC has reached the value agedDTCLimit defined for the DTC), all DTC information, except the DTC status bits and FDC10, shall be cleared for that DTC.When implementing with Autosar 4.1 or newer:This requirement is Not Applicable

title: Clear DTC information when the long term memory overflows
body: 1814 v6 Clear DTC information when the long term memory overflows Version history:(6): Change the Verification Method from Test to Analysis Purpose: To define the rules for what DTC information that shall be stored and what shall be discarded in the event that long term DTC memory is full when new DTC information needs to be stored.Source: Table "Requirements in implementation of clear of DTC information" - item 2Verification Method: AnalysisLegacy ID: 72148v4If storage of DTC information is required but available storage for the DTC information in the long term memory is already full, all DTC information for all DTCs supported by the ECU, except the DTC status bits and FDC10, of lowest storage priority (see note 1 below) shall be cleared from the long term memory and replaced by the data that is required to be stored if the data that is required to be stored has higher storage priority according to the following priority order (1 is the highest priority):1. The DTC is associated with a warningIndicator (i.e. support the value 1 of the DTC status bit 7) and is not aged. See note 2 below.2. The DTC is not associated with a warningIndicator (i.e. do not support the value 1 of the DTC status bit 7).See note 2 below.3. The DTC is aged (i.e. the DTC status indicator 30, bit 3 is set to 1).Excluded from above stated storage priority are development specific DTCs (refer to table Requirements on implementation of DTCs regarding definition of development specific DTCs). They shall have the lowest storage priority (i.e, priority 4) of all DTCs supported by the ECU. However, development specific DTCs may have higher storage priority if the minimum number of DTCs that shall be possible to store in long term memory (according to Table: Requirements on minimum number of DTCs for which DTC information shall be possible to store in long-term memory) is increased with the number of the development specific DTCs that shall have higher storage priority. The mutual storage priority between developments specific DTCs is specified by the implementer.Safety and emission related DTCs and other specific DTCs may have additional storage priorities than above where approved by the responsible authority appointed by OEM.Note 1: If several data items (DTC information for several DTCs) of the same storage priority Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU are stored then shall the data item that has the highest value of OOC2 be cleared. If several data items (DTC information for several DTCs) of the same priority and the same value of OCC2 are stored then is it up to the implementer to specify which of these data that shall be cleared.Note 2: Stored DTC information is not aged when DTC status indicator 30, bit 3 is set to 0. DTC information that is required to be stored is not aged because DTC information is required to be stored when the DTC fault detection counter 10 reach a value in the range [unconfirmedDTCLimit, +127].4.5.2.1.2.30 Requirements from section Routines - General

body: 2329 v1 Check Programming Pre-conditions routine Version history:(i):Purpose: All ECUs must support routines defined for SWDL.The tester will send requests to all ECU to find out if they are prepared to enter program mode. This enables a robust and secure transition from the application to the bootloader by ensuring that all pre-conditions to transition to the bootloader are fulfilled when requested.Source: Table "Requirements for implementation of routines" - item 2Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 72177v0The Check Programming Pre-conditions routine with routine identifier 0x0206 shall be implemented as defined in [Data_4] Global Master Reference Database. If the ECU is able to enter program mode or not, i.e. if the criteria for entering program mode are fulfilled or not, at the moment of the routineControl request, shall be indicated by the corresponding RoutineStatusRecord response parameter. body: 2331 v2 Erase Memory routine Version history:(2):Purpose: All ECUs must support routines defined for SWDL.Source: Table "Requirements for implementation of routines" - item 4Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 72203v1The Erase Memory routine with routine identifier 0xFF00 shall be implemented as defined in [Data_4] Global Master Reference Database. The routine shall perform a non-volatile memory erase of the memory blocks defined by the memoryAddress and memorySize request parameters. The routine does not to be supported if the ECU has file system data storage and implements an alternative method e.g RequestFileTransfer – modeOfOperation parameter DeleteFile or ReplaceFile.

title: Erase Memory routine "already erased" detection
body: 2332 v1 Erase Memory routine "already erased" detection Version history:(1):Purpose: To reduce the overall software download time in case the memory is already erased when the ECU is delivered the factory.Source: Table "Requirements for implementation of routines" - item 4Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 72206v0If the ECU is delivered to CEVT with the complete programmable memory already erased, the routine shall include an "already erased" detection in order to reduce the overall software download time. If the complete programmable memory is "already erased" and all other preconditions are met (e.g. SBL is downloaded and activated), the routine shall not perform any erase operation and immediately send a final positive response message with RoutineCompleted=1 (Routine is completed ).Once one or more bytes of the ECU programmable memory area has been programmed, the "already erased" status shall be invalidated.Any erase memory requests when the "already erased" status is invalid shall erase the requested memory area. Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU

The information in each of the columns, and general requirements applicable to all tables, are described below:Type of item:General description of the type of item that shall be monitored by the DTC test.Depending on the subject of the specific table, this can be a description of the type of component, circuit, system, data, ECU etc., that shall be monitored.Item no.:A sequential number for each separate item, used for references.Detected faults/errors:Definition of the fault, or error, that shall be possible to detect by the DTC test.The detailed criteria for increasing/decreasing the DTC fault detection counter (see section DTC fault detection counters) shall be specified by the implementer, unless it is specified in the Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU table.Test PeriodIf a value is included in this column, the DTC test shall produce Test Samples, i.e. the DTC test fault detection logic shall execute and the DTC fault detection counter shall be updated (see section DTC fault detection counters for details regarding update of the DTC fault detection counter), periodically at this or a higher rate all the time while the Test Run Criteria are met (see column Test Run Criteria below) unless otherwise is specified by the table.The maximum period time between Test Samples shall be as specified by the table. However, in cases where the ECU application software uses a signal monitored by the DTC test more frequently than this specified maximum, then the period time shall be reduced to match that used by the application software.If no value is included in this column, the DTC test shall run one single time when the Test Run Criteria are met.Test Run Criteria:The Test Run Criteria defines the criteria that must be met for the DTC test to run.The Test Run Criteria can be defined both as Enable Criteria, e.g. "While output is activated", and as Inhibit Criteria, e.g. "Not during engine cranking". The DTC test shall run when all of the Enable Criteria are met and shall be inhibited if any of the Enable Criteria are not met, or if any of the Inhibit Criteria are met (Inhibit Criteria has priority over Enable Criteria, i.e. if at least one Inhibit Criteria is fulfilled while all of the Enable Criteria are met the DTC test shall be inhibited).If the test is inhibited it shall, as a minimum, stop updating the DTC Fault Detection Counter (FDC10, see section DTC fault detection counters). If the actual test can be stopped or not, or if it needs to run for other reasons, e.g. safety related or other application requirements, this shall be defined by the implementer. Note that if the actual test is not stopped and the ECU can take any action due to faults detected by the DTC test (e.g. reduce or shut off its functionality or request a warring indicator) that for sure can cause customer symptom the updating of the FDC10 should not be stopped (i.e. the test is not inhibited in this case).If the DTC test shall run one single time when the Test Run Criteria are met (no value is included in the "Test Period Time" column) the Test Run Criteria shall include an event description which will be a trigger condition for the test to run.The implementer shall specify if any partial DTC test results, obtained prior to the DTC test being inhibited by a Test Run Criteria, shall be used when the DTC test resumes execution. Table: Supported negative response codes Hex Description 12 subFunctionNotSupported- sub-function different from 0x04 or 0x06 in the request. 13 incorrectMessageLengthOrInvalidFormat- The length and/or format of the request message is incorrect. 31 requestOutOfRange- DTCMaskRecord is different from 0xFFFFF and different from a supported DTC number.or- sub-function is 0x04 and DTCSnapshotRecord is different from 0x FF and different from a supported DTCSnapshotRecordNumber.or- sub-function is 0x06 and DTCExtendedDataRecord is different from 0x FF and GEELYGeely Automotive Research Institute(Ningbo)Co.Ltd Document TypeNote-SWRS Document Release StatusRELEASED Document No Revision005 Volume No01 Page No1115(1572) Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU different from a supported DTCExtendedDataRecordNumber. 22 conditionsNotCorrect- DTCMaskRecord = 0xFFFFF and no snapshot data has been stored for any DTC.or- DTCMaskRecord = a supported DTC number and no snapshot data has been stored for this DTC. 78 requestCorrectlyReceived-ResponsePending- Depending on the amount of data in the response NRC 78 will be used to respond within the required response time. 4.5.3.1.2 Diagnostic service requirementsDiagnostic services shall be supported by the ECU as specified in this section. Note that r equirements on diagnostic services are defined for both diagnostic application software (i.e. software that execute services in other sessions than the programmingSession) and bootloader software (i.e. software that execute services in the programmingSession).The diagnostic services required by this document are defined by [Services_9] ISO 14229-1. This section specifies additions and restrictions that are compliant to [Services_9] ISO 14229-1.Additionally requirements on diagnostic services, which are network dependent, are specified in the implementation specification for the respective networks (e.g. internal specifications UDSonCAN, UDSonFR and UDSonIP).The diagnostic services that shall be supported by the ECU in the safetySystemDiagnosticSession are specified by [Services_10] ISO 26021-1 and [Services_11] ISO 26021-2 "End-of-life activation of on-board pyrotechnic devices"The ECU is not allowed to support other diagnostic services without approval from CEVT Electrical Architecture.If the ECU implements safety requirements with an ASIL higher than QM, it shall be ensured that the diagnostic services supported by the ECU in all sessions except in programmingSession cannot violate any of those safety requirements, i.e. to demonstrate independence as required by [Services_12] ISO-26262. Exception to this requirement is allowed only when approved by CEVT Electrical Architecture and will require that the diagnostic services are developed according to [Services_12] ISO-26262 and the allocated ASIL of those safety requirement for which independence cannot be demonstrated4.5.3.1.2.1 Supported servicesDiagnostic services shall be supported by the ECU and enabled in diagnostic sessions according to the tables in the following sub sections.Abbreviations in the table Requirements on diagnostic services that shall be supported by the ECU:MC1= Mandatory if the ECU is not emission related. Mandatory if the ECU is emission related and support “calibration DTCs” (one or more). The emission related ECU shall in this case support the groupOfDTC set to value of a “calibration DTC” that is supported by the ECU. If the ECU is emission related the ECU is allowed to support the groupOfDTC set to value of a non-emission DTCs other than a “calibration DTC”. Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU If the ECU is emission related the ECU is not allowed to support the groupOfDTC set to value of an emission related DTC.A “calibration DTC” is a non-emission related DTC that indicates that a specific action (e.g. request a diagnostic service for initiating or calibrating a function controlled by the ECU) that must be performed as a part of the car manufacturing process has not yet been performed and that shall be cleared (by the diagnostic service ClearDiagnosticInformation with the data parameter groupOfDTC set to a value of the “calibration DTC”) as soon as the action has been completed.MC2= Mandatory if the ECU is emission related. Not allowed if the ECU is not emission related.MC3= Mandatory if the dataRecord consists of more than one parameter (i.e. the dataRecord is packeted or bitmapped). Not allowed if the dataRecord consists of one parameter.MC4= Mandatory if [Services_1] UDS Data specifies that the value of a data record, pointed out by a dataldentifier, shall be possible to write (by diagnostic service specified by this document). Otherwise, the service WriteDataByIdentifier may be supported by the ECU in one, some or all sessions. title: ClearDiagnosticInformation (14)
body: 2534 v1 ClearDiagnosticInformation (14) Version history:(1):Purpose: Erase DTCsSource:Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 76496v0The service ClearDiagnosticInformation shall be supported by the ECU in defaultSession and extendedDiagnosticSession.

title: ClearDiagnosticInformation (14) - groupOfDTCSpecific DTC
body: 2537 v3 ClearDiagnosticInformation (14) - groupOfDTCSpecific DTC Version history:(3):Purpose: It shall be possible to remove specific DTCs.Source:Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 76497v2If the ECU is not emission related, the service ClearDiagnosticInformation with the data parameter groupOfDTC set to a value of any specific DTC shall be supported by the ECU in all sessions where the ECU supports the service ClearDiagnosticInformation.If the ECU is emission related, the service ClearDiagnosticInformation with the data parameter groupOfDTC set to a value of a “calibration DTC” shall be supported by the ECU in all sessions where the ECU supports the service ClearDiagnosticInformation.A “calibration DTC” is a non-emission related DTC that indicates that a specific action (e.g. request a diagnostic service for initiating or calibrating a function controlled by the ECU) that must be performed as a part of the car manufacturing process has not yet been performed and that shall be cleared (by the diagnostic service ClearDiagnosticInformation with the data parameter groupOfDTC set to a value of the “calibration DTC”) as soon as the action has been completed. This requirement is only applicable if the ECU support “calibration DTCs” (one or more).If the ECU is emission related, the service ClearDiagnosticInformation with the data parameter Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU groupOfDTC set to a value a non-emission related DTC, other than a “calibration DTC”, is allowed to be supported by the ECU in all sessions where the ECU supports the service ClearDiagnosticInformation.If the ECU is emission related, the service ClearDiagnosticInformation with the data parameter groupOfDTC set to a value of an emission related DTC is not allowed to be supported by the ECU.

title: ClearDiagnosticInformation (14) - groupOfDTC All DTCs in emission related ECU
body: 2535 v1ClearDiagnosticInformation (14) - groupOfDTC All DTCs in emission related ECU Version history:(1):Purpose: To shorten the time the ECU is in the workshop or during the assembly process, it shall be possible to clear all DTCs in emission related ECUs with one diagnostic request.Source:Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 363603v0If the ECU is emission related, the service ClearDiagnosticInformation with the data parameter groupOfDTC set to the value 0xFFF000 – “All DTCs in emission related ECU” shall be supported by the ECU in all sessions where the ECU supports the service ClearDiagnosticInformation but only for functional addressed diagnostic request messages. An emission related ECU is not allowed to support this for physical addressed diagnostic request messages. Refer to section Diagnostic message addressing for details regarding functional addressed requests. Note that the requirement “The server shall support its list of diagnostic services regardless of addressing mode (physical, functional addressing type)” specified in [Services_9] ISO 14229-1, shall not apply in this case. Note that this data parameter groupOfDTC – “All DTCs in emission related ECU” is not defined in [Services_9] ISO 14229-1.If the ECU is not emission related, the service ClearDiagnosticInformation with the data parameter groupOfDTC set to the value 0xFFF000 – “All DTCs in emission related ECU” is not allowed to be supported by the ECU.

N M N 85 controlMask See note 15 N MC3 N Notes:6. a. From the time the request is received by the ECU until the ECU regains control, the substituted values of the data record (referenced by the dataidentifier) shall remain static. If the substituted values need to change over time, for example due to safety reasons, the service routineControl (0x31) shall be used.b. The service InputOutputControlByIdentifier (0x2F) is the only service intended for temporarily controlling inputs (e.g., real world sensors) and outputs (e.g., real world actuators). Unlike service writeDataByIdentifier (0x2E) and writeMemoryByAddress (0x3D), the values substituted by the service 0x2F shall always be immediately effective and revert back to the normal value (as determined by the control system) when the ECU regains control over the values.7. a. The controlState parameter (of the controlStatusRecord) of the positive response shall always be equal to the size of the dataRecord (referenced by the dataidentifier) and shall represent the actual current value(s) for each parameter within the dataidentifier, independent of the value of the controlMask (i.e., the values that would be returned if the data were to be included in a positive response to a service readDataByIdentifier (0x22) request at that time).14. title: InputOutputControlByIdentifier (2F)
body: 2513 v2 InputOutputControlByIdentifier (2F) Version history:(2):Purpose: By controlling inputs and outputs it is possible to make quick fault tracing methods. For example if there is a problem with an electric window, simulating button presses via InputOutputControlByIdentifier can rule out if the problem is on the button side or if on the electric engine side.Source:Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 76588v1The service InputOutputControlByIdentifier shall be supported by the ECU in extendedDiagnosticSession if [Services_1] UDS Data specifies that the value of a data record, pointed out by a dataldentifier, shall be possible to controllable by the service InputOutputControlByIdentifier. Otherwise the service InputOutputControlByIdentifier may be supported in extendedDiagnosticSession. The service InputOutputControlByIdentifier shall not be supported by the ECU in defaultSession or programmingSession.

body: 2598 v5 RequestTransferExit (37) transferResponseParameterRecord Version history:(5):Purpose: There are two transferResponseParameterRecord alternatives: with/without CRC.An integrity check of the programmed data is performed at the ECU authenticity verification (Check Memory), according to the Software Authentication concept. A checksum calculation is also not suitable when delta encoding is used, as the location and number of transferred data block and written data block might differ. CheckMemory is not implemented.Table - Example 1: RequestTransferExit positive response when CheckMemory is not implemented Tester Description Data Explanation Tx RequestTransferExit (S.F) 01 37 00 00 00 00 00 00 Rx Positive response 03 77 xx xx 00 00 00 00 2-byte CRC 2. CheckMemory is implemented.Table - Example 2: RequestTransferExit positive response when CheckMemory is implemented (i.e. Software Authentication supported) Tester Description Data Explanation Tx RequestTransferExit (S.F) 01 37 00 00 00 00 00 00 Rx Positive response 01 77 00 00 00 00 00 00 CRC omitted

The presence of the parameter depends on the modeOfOperation parameter.4.5.3.1.2.1.7 Additional routine requirementsThe positive response on the service routineControl request, regardless of sub-function, shall have the data parameter RoutineStatusRecord. The first byte of the data parameter RoutineStatusRecord shall be the RoutineInfo byte. The RoutineInfo byte shall consist of two fields where bits 7-4 defines RoutineType (see table RoutineType definition ) and bits 3-0 defines RoutineStatus (see table RoutineStatus definition ).The result of the routine shall (at least) be available, via requestRoutineResults, as long as the diagnostic session is kept or until the routine is re-started.Table: Routine type definition Index Hex Name Definition 1 0 Reserved Reserved by this document 2 1 Type 1- Short routine The routine stops after a certain time when it is completed. The routine is completed before a positive response on startRoutine request is sent.A positive response on startRoutine request shall be sent and only be sent in the following situations :The entry conditions have been fulfilled and the routine has been completed (and stopped).The entry conditions have not been fulfilled.Any of exit conditions have occurred.The sub-function stopRoutine shall not be supported.It is not possible to abort a short routine by diagnostic service during its execution as the positive response on startRoutine request is sent after the routine has been stopped (aborted or completed).The sub-function requestRoutineResults may be supported. 3 2 Type 2- Long routine The routine stops after a certain time when it is completed. The routine may be completed before or after a positive response on startRoutine request is sent.A positive response on startRoutine request shall be sent and only be sent in the following situations:The entry conditions have been fulfilled and the routine has been started or completed (and stopped).The entry conditions have not been fulfilled.Any of exit conditions have occurred.The sub-function stopRoutine shall be supported.It shall be possible to abort a routine during its execution, before it is completed, by stopRoutine requests (after a positive response on startRoutine request has been sent).The sub-function RequestRoutineResults shall be supported.It shall be possible to read the RoutineInfo byte by Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU RequestRoutineResults requests (after a positive response on startRoutine request has been sent) both while the routine executes and after it has been stopped (aborted or completed).Note that the routine type is compliant with the "Method B" specified in [Services_9] ISO 14229-1. 4 3 Type 3 - Continuous routine The routine is stopped by stopRoutine request. The routine don't need a certain time in order to be completed. It is completed when it is stopped by stopRoutine request.A positive response on startRoutine request shall be sent and only be sent in the following situations:The entry conditions have been fulfilled and the routine has started.The entry conditions have not been fulfilled.The sub-function stopRoutine shall be supported.The sub-function RequestRoutineResults shall be supported.It shall be possible to read the RoutineInfo byte by RequestRoutineResults requests both while the routine executes and after it has been stopped (aborted or completed).Note that the routine type is compliant with the "Method A" specified in [Services_9] ISO 14229-1. 5 4-F Reserved Reserved by this document Table: Routine status definition Index Hex Name Definition 1 0 RoutineCompleted The routine completed all requested functionality (successfully or not).The routine results (if any), readable via service routineControl and/or any other service, are valid. 2 1 RoutineAborted The routine aborted before completion of all requested functionality due to any of the following reasons:1. The routine has not started due to the entry conditions are not fulfilled.2. The routine has been aborted due to any of the exit conditions have occurred.3. The routine has been aborted by a stopRoutine request (only applicable for routine type 2). 3 2 RoutineExecutes The routine is under execution and not yet completed (only applicable for routine type 2 and 3). 4 3-F Reserved Reserved by this document

If data that is read by service readDataByIdentifier or readMemoryByAddress is protected by security access, then the service shall be protected by security access when including this same data (completely or partly) in the dynamically defined dataldentifier. Version history:(4): Change the Verification Method from Test to AnalysisPurpose: Standardise the negative response codes that an ECU may send to make it easier to understand why a ECU rejects a diagnostic service request.Source:Verification Method: AnalysisLegacy ID: 74510v2Negative response code other than generalReject (10) and busyRepeatRequest (21) sent by negative responses on diagnostic services requests is allowed as specified by [Services_9] ISO 14229-1 unless otherwise is specified by this document or in the implementation specification for the respective networks (e.g. UDSonCAN, UDSonFR and UDSonIP).4.5.3.1.3 Diagnostic message addressingThe normal vehicle network configuration will be a multi level network, as described in the figure Typical vehicle network topology below , with both public and private ECUs on the different networks. This chapter defines requirements for diagnostic message addressing for all public ECUs on any network. It is however not applicable to ECUs on networks where the network frame ID is less than 16 bits. For further information regarding addressing on networks with a network frame ID less than 16 bits, see the corresponding implementation specification. Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHII Figure - Typical vehicle network topologyA distributed server system shall be used where all public ECUs shall have their own server.To make it possible for the tester to send a specific request to a public ECU on a network in the vehicle, each public ECU needs to have its own unique address. The address will be dependent on which network the ECU is located on and which domain the network belongs to.The logical address range 0x1000 – 0x7FFF (Vehicle manufacturer specific) defined in [Services_13] ISO-13400-2 Road vehicles – Diagnostic Communication over Internet Protocol (DoIP) – Part 2: Network and Transport Layer Requirements and Services, where the range 0x1000 to 0x1FFF is used as addresses for the public ECUs in the platforms using this specification.The logical address range 0x0E80 – 0x0EFF (External vehicle manufacture / aftersales enhanced diagnostic test equipment) defined in [Services_13] ISO-13400-2 Road vehicles – Diagnostic Communication over Internet Protocol (DoIP) – Part 2: Network and Transport Layer Requirements and Services, is used for the external diagnostic tester. Only 0x0E80 can be used, (using another address would affect internal routing tables).4.5.3.1.3.1 Logical address format for diagnostic request and responseThe addressing format used for diagnostic request (target address) and response (source address) is divided into three parts where the combination of Domain ID, Network ID and ECU ID is utilized, see the figure below. This addressing format gives the advantage of less complex gateway implementations. Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU The addressing format supports both physical and functional addressing for request messages.All diagnostic services defined in this document shall be supported for both physical and functional addressing unless otherwise is specified in this document. Bit 12-15 0x1 (VCC address range) Bit 8-11 Domain ID Bit 4-7 Network ID Bit 0-3 ECU ID Figure – addressing formatThe maximum number of ECUs per network range is limited to 15 since the 16'th (bit 0-3 equal to 0xF) is allocated for functional requests. If there is a need to have more than 15 ECUs within a network the network can be extended by assigning two or more logical Network IDs to the same physically network i.e. the ECU's will physically be on the same network but will have different Network IDs.The maximum number of networks per domain is limited to 7 since Networks IDs (0x0 to 0x6) are assigned for communication with external diagnostic tester and Networks IDs (0x7 to 0xD) reserved for future communication with internal diagnostic tester. If there is a need to have more than 7 physical networks within a domain the domain can be extended by assigning two or more logical Domain IDs.

title: Unique ECU address
body: 2336 v1 Unique ECU address Version history:(i):Purpose: Define how the unique ECU ID is decided for each network.Source:Verification Method: AnalysisLegacy ID: 74081v0Of the 16 bits that is used for TA and SA bit 0-3 shall define ECU ID, bit 4-7 shall define Network ID, bit 8-11 shall define Domain ID and bit 12-15 shall define the address range and shall be set to 0x1.4.5.3.1.3.2 Physical logical address rangeEach ECU shall have one vehicle unique physical logical address assigned within the ranges ![](images/41d27ebec35e328ea8484456a0548903584072828c0b3ef8eef2936148f65608.jpg) GEELYGeely Automotive Research Institute(Ningbo)Co.Ltd Document TypeNote-SWRS Document Release StatusRELEASED Document No Revision005 Volume No01 Page No1211(1572) Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU defined by the table below.The system architect defining each ECU physical logical address needs to be aware of the parallel request algorithm which the tester uses to distribute the diagnostic request messages during software download based on the logical address. The ECUs which takes the longest time to re-program shall have the lowest Domain/Network/ECU ID.The system architect must also make sure that a Network ID equal to 0xD is not assigned to a CAN network including emissions related ECUs (this is necessary in order to avoid possible conflicts with request messages sent from an OBD scan tool).The system architect shall check respective transport/network layer specification (e.g. CAN, LIN, IP, FlexRay, MOST150), regarding limitations when assigning a physical address to an ECU. Table - Physical logical address range(msb)Physical logical address range(Isb) Comment Address rangeBit 15-12 Domain IDBit 11-8 Network IDBit 7-4 ECU IDBit 3-0 0x1 0x0 to 0xE 0x0 to 0x6 0x0 to 0xE Reserved for external diagnostic tester communication 0x1 0x0 to 0xE 0x7 to 0xD 0x0 to 0xE Reserved for future internal diagnostic tester communication

Document Name Base Tech SWRS DHU 4.5.3.1.3.3 Functional logical address range It shall be possible via a functional logical address, to send a request to all (public) ECUs in the complete vehicle. However, in programmingSession there may be ECUs on a specific network not supporting functional addressed requests where a response is expected. .Refer to the implementation specification for respective network (e.g. UDSonLIN) for more information. A functional request message must be unsegmented on all networks, i.e. the tester shall only send functional request messages that can be transported in a single frame on all networks (with public ECUs) in the vehicle. E.g., for a LIN network the largest functional request message is 6 bytes (payload data). The ECU shall support the functional address specified in the table below. Table - Functional logical address range (msb) Functional logical address range (lsb) Comment address range Bit 15 - 12 Domain ID Bit 11 - 8 Network ID Bit 7 - 4 ECU ID Bit 3 - 0 0x1 0xF 0xF 0xF All ECUs on all networks within all domains are functionally addressed

title: Session Layer
body: 2613 v4 Session Layer Version history:(4): Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU Purpose: Standardise communication to ensure all ECUs uses the same diagnostic communication specifications. ISO standard shall be followed to reduce cost and make implementation easierSource: Road vehicles - Unified diagnostic services - Part 2: Session layer servicesVerification Method: InspectionLegacy ID: 113482v3The session layer defined in [Session_3] Road vehicles — Unified diagnostic services — Part 2: Session layer services shall be implemented with restriction/additions defined by the requirements in this specification.4.5.4.2 UDS Session ECU reqs4.5.4.2.1 Appendix4.5.4.2.1.1 Example, queuing of requests in a serverThe sequence below shows examples where multiple requests are sent to a server, a typical case is in programming session where the client will send additional request to be queued in the server. The requests are typically TransferData with Block 1, 2, 3 and so on where the data is known in advance and do not depend on any data received in a previous response. ![](images/c82afb11197719488e36c9a51a9f4eb4268ce181bfb4b44c8dc54a626be3ef4c.jpg) GEELYGeely Automotive Research Institute(Ningbo)Co.Ltd Document TypeNote-SWRS Document Release StatusRELEASED Document No Revision005 Volume No01 Page No1226(1572) Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU C ClientorGateway Server FirstRequest FirstFrameFlowControl(CTS) Processing first request ConsecutiveFrame ConsecutiveFrame ConsecutiveFrame FirstFrame SecondRequest Queuingof onerequest FlowControl(CTS) Processing second request ConsecutiveFrame ConsecutiveFrame ConsecutiveFrame Final Response (1) FirstFrame ThirdRequest Queuingof onerequest FlowControl(CTS) Processing third request ConsecutiveFrame ConsecutiveFrame ConsecutiveFrame Final Response (2) Final Response (3) GEELYGeely Automotive Research Institute(Ningbo)Co.Ltd Document TypeNote-SWRS Document Release StatusRELEASED Document No Revision005 Volume No01 Page No1227(1572) Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU to determine by observing network communication between a request that has been processed completely inside a server but not yet responded to and a request that has not yet been processed completely by a server, the observable network communication will be used to judge if a specific sequence is queued requests or full duplex communication.The sequences shows examples where multiple requests are sent to a server, a typical case in programming session where the client will send additional request to be queued in the server. If gateways are located between client and server, due to delays in gateways, the second request (believed by client to be queued in vehicle) may arrive to the server slightly differently now and then in time relation to the server responses. The server may already have started responding to a previous request. In that case the second request is not considered to be queued, as perceived by server, but is instead only full duplex communication. ![](images/f11c524b32630123e927d7aae7c713de61a6e9b1fbf3849fd035077d78c114d3.jpg) GEELYGeely Automotive Research Institute(Ningbo)Co.Ltd Document TypeNote-SWRS Document Release StatusRELEASED Document No Revision005 Volume No01 Page No1228(1572) Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU In sequence to right the server has begun the response by a First Frame (processing of request is completed but response not yet completely sent) when a second request is received. Since the (segmented) response is in progress, and a new request is received within the response transmission it is full duplex instead of queued request. GEELYGeely Automotive Research Institute(Ningbo)Co.Ltd Document TypeNote-SWRS Document Release StatusRELEASED Document No Revision005 Volume No01 Page No1229(1572) Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU services, section “Timing handling during communication” with the restrictions/additions as defined by the subsequent sub-sections.4.5.4.2.2.1 Queued request messages to one serverMessages sent in-between the client and the server may pass several gateways which results in greater latency, compared to if the client was directly connected to same network as the server. To make the client server communication faster, a feature is introduced named “queued request”. The method used is to send an extra request directly after sending the first request (i.e. receiving the response of the first request). The time saved by using queued request is the response time up to the client + client processing the response and then send a new request + the time for the second request to be sent from the client to the server through all gateways.A LIN slave shall not implement support for queued request. The LIN network/transport layer standard is not allowing this feature. The LIN master is therefore required to buffer the second (queued) request.

title: Server support of queued requests in programming session
body: 2618 v4 Server support of queued requests in programming session Version history:(4):Purpose: To reduce the (delta)P2Request time.Source:Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 56192v3In programming session the server shall be able to handle the minimum of one (1) queued physical request during processing of an already received physical request which do not lead to a server reset , meaning the server shall store the second request in a FIFO queue for later processing.If the server isn’t able to receive the complete second message due to lack of receive buffer space the server shall halt the message with the help of the network/transport layer e.g. WAIT on CAN/FlexRay or window size on TCP. Messages that can be fully received in addition to the minimum one queued request shall be stored in queue. If the queue is full, any further requests shall be ignored.

If implemented it will not be verified and shall not be expected to be supported by tools. Missing frame master The missing frame master for a network is the ECU which is connected to a higher hierarchical network and act as a gateway for diagnostic request messages from the higher hierarchical network to the ECUs on the network. See General diagnostic guideline. Missing frame slave All ECUs, except the missing frame master, on a network. See Missing frame guideline requisite documents. Network configuration master The ECU that is responsibly for the network configuration. Private ECU An ECU not addressable from a client/tester point of view.Note:An ECU can partly be public and partly private i.e. some diagnostic services and diagnostic data supported by the ECU are addressable and some are not. Public ECU An ECU addressable from a client/tester point of view. Public ECU Master A public ECU responsible to act as a diagnostic server for one or more private ECUs. Tester A system that controls functions such as test, inspection, monitoring, Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU or diagnosis of an on-vehicle electronic control unit and may be dedicated to a specific type of operators (e.g. a scan tool dedicated to garage mechanics or a test tool dedicated to assembly plant agents).The tester is also referenced as the client. TRC The Test Run Criteria defines the criteria that must be met for the DTC test to run, i.e. for the DTC test fault detection logic to execute and the DTC fault detection counter to be up-dated.SeeUDSServicesrequisite documents for further detailed explanation. Abbreviation Description CAN Controller Area Network DTC Diagnostic Trouble Code ECU Electronic Control Unit MFCS Missing frame Counter Signal. 1 byte counter sent by the missing frame master which all missing frame slaves shall use to ensure that the missing frame slave has continuous network access. TRC Test Run Criteria UDS Unified Diagnostic Services 4.5.5.1.4.3 OverviewThis document specifies the CAN specific diagnostic requirements that shall apply to a CAN based ECU. All diagnostic messages on CAN shall be sent and received according to this and referenced documents in section Requisite documents .Additional requirements are added if the ECU shall act as a diagnostic gateway to a sub network which is defined in the [UDSonCAN_6] Diagnostic And Bootloader Gateway Specification.Depending on configuration, this document may consist in different combinations of the following sections:- Generic CAN ECU (Applicable to all diagnosable and/or programmable CAN ECUs)- Public CAN ECU (Applicable to all CAN ECUs supporting a total diagnostic implementation)- Private Programmable CAN ECU (Applicable for CAN ECUs with "limited" diagnostic implementation)For those ECUs who implements a "limited" diagnostic functionality to support software download the Public ECU master is responsible on the private programmable CAN ECU behalf to response on DTCs etc.NoteThis document covers both the older CAN standard, referred to as classic CAN, and the updated standard CAN Flexible Data-Rate, referred to as CAN FD. Unless explicitly specifying the standard of CAN in this document, any reference to CAN refers to both the classic CAN and CAN FD standards. All parameters used as test run criteria for missing frame tests shall be received outside the network that is being tested.4. The testing for missing frames shall only be done when the frame is expected; for example missing frame master shall be configured such that it is aware if an optional missing frame slave is present (mounted or not) on the bus or not.5. The missing frame master shall be aware of different operation modes preventing the missing frame slaves to send frames. For example if a missing frame slave is in power-off, low-power, sleep or equivalent mode, the missing frame slave might be prevented from sending frames. The missing frame master shall be aware when the missing frame slave is prevented from sending frames and shall not set any missing frame DTCs during this these modes.6. Missing frame tests shall only be done when the ECU is the usage mode "Driving".7. Missing frame tests shall never be done during combustion engine crank.8. The missing frame master shall never set TRC true until 5±2 seconds after all criteria for a DTC test, for permanent and intermittent missing frame DTCs, to run, is satisfied. This inhibit time period include the same inhibit time period, that starts after transition from one usage to another or one car mode to another, specified as Generic Test Run Criteria in [UDSonCAN_2] UDS Data (i.e. no additional time period is needed).9. The voltage of the vehicle battery, Ubat, shall be within: 10,0 ≤ Ubat ≤ 15,4V. Note: The battery voltage shall be measured as close to the battery as possible in order to minimize the measuring fault.10. If a missing frame master does not receive the missing frame TRC no missing frame DTCs shall be set.11. Missing frame tests shall never be done when fault is detected on the parameters used as test run criteria (e.g., when the value of parameters, used as test run criteria, distributed on an in-vehicle network is not updated (indicated by an update bit) or not correct (indicated by a quality factor)).3. Each missing frame slave shall periodically send at least one frame with a shorter periodicity than 100 ms. To save bandwidth on the CAN net, first check if there is an existing frame the missing frame master can perform the DTC test on. Secondly the send frequency of an existing frame shall be increased to match the 100 ms requirement. The missing frame master shall check permanent missing frame DTCs every 150ms-170ms.4.
