body: 2768 v2Permanent missing frame _ Test period missing frame slave Version history:(2): Purpose: A standardized test period should be used for testing the DTC so the behavior is as similar as possible between the ECUs.Source: Table: "Summary of CAN related external circuit faults" Item 3Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 55861v1 Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU Each missing frame slave shall periodically send at least one frame with a shorter periodicity than 100 ms. To save bandwidth on the CAN net, first check if there is an existing frame the gateway can perform the DTC test on. Secondly the send frequency of an existing frame shall be increased to match the 100 ms requirement.

title: Permanent missing frame _ Test period missing frame master frame reception
body: 2767 v2 Permanent missing frame _ Test period missing frame master frame reception Version history:(2):Purpose: Missing frame master shall base its permanent missing frame DTC detection on a signal frame reception timeout.Source: Table: "Summary of CAN related external circuit faults" Item 3Verification Method: AnalysisLegacy ID: 55881v1The missing frame master shall be configured to receive the periodically transmitted frame from each missing frame slave within the supervised network.

title: Permanent missing frame _ Test period missing frame master
body: 2776 v2 Permanent missing frame _ Test period missing frame master Version history:(2):Purpose: Define how long time the missing frame master shall wait for each frame.Source: Table: "Summary of CAN related external circuit faults" Item 3Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 55883v1The missing frame master shall check permanent missing frame DTCs every 150ms-170ms.

title: Permanent missing frame _ TRC 1
body: 2764 v4 Permanent missing frame _ TRC 1 Version history:(4):Purpose: Only one ECU shall administer missing frame TRC to be sure the same TRC are used for all ECUs in the network.Source: Table: "Summary of CAN related external circuit faults" Item 3 and 4;Verification Method: AnalysisLegacy ID: 55885v3The missing frame master, and not the missing frame slaves, shall manage all the enabling and disable conditions (i.e. set TRC to true or false) for the missing frame DTCs, both for permanent and intermittent missing frame.

title: Permanent missing frame _ TRC 2
body: 2765 v7 Permanent missing frame _ TRC 2 Version history:(7):Purpose: Missing frame DTCs shall be set in a predictable fashion (i.e. not allowed Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU using event based frames for missing frames monitoring).Source: Table: "Summary of CAN related external circuit faults" Item 3 and 4Verification Method: AnalysisLegacy ID: 55888v6The missing frame detection shall only be based on periodic frames sent in at least the usage mode "Driving".

title: Permanent missing frame _ TRC 3
body: 2780 v3 Permanent missing frame _ TRC 3 Version history:(3):Purpose: If these parameters are sent from a missing frame slave within the network being supervised, the TRC would not be possible to obtain by the missing frame master during an error situation.Source: Table: "Summary of CAN related external circuit faults" Item 7.3 and 7.4Verification Method: AnalysisLegacy ID: 55891v2All parameters used as test run criteria for missing frame tests shall be received outside the network that is being tested.

title: Permanent missing frame _ TRC 4
body: 2781 v3 Permanent missing frame _ TRC 4 Version history:(3):Purpose: It must be possible to have different network configurations in regards of mounted ECUs on a network, without the missing frame master reporting missing slaves.Source: Table: "Summary of CAN related external circuit faults" Item 3 and 4Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 55921v2The testing for missing frames shall only be done when the frame is expected; i.e. missing frame master shall be configured such that it is aware if an optional missing frame slave is present (mounted or not) on the bus or not.

title: Permanent missing frame _ TRC 5
body: 2782 v4 Permanent missing frame _ TRC 5 Version history:(4):Purpose: Prevent setting missing frame DTC due to the mode the ECU currently has, prevents the ECU from sending the frame.Source: Table: "Summary of CAN related external circuit faults" Item 3 and 4;Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 55922v3The missing frame master shall be aware of different operation modes preventing the missing frame slaves to send frames. For example if a missing frame slave is in power-off, low-power, Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU sleep or equivalent mode, the missing frame slave might be prevented from sending frames.The missing frame master shall be aware when the missing frame slave is prevented from sending frames and shall not set any missing frame DTCs during this these modes.

title: Permanent missing frame _ TRC 6
body: 2783 v5 Permanent missing frame _ TRC 6 Version history:(5):Purpose: Missing frames shall only be tested during usage modes when all ECUs are expected to be active.Source: Table: "Summary of CAN related external circuit faults" Item 3 and 4Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 55925v4Missing frame tests shall only be done when the ECU is the usage mode "Driving"

title: Permanent missing frame _ TRC 7
body: 2784 v4 Permanent missing frame _ TRC 7 Version history:(4):Purpose: Missing frames shall only be tested during usage modes when all ECUs are expected to be active and non-transient operation mode.Source: Table: "Summary of CAN related external circuit faults" Item 3 and 4Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 55927v3Missing frame tests shall never be done during combustion engine crank.

title: Permanent missing frame _ TRC 8
body: 2785 v5 Permanent missing frame _ TRC 8 Version history:(5):Purpose: To ensure missing frame DTCs are not falsely set due to differences in ECU power-up times, missing frames shall only be tested during non-transient conditions.Source: Table: "Summary of CAN related external circuit faults" Item 3 and 4Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 55930v4The missing frame master shall never set TRC true until 5±2 seconds after all criteria for a DTC test, for permanent and intermittent missing frame DTCs, to run, is satisfied. This inhibit time period include the inhibit time period, that starts after transition from one usage to another or one car mode to another, specified as Generic Test Run Criteria in [UDSonCAN_2] UDS Data (i.e. no additional time period is needed).

title: Permanent missing frame _ TRC 9
body: 2786 v3 Permanent missing frame _ TRC 9 Version history:(3): Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU Purpose: Missing frames shall only be tested within the battery voltage when communication networks shall be active.Source: Table: "Summary of CAN related external circuit faults" Item 7.3 and 7.4Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 55932v2The voltage of the vehicle battery Ubat, shall be within: 10,0 ≤ Ubat ≤ 15,4V.Note: The battery voltage shall be measured as close to the battery as possible in order to minimize the measuring fault.

title: Permanent missing frame _ TRC 10
body: 2778 v3 Permanent missing frame _ TRC 10 Version history:(3):Purpose: Prevent setting fault DTCs, due to vehicle not being in a normal state.Source: Table: "Summary of CAN related external circuit faults" Item 3 and 4Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 55934v2If a missing frame master does not receive the missing frame TRC no missing frame DTCs shall be set.

title: Permanent missing frame _ TRC 11
body: 2779 v2 Permanent missing frame _ TRC 11 Version history:(2):Purpose: Prevent setting fault DTCs, due to vehicle not being in a normal state.Source: Table: "Summary of CAN related external circuit faults" Item 3 and 4Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 398851v1Missing frame tests shall never be done when fault is detected on the parameters used as test run criteria (e.g., when the value of parameters, used as test run criteria, distributed on an in-vehicle network is not updated (indicated by an update bit) or not correct (indicated by a quality factor)).

title: Permanent missing frame _ Failure type
body: 2773 v2 Permanent missing frame _ Failure type Version history:(2):Purpose: The OEM shall define which failure type that shall be used to minimize the differences in between different ECUs, so that administration is kept to a minimum.Source: Table: "Summary of CAN related external circuit faults" Item 3Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 55935v1For permanent missing frame DTCs the failure type 0x00 shall be used. Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU

title: Permanent missing frame _ DTC ID
body: 2770 v2 Permanent missing frame _ DTC ID Version history:(2):Purpose: The OEM shall define which DTC ID to use to minimize differences in between different ECUs, so that administration is kept to a minimum.Source: Table: "Summary of CAN related external circuit faults" Item 3Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 55936v1The permanent missing frame DTC ID shall be as defined in [UDSonCAN_10] Global Master Reference Database.

title: Permanent missing frame _ Test sample failed criteria
body: 2777 v2 Permanent missing frame _ Test sample failed criteria Version history:(2):Purpose: The missing frame master shall be able to detect when the missing frame slaves fails to send their respective periodic frame.Source: Table: "Calibration of CAN DTCs" Item 3Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 55937v1The reported value of the DTC fault detection counter, for a specific ECU, shall increase when the missing frame master have not received the periodic missing frame slave frame, for that specific ECU, in the test period time.

title: Permanent missing frame _ Increase FDC10 steps
body: 2775 v2 Permanent missing frame _ Increase FDC10 steps Version history:(2):Purpose: Permanent missing frame DTCs shall be set with filtering to be sure the validity of the DTC. However the DTC must be set within 3 seconds to not have a gap in between permanent and intermittent missing frame detection.Source: Table: "Calibration of CAN DTCs" Item 3Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 55938v1The missing frame permanent FDC shall be increased by 9 at every test sample failed.

title: Permanent missing frame _ Test sample passed criteria
body: 2788 v2 Permanent missing frame _ Test sample passed criteria Version history:(2):Purpose: The missing frame master shall be able to detect when the missing frame slaves succeeds in sending their respective periodic frame.Source: Table: "Calibration of CAN DTCs" Item 3Verification Method: Test Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU Legacy ID: 55939v1The reported value of the DTC fault detection counter, for a specific ECU, shall decrease when the missing frame master have received the periodic missing frame slave frame, for that specific ECU, in the test period time.

title: Permanent missing frame _ Decrease FDC10 steps
body: 2769 v2 Permanent missing frame _ Decrease FDC10 steps Version history:(2):Purpose: Permanent missing frame DTCs shall be set with filtering to be sure the validity of the DTC.Source: Table: "Calibration of CAN DTCs" Item 3Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 55940v1The permanent missing frame FDC10 shall be decreased by 9 at every test sample passed.

title: Permanent missing frame _ UnconfirmedDTCLimit
body: 2787 v2 Permanent missing frame _ UnconfirmedDTCLimit Version history:(2):Purpose: Due to the seriousness of the error when an ECU is unresponsive, it is good to see shorter occurrences of when ECUs fails to send frames.Source: Table: "Calibration of CAN DTCs" Item 3Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 55942v1The permanent missing frame DTC test shall use UnconfirmedDTCLimit = 18.

title: Permanent missing frame _ FDC10 max value
body: 2774 v2 Permanent missing frame _ FDC10 max value Version history:(2):Purpose: If a permanent missing frame occurs it is assumed it has big impact on the functionality of the system and hence it shall be able to set the confirm bit.Source: Table 3 item 3Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 152142v1The DTC test for permanent missing frame shall have FDC10 max value = 127

title: Permanent missing frame _ DTCConfirmedLimit
body: 2772 v3 Permanent missing frame _ DTCConfirmedLimit Version history:(3):Purpose: Permanent missing frame DTCs shall be set with filtering to be sure the validity of the DTC.Source: Table: "Calibration of CAN DTCs" Item 3 Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 55944v2The permanent missing frame DTC shall use DTCCConfirmedLimit = 3.

title: Permanent missing frame _ DTCAgedLimit
body: 2771 v2 Permanent missing frame _ DTCAgedLimit Version history:(2):Purpose: Due to the seriousness of the DTC.Source: Table: "Calibration of CAN DTCs" Item 3Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 55945v1The permanent missing frame DTC shall use DTCAgedLimit = 255.4.5.6 UDSonFR4.5.6.1 UDSonFR - Slave Frame Miss4.5.6.1.1 Unified diagnostic services implementation4.5.6.1.1.1 Diagnostic trouble code information

title: Application layer
body: 2987 v2 Application layer Version history:(2):Purpose: To define the application layer used for communicating on IP based networks.Source:Verification Method: AnalysisLegacy ID: 60615v1The application layer shall be compliant with [UDSonIP_14] ISO 14229-5: Road vehicles —Unified diagnostic services (UDS) — Part 5: Unified diagnostic services on Internet Protocol implementation (UDSonIP).4.5.7.1.2 Unified diagnostic service implementationThis section specifies the diagnostic services and data required for an IP ECU.4.5.7.1.2.1 Diagnostic servicesThe required diagnostic service are defined in [UDSonIP_1] UDS Services with the restrictions and additions in subsequent subsections.The services and data (defined in [UDSonIP_1] UDS Services and [UDSonIP_2] UDS Data) sent on IP between tester and Edge node are encapsulated by the Diagnostic Message defined in [UDSonIP_4] DoIP.A TCP connection is used for in vehicle communication and for external communication with vehicle as well as between a stand alone ECU and tester. When a reset occurs the TCP connection is lost and needs to be established again after the reset. The only time it is ok for an ECU to do a reset is when tester sends ECUReset or whenDiagnosticSessionControl(programmingSession) is received.4.5.7.1.2.1.1 ReadDataByPeriodicIdentifierReadDataByPeriodicIdentifier is sent on TCP as well as all other services. The Response Message Type for this service shall be of type#2 format.

title: ReadDataByPeriodicIdentifiers Response Message Type

title: Ethernet Error Message Counter data record
body: 2991 v2 Ethernet Error Message Counter data record Version history:(2):Purpose: To support test and verification during developmentSource:Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 435949v1A data record with identifier 0xD240 shall be implemented exactly as defined in [UDSonIP_12] Global Master Reference Database. The 4 byte counter shall stop counting when it has reached its maximum value, i.e. it shall not act as a rolling counter.Read access: It shall be possible to read the data record 0xD240 by using services specified in [UDSonIP_1] UDS Services in all diagnostic sessions in which the service used for read the data record is supported, except programming session.

title: Ethernet Error Message Counter History data record
body: 2992 v2 Ethernet Error Message Counter History data record Version history:(2):Purpose: To enable evaluation and statistic of error message on Ethernet.Source:Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 435939v1A data record with identifier 0xD230 shall be implemented exactly as defined in [UDSonIP_12] Global Master Reference Database. The data record shall consist of the ten latest driving cycles where error messages on the Ethernet link occurred. Each error message event shall consist of a 4 byte counter value and a timestamp.The 4 byte counter shall stop counting when it has reached its maximum value, i.e. it shall not act as a rolling counter.The timestamp shall be the global real time value defined in [UDSonIP_2] UDS Data.Read access: It shall be possible to read the data record 0xD230 by using services specified in [UDSonIP_1] UDS Services in all diagnostic sessions in which the service used for read the data record is supported, except programming session.

title: Diagnostic routing or switching
body: 2989 v2 Diagnostic routing or switching Version history:(2):Purpose: To define how to gateway signals from one IP based network to another.Source: Section "Overview", IP Routing SpecificationVerification Method: AnalysisLegacy ID: 60592v1ECUs that shall route or switch diagnostic messages shall support applicable parts of routing or switching in accordance to IP Routing Specification, UDSonIP, Requisite documents.4.5.7.2 UDSonIP - IP Router Switch ECU reqs4.5.7.2.1 Detection of no Ethernet link to ECUThe IP Router/switch ECU shall discover when there is no Ethernet link to the IP ECU. This is done by polling if Link is up or down in control register. The polling shall be performed periodically when the IP ECU's conditions for communicating as well as the conditions for performing diagnostics are met.

title: IP Router Switch ECU - Ethernet link_Increase FDC steps
body: 3011 v1IP Router Switch ECU - Ethernet link_Increase FDC steps Version history:(1): Purpose: Each time the Ethernet link is not detected, the ECU shall consider the DTC as set.Source: Section "Diagnostic trouble code information", table "Calibrations of Ethernet DTCs", item 1Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 338291v0The Ethernet link FDC shall be increased by 10 at every test sample fails.

Document Name Base Tech SWRS DHU Item Detected fault Test Period Time Test Run Criteria (TRC) Failure type (hex) DTC ID M/O 1 Faulty transmitted data. Data sent by the LIN master (either header or response from LIN master) is faulty. The DTC fault detection counter counts up when data read back does not match data sent. The DTC fault detection counts down when data read back matches data sent. Every sent LIN frame 86 Defined in Global Master Reference Database. M 2 Faulty LIN response LIN frame checksum error. The DTC fault detection counter counts up when a checksum in one LIN frame from one LIN slave differs from expected value. The DTC fault detection counter counts down when any LIN frame with correct checksum from a specific LIN slave is received. Every received LIN frame 83 Defined in Global Master Reference Database. M 3 Missing LIN response No response (i.e. no bytes received at all) when the master expects to receive a LIN frame response. The DTC fault detection counter counts up when no response is received from a LIN slave. The DTC fault detection counter counts down when a response is received from a LIN slave. Every expected LIN response except frame identifier 0x3D triggered responses 87 Defined in Global Master Reference Database. M 4 Faulty LIN physical bus. LIN physical bus short to ground or battery voltage. The DTC fault detection counter counts up when LIN physical bus short to ground or battery voltage is detected (e.g. when master fail to detect the synchronisation break or the start-bit of the synchronisation/identifier field). The DTC fault detection counts down when not LIN physical bus short to ground or battery voltage is detected (e.g. when master succeeds to detect the synchronisation break or the start-bit of the synchronisation/identifier field). Every sent LIN frame 01 Defined in Global Master Reference Database. M 5 Other LIN network faults. Other faults identified by the implementer. Cold Start The start-up of the ECU from a powered-down or off state. Compatible check Check that all data files fit together and the ECU is capable to starts its normal application functionality. Complete check Check that every individual data file is present, this can be done that each file has a signature placed in the beginning and end of each file that are checked. Tester A system that controls functions such as test, inspection, monitoring, or diagnosis of an on-vehicle electronic control unit and may be dedicated to a specific type of operators (e.g. a scan tool dedicated to garage mechanics or a test tool dedicated to assembly plant agents). The tester is also referenced as the client. Final response Positive or a negative response other than response code 0x78"requestCorrectlyReceived-ResponsePending" Program mode The ECU executing the primary or secondary bootloader Public ECU An ECU addressable from a client/tester point of view. Private ECU An ECU not addressable from a client/tester point of view. Warm start The start-up of the ECU initiated by the application. Abbr. Description CRC Cyclic Redundancy Check ECU Electronic Control Unit HW Hardware NRC Negative Response Code PBL Primary Bootloader SBL Secondary Bootloader SPRMIB SuppressPositiveResponseMessageIndicationBit SW Software SWDL Software Download UDS Unified Diagnostic Services GEELYGeely Automotive Research Institute(Ningbo)Co.Ltd Document TypeNote-SWRS Document Release StatusRELEASED Document No Revision005 Volume No01 Page No1328(1572) Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU 4.6.1.1.2 Requisite documentsThe following documents are either referenced by this specification, or contain information that is relevant to this specification. Reference Source Document [SWDL_1] Internal VBF (Versatile Binary Format) [SWDL_2] Internal VSF (Volvo Cars Software Format) [SWDL_3] Internal Data Compression and Encryption [SWDL_4] Internal Delta encoding [SWDL_5] Internal UDS Services [SWDL_6] Internal UDS Data [SWDL_7] Internal UDS Session [SWDL_8] Internal Diagnostic and Bootloader Gateway [SWDL_9] Internal Software Authentication [SWDL_10] Internal General Software Authentication [SWDL_11] ISO ISO14229-1: Road vehicles — Unified diagnostic services (UDS) — Part 1: Specification and requirements.Revision as stated in [SWDL_6] UDS Data. Note:Internal references is typically found as a separate chapter in the ECU specific Base Technology SWRS.Information obtaining ISO documents may be found on the internet: www.iso.org4.6.1.1.2.1 Referenced document, structure and relationsThe Software Download concept includes a list of specifications that has a tight relation to each other, the Figure "SWDL specification structure", shows the overview and their relation to the ISO documents which is the base.All listed documents are not applicable for each and every ECU. Which specifications that are applicable depends of type of data link, whether the ECU is a gateway or not etc. It is each SW-responsible to request the applicable requirements to each ECU supplier. Note that the specific data link, network and transport protocol specifications not are referenced from this document. Figure - SWDL specification structure 1 - The "VBF (Versatile Binary Format)" data file format is supporting ECUs with addressed based memory data storage. 2 - The "VSF (Volvo Cars Software Format)" data file format is supporting ECUs with both file system and/or memory addressed based data storage. 3 - The "Data Compression and Encryption" specifies how data stored in the data file shall be compressed and how the data shall be decompressed by the ECU. The specification includes a reference implementation of the two algorithms. 4 - The "Software Authentication" is defining a method to protect that the data file origins from a legitimated source. 5 - The "General Software Download", is the top document for the software download concept. It describes the background and the non-network dependent requirements for a bootloader as well as the programming sequences used for software download. GEELYGeely Automotive Research Institute(Ningbo)Co.Ltd Document TypeNote-SWRS Document Release StatusRELEASED Document No Revision005 Volume No01 Page No1330(1572) Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU 6 - The "UDS Services" specifies which diagnostic services that is applicable for the bootloader(programmingSession).7 - The "UDS Data" specifies the data used by each diagnostic service that is applicable for thebootloader (programmingSession).8 - The "UDS Session" specifies the requirements for the session layer.9 - The "Diagnostic and Bootloader Gateway" specifies the gateway requirements for thoseECUs that act as a diagnostic gateway.10 - The "General Software Authentication" specifies the Software Authentication concepts, i.e методs used to ensure that the software is authentic.11 - The "Delta Encoding" specifies the requirements to enable delta encoding as compressionmethod for data files.4.6.1.1.3 OverviewSoftware Download involves the transfer of information from a tester to an ECU using datastored in a file. The data transferred may contain configuration or calibration data for the ECUor completely new software. It also includes uploading of data from the ECU to the tester fordebugging.The Software Download concept provides a means for a tester to send multiple bytes of data toan ECU.4.6.1.1.4 What is the purpose of this documentThis specification is the top document of the SoftWare DownLoad (SWDL) concept. Thespecification describes the background and the non-data link dependent requirements for abootloader as well as the programming sequences used for software download. For details onspecific protocols, data links, components and algorithms, please read the respectivelydocuments.This specification is intended to provide guidance and requirements to architects, systemdesigners, application developers, and ECU suppliers. Adherence to the specificationscontained within this document is required to ensure compatibility within the corporate productline from vehicle to vehicle, model year to model year and maintain compatibility with theindustry driven standards.Important to understand is that this specification only specifies the general non network specificrequirements for a bootloader.4.6.1.1.5 IntroductionElectronic Control Units (ECUs) have demonstrated continued increase in feature, count,memory size, I/O circuit count, and part number complexity. All areas of the vehicleelectrical/electronic system are affected. Electronic Control Units are experiencing late andfrequent changes many of which affect software. These trends will undoubtedly continue intothe foreseeable future.There is a need to reduce vehicle build and service complexity, reduce ECU suppliercomplexity, and allow for maximum flexibility in software design by establishing designs andprocedures providing the ability to configure and program ECUs in assembly and in service.Configuration and module programming will allow module design and release activities tominimize part complexity, economies of scale and allow bookshelf software to be utilized. Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU By having software download possibility in all ECUs with complex functionality the cost of correcting software errors is significantly reduced and new functions can be added after production. The software download functionality is used both in the production line to customize the hardware for the specific car and in workshops to correct errors or improve functions. The software download concept is based on a primary bootloader that is fixed in the ECU and always executed at power on before the application is started and a secondary bootloader, including non-volatile memory programming routines that is downloaded before downloading the rest of the applications and configuration files.Important is to reduce the download time as much as possible to enable a convenient user experience and reduced assembly and workshop time/cost spent on the programming phase. Important technologies such as compression and delta encoding of data reduce the software size as well as using available bandwidth by parallel download of multiple ECUs is therefore motivated.4.6.1.2 General Bootloader requirements4.6.1.2.1 Validation of ECU software(s) - Complete and CompatibleThe bootloader shall at every start (initiation phase) and upon request from the diagnostic tester (routineldentifier(Check Complete & Compatible), check if the ECU software(s) is complete and compatible before starting execution of the application.The purpose of the "Complete & Compatible Check" is to ensure that the expected software parts are programmed successfully and are valid (complete), e.g. to detect if any part of the software is missing, broken (partly present/downloaded) or has been altered. This check shall also decide whether the combination of stored software parts are compatible to each other. The compatible check can be done in many different ways and will be different from case to case. It is either exclusively handled by the bootloader or by using a call-out to a function block that is part of the application. The compatibility check is only performed once the complete check has passed successfully.The Complete & Compatible check shall be implemented in such a way that it must not be updated for each new or modified data file. ![](images/9ebcfe15a0e599e0dca2a23c00bac5d8e5c9215de6dacc7c729e30f522c83551.jpg) GEELYGeely Automotive Research Institute(Ningbo)Co.Ltd Document TypeNote-SWRS Document Release StatusRELEASED Document No Revision005 Volume No01 Page No1333(1572) Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU Legacy ID: 53935v1The bootloader shall at every start check if the ECU software(s) is complete and compatible before starting execution of the application.

If the ECU contains incomplete software(s) it shall not check whether the software(s) is compatible. Hence, the ECU cannot indicate that both the complete and compatible check has failed. Used defined SW parts(s) 3 Return result. If any SW part(s) is incomplete the Complete & Compatible function shall indicate that in the response 4 If all SW part(s) are complete 5 The Complete & Compatible function checks if stored SW parts(s) iscompatible, using the same order as defined in step 2 but ESS is optional. 6 Return result Figure - CompleteCompatibleFunction() sequence diagram4.6.1.2.1.1 Complete and Compatible - Complete check

title: Complete and Compatible - Complete function

title: Complete&Compatible - Definition of being Compatible
body: 3181 v4 Complete&Compatible - Definition of being Compatible Version history:(4):Purpose: The purpose with the compatibility validation is to detect if present softwares are compatible in such way that the ECU is able to start and communicate.Hence, the ECU application could inform the user by e.g. setting a diagnostic trouble code.Source:Verification Method:Legacy ID: 401140v3The ECU is compatible if it is at least able to start the application, is able to respond to diagnostics and alert the user if a function is disabled or degraded. Please pay attention to e.g. post-build (e.g. reconfiguration of the communication matrix by moving an existing signal) consistency check requirements, which might require information about the application build process.Note 2: See also "Appendix: Section Examples of different compatible functions". title: CompleteCompatibleFunction()
