title: Maximum time to perform the Complete&Compatible validation
body: 3187 v4 Maximum time to perform the Complete&Compatible validation Version history:(4):Purpose: To define the maximum time to perform the Complete & Compatible validation of ECU software(s), to fulfill the ECU start-up timing requirement.Source:Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 53970v3The maximum time to perform the total Complete & Compatible sequence described in Figure - CompleteCompatibleFunction() shall not exceed 20ms.

title: CompleteCompatibleFunction - error handling
body: 3184 v2 CompleteCompatibleFunction - error handling Version history:(2):Purpose: Define a error handling strategy, where a restricted approach is applied meaning that the application must not be started unless it is proven to be valid.Source:Verification Method: InspectionLegacy ID: 405051v1In case of an unexpected fault during the CompleteCompatibleFunction() that prevents the function to be completed and the root cause cannot be derived to a specific software part, the ECU shall be considered as not complete (or not compatible respectively, dependent of the check that was not completed). This shall be indicated in the response to the routineldentifier(Check Complete & Compatible) request. If the bootloader cannot identify which part that failed the verification, the bit for the Executable shall be set. 4.6.1.2.2 Software Authentication 4.6.1.2.2.1 Software Authentication - IntroductionThe purpose of Software Authentication is described in [General Software Authentication], i.e. to verify that the installed software is authentic (originates from a legitimate source and has not been altered). To perform the authenticity verification, using digital signatures, the ECU must (at least) know:· The data that must be checked for authenticity and where it is located in the memory.Verification Block Tables are used [General Software Authentication]. The verification block table (one per software part) contains the placement and hash value for the expected programmed data blocks.· How to get the corresponding digital signature.· Conditions for starting the verification and what is required for the verification to pass or fail Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU respectively. If a complete verification is not performed at every application start, information about the verification status (validity status information) must be stored.• How many software parts (and their location) that must be successfully verified in order to start the application: ECU Software Structure and Logical Blocks are introduced.The ECU authenticity verification (for a single software part, i.e. a logical block) is performed according to Figure - Authenticity verification principle:(1) - The data blocks of the software part is programmed to the ECU. The corresponding digital signature is transferred using a Check Memory control routine, which will also initiate the verification.(2) - The signed verification block table is verified. The placement of the verification block is ensured as its start address and length parameters are part of the signature generation, i.e. the length (unprocessed) must be calculated by the ECU (the start address is known for the updated logical block).(3) - The programmed data blocks, according to the authenticated verification block, are then verified. The placement of all ingoing data blocks are ensured as their start address and lengths together with the corresponding hash values are part of the verification block table.(4) - The remaining memory area within the logical block shall not have been programmed (the verification block table only contains the programmed data blocks). The ECU verifies that these parts are "blank" (not programmed), e.g. the value of erased memory (hardware dependent) or filled with some known value (e.g. for the SBL). It must be ensured that erased state is a valid state for the used HW. ![](images/975e97dc1ad0219c182404a929c243aab170c875dc7318b6ced47b7b4ef89a59.jpg) GEELYGeely Automotive Research Institute(Ningbo)Co.Ltd Document TypeNote-SWRS Document Release StatusRELEASED Document No Revision005 Volume No01 Page No1340(1572) Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU installed data is erased)Mark the logical block as invalid (i.e. it has not passed the signature verification), prior to any data erase/write operations.Check at every Request Download that the logical block is marked as invalid.Check at Request Download and at Transfer Data that only one logical block has been addressed. Note that the "compressed" (processed) memory size is used as input parameter to the Request Download, i.e. actual programmed length might differ (typically longer).Check at Request Download and at Transfer Data that no memory area is addressed that is exclusive to the bootloader. It must also be ensured that no memory is addressed that is not define, e.g. outside the range of where the application data is allowed to be programmed.At Check Memory, verify according to (1) to (4) in Figure - Authenticity verification principle.Only upon a successful authenticity verification, set the validity status for the verified logical block to valid.At every ECU start, the bootloader must:Verify that all logical block are present and valid (i.e. signature verification is passed). The number of logical blocks and corresponding locations are defined by the ECU Software Structure, i.e. this must be authenticated first. All software must have passed the authenticity verification in order to be executed in the ECU.If the verification is failed, the complete part of the complete and compatible function must fail and the application is not started.4.6.1.2.2.2 Software StructureThe ECU is to be organized into different "logical blocks", the ECU software structure. Each logical block is to be verified (and signed) individually and because of that it must only be one software part (e.g. a VBF) allocated per logical block. A software part is typically segmented into one or many data blocks. That means that all data blocks must reside in the dedicated logical block in order to be able to verify each logical block individually. Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU Figure - Logical Block DefinitionIn Figure - Logical Block Definition, a software part n is segmented into m data blocks and is dedicated to the logical block n.

title: Programming of Logical Blocks
body: 3146 v3 Programming of Logical Blocks Version history:(3):Purpose: Define properties for a logical block, that are required for the ECU to be able to manage each logical block independently but also to simplify the signing process at the trust centre.Source:Verification Method: Test + AnalysisLegacy ID: 400425v2Each logical block shall be possible to sign separately, i.e. each logical block must be possible to erase, program and verify independently in the ECU.

title: Software parts per logical block
body: 3147 v3 Software parts per logical block Version history:(3):Purpose: Define the software structure to enable that each software part is possible to individually sign and verify.Source:Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 397292v2The content (data blocks) of a software part must be within a single logical block range, i.e. two different logical blocks must not be addressed by a single software part.

title: Number of logical blocks
body: 3145 v2 Number of logical blocks Version history:(2):Purpose: Define the minimum number of logical block. The actual number of logical blocks are defined by the ECU Software Structure.Source:Verification Method: Test + AnalysisLegacy ID: 397293v1The ECU shall contain at least one logical block. The maximum number of blocks shall be statically configured in the bootloader.

title: Logical Block - Properties
body: 3143 v4 Logical Block - Properties Version history:(4):Purpose: Define the constraints of a logical block Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU Source:Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 397291v3The non-volatile memory for software download shall be divided into logical blocks that must start and end at the boundary of a flash sector. The logical blocks must not share a common flash sector, i.e. logical blocks must not overlap or contain another logical block. Logical blocks must also not cross different memory devices. It shall be contiguous.Clarification for ECUs having file-based data storage: erasure or modification of a single logical block should not affect contents of other logical blocks (unless explicitly specified in other requirements (e.g. for ESS update)).

title: Logical Block Declaration
body: 3144 v5 Logical Block Declaration Version history:(5):Purpose: To define the properties for each logical blockSource:Verification Method: Test + AnalysisLegacy ID: 397432v4For each individual logical block, following properties must be defined:1. its start address and length, i.e. the location (mandatory)2. where the verification block table is located (mandatory). The verification block contains information (location and hash value) of the data blocks that shall have been programmed to the logical block. It is typically the first downloaded data block of a Software Part.3. how to get the corresponding signature (mandatory) and where is shall be stored (optional). Storing the signature in a non-volatile memory is only applicable for use cases where it is required to perform a signature verification at a later time, i.e. the verification is not only performed at the programming sequence.4. where the validity status information is located (mandatory)5. where the erase status information is located (mandatory), used to identify if a logical block is erased or not, to e.g. not erase memory when it is already erased (time consuming).6. where the compatibility information is located (optional). Used to decide the compatibility to other downloaded parts. This must be known to the bootloader if the check is done by the bootloader itself. See section for Complete&Compatible function for further details.Example.A logical block will contain 1:m data blocks and 1 verification block table. 4.6.1.2.2.2.1 ECU Software Structure (ESS)The ECU Software Structure (ESS) carries the information of all logical block ranges and properties. It shall be stored in a dedicated logical block which position is known to the primary bootloader, e.g. a flash sector exclusively reserved to the ESS. It is however re-programmable as any other software part, according to the Programming sequence.Typical use cases for updating the ESS are when a software part growths beyond its previously Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU reserved logical block or when a software part is divided into two parts.ECU Flash memory Figure - Re-programmable ECU Software Structure(1) The location of the ESS is known by the primary bootloader.(2) The bootloader uses the definitions in the ESS to identify the properties of the other logical blocks. The ESS must first be verified (valid) before its definitions are applied.When there is no valid ESS stored in the dedicated logical block, the ECU must only allow software download of the SBL and to ESS as the information in the ESS is required in order to validate other logical blocks. Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU Figure - Non-protected flash to be erased when the ESS is updated

title: Storage of the ECU Software Structure (ESS)
body: 3153 v2 Storage of the ECU Software Structure (ESS) Version history:(2):Purpose: To reduce the complexity of the bootloader implementation with respect to ESS update use case and for the bootloader to know where to find the logical block definitionsSource:Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 397435v1The ECU Software Structure (ESS) shall be stored at a reserved logical block (flash sector), i.e. dedicated to the ESS only.

title: Reprogrammable ECU Software Structure (ESS)
body: 3151 v3 Reprogrammable ECU Software Structure (ESS) Version history:(3):Purpose: To enable updates of the ESS without requiring a hardware or bootloader update. Typical use cases are when software parts growths in size, the software structure is changed (e.g. a software part is divided into two parts or vice versa).Source:Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 397436v2The ESS shall be reprogrammable according to the Programming Sequence described in this document, i.e. as any other software part. Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU

title: Immediately apply ESS update
body: 3150 v2 Immediately apply ESS update Version history:(2):Purpose: The ESS is downloaded as any other software parts. For example, an ECU reset cannot be added to the programming sequence every time an ESS is updated.Source:Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 411891v1The ESS updates must be applied immediately after being verified correctly, i.e. an initiation of the bootloader must not be required. This means that another software part (e.g. EXE) shall be possible to program next to the ESS without requiring an ECU reset.

title: Restricted software download when no valid ESS stored
body: 3152 v4 Restricted software download when no valid ESS stored Version history:(4):Purpose: To enable ECU Software Structure (ESS) update when there is no valid ESS stored.Source:Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 397438v3If there is no valid ESS stored, the software download must be restricted to the SBL and the logical block dedicated to the ESS only. That means that attempts to address other logical blocks shall be rejected. The ECU shall inform the tester of the aborted erase memory attempt or aborted request download.Note: The SBL is verified by the primary bootloader.

title: Validation of the ECU Software Structure
body: 3154 v4 Validation of the ECU Software Structure Version history:(4):Purpose: The verification of the programmed data could be bypassed if the logical block carrying the ESS is not valid.Source:Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 404771v3The ESS must be validated before the bootloader applies the ESS definitions. The minimum requirements are that it shall be verified as any other logical blocks and ensure that the complete memory is covered by the defined logical blocks.Note: The ECU is recommended to add additional checks to e.g. ensure that the format or length is correct, even though these parts are to be verified prior to the software part is signed. Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU

title: Erase memory when ECU Software Structure (ESS) is updated
body: 3149 v3 Erase memory when ECU Software Structure (ESS) is updated Version history:(3):Purpose: To ensure a known memory state when the ESS is updated.Source:Verification Method: Test + AnalysisLegacy ID: 397440v2The complete programmable flash memory shall be erased when the logical block dedicated to the ESS is (internally) addressed for erasure, i.e. being updated and its validity is changed from valid to invalid.Example.The bootloader detects that the ESS is addressed for erasure. The bootloader will ensure that all flash memory is erased according to a defined physical flash layout. Note that a logical block shall be set to 'invalid' prior to it is erased. The erase might be initiated by either EraseMemory or RequestDownload.4.6.1.2.2.2.2 ECU Software Structure - DeclarationThe format of the ECU Software Structure is design specific and will not be specified in details. Some parts might be explicitly defined in the structure itself or derived from another known location, e.g. the logical block range.Example. ---- ESS ----ESS Start Pattern = ...Number Of Logical Blocks = ...Application Start Address = ...---- Logical Block 1 ----startAddress = ...length = ...Verification Block Table location = ...Validity Status location = ...Erase Status location = ...Compatibility information location = ...---- Logical Block 2 ----startAddress = ...length = ...Verification Block Table location = ...Validity Status location = ...Erase Status location = ...Compatibility information location = ... Logical Block 1Logical Block 2Logical Block ES Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU Figure - Example of ESS DeclarationTo have a simplified view, the Figure - Example of ESS Declaration shows when Validity Status information and Erase Status information are stored within each logical block range. These could also be stored elsewhere, e.g. in a dedicated memory exclusive to the bootloader. See separate section for Validity Status as it has dependencies to the ECU verification being executed at start (boot). Previous figure shows the case where the Validity Status is used to indicate the latest software download status. The recommendation is to verify all software also at boot.

title: ECU Software Structure Declaration
body: 3148 v3 ECU Software Structure Declaration Version history:(3):Purpose: Define the properties of the ECU Software Structure. The supplier is responsible to specify the format of the ESS in detail. This degree of freedom is left to the supplier in order to not interfere with supplier specific tool chain and implementations.Source:Verification Method: Test + AnalysisLegacy ID: 399873v2The ECU Software Structure shall at least contain:A pattern known to the bootloader, defining the existence of the structure, i.e. always starting with a known pattern.The number of logical blocks defined in the ESS.The definitions of all logical blocks, see REQPROD Logical Block Declaration.4.6.1.2.2.2.3 Root ECU Software StructureThe ECU Software Structure is stored in a dedicated logical block. But, the bootloader must know the properties of that logical block. Hence, the term Root ECU Software Structure is introduced. This structure is stored in a protected area known to the bootloader (e.g. in the bootloader area itself).

title: Root ECU Software Structure Declaration
body: 3155 v3 Root ECU Software Structure Declaration Version history:(3):Purpose: Define ESS properties that must be stored in a protected area known to, or part of, the bootloader. This properties are required when there is no ESS stored and for the bootloader to be able to verify that the stored ESS is valid (i.e. has passed the authenticity verification).Source:Verification Method: Test + AnalysisLegacy ID: 399878v2The ECU shall in a protected (not possible to alter nor read) area statically store the definitions required to verify the logical block dedicated to the ECU Software Structure, i.e:(i) start address and length (mandatory) Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU (ii) where the verification block table is located (mandatory)(iii) where the validity status information is located (mandatory)(iv) where the erase status information is located (mandatory)(v) where the compatibility information is located (optional)(vi) where the signature of the verification block table is to be stored (optional). 4.6.1.2.2.3 Erase Status InformationPer logical block, the bootloader shall able to identify if the logical block is erased or not. This is typically used by the bootloader to not erase memory (time consuming) when it's already erased, but also to ensure that the memory has been erased as expected for use cases where this is required.

title: Erase Status Information
body: 3128 v4 Erase Status Information Version history:(4):Purpose: To reduce software download time and to ensure that the memory has been erased as expected.Source:Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 401108v3The ECU shall reserve some dedicated memory to the Erase Status Information. This information must be exclusively handled by the bootloader. If the logical block is "already erased" and an valid erase request is detected, the ECU shall not perform any erase operations. Once one or more bytes of the programmable area has been programmed, the addressed logical block must be considered as "not erased" until it is ensured that the complete block has been erased again. The ECU supplier must ensure that a "virgin" ECU has this information set to erased and that a completely programmed ECU has the erase information set to "not erased".4.6.1.2.2.4 Verification Block TableA Verification Block Table is introduced, representing the expected segmented data blocks (including address, length and hash values per data block) of a complete software part. By that, the signature could be created on the verification block table. When that block is verified correctly at the ECU, the ECU could continue to verify also the other data blocks that has been programmed. Hence, the security principle of "chain-of-trust" is applied. Note that the verification block table is downloaded as any other data block, i.e. the verification block is a separate data block with defined properties. Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU Verification of programmed data blocks is NOK Verification of programmed data blocks is OKFigure - Verification of programmed data blocksThe verification block table must be put in a separate data block (i.e. downloaded as a separate data block to the ECU) and it shall contain:Verification Block Table format identifier, e.g. a version number if the format of the table is changed in the futureNumber of data blocks (the verification block table itself is excluded)StartAddress data block 1, length data block 1, hash value of data block 1...StartAddress data block m, length data block m, hash value of data block mNote that there is one verification block table per every software part. Figure - Restricted SWDL when no valid ESS stored ![](images/241291edf0a610be442256c84081b49116578aa0d3e981f630c9b048e74d5ab0.jpg) Figure - Verification Block Table overview GEELYGeely Automotive Research Institute(Ningbo)Co.Ltd Document TypeNote-SWRS Document Release StatusRELEASED Document No Revision005 Volume No01 Page No1350(1572) Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU In Figure - Verification Block Table overview it is shown how the verification block table is constructed. The hash values are calculated on the data parts only, i.e. the start address and length is not used as input to the hash function. The placement of each data block is ensured as the start address and length are also defined in the table. The format of the table is defined in [General Software Authentication].

title: Allocation of the Verification Block Table
body: 3161 v4 Allocation of the Verification Block Table Version history:(4): Clarifiction Purpose: The position of the verification block table must be known by the bootloader in order to perform the verification. The verification block must not be part of any other data block, as the verification block table contains hash values of all other data blocks, i.e. it cannot contain the hash of itself. Source:Verification Method: Analysis AND TestLegacy ID: 398372v2 A verification block table as defined Req ID1600: Format of the Verification Block Table shall be stored in a separate data block. The start address shall be defined by the logical block definition, i.e. by the ECU Software Structure. The correct location of the verification block is ensured by including its address information (start and length) when it is being signed. The length (unprocessed) must be calculated by the ECU when the data is programmed. Design consideration: When delta encoding is applied, the length of the Verification Block Table could be derived by using the start address and Number of data blocks.

title: Verification Block Table - Reserve space at application build process
body: 3162 v2 Verification Block Table - Reserve space at application build process Version history:(2): Purpose: The verification block table is part of the post processing sequence, meaning that it is generated after the actual software is build. Source:Verification Method: Test + AnalysisLegacy ID: 402292v1 The application software build process must reserve memory space for the verification block table within a logical block. It is the software supplier that creates the block table and includes it in the software part. 4.6.1.2.2.5 Validation of ECU software(s) - Authenticity Verification 4.6.1.2.2.5.1 Authenticity Verification - Overview An overview of the authenticity verification was previously described in the beginning of the section Software Authentication - Introduction. The programming sequence, highlighting the authenticity verification parts is shown in Figure - Programming Sequence and authenticity ![](images/97a9b7dfdd3abc0630cf688bc206672039f079b8dc51cfbc5aea82e774796729.jpg) GEELYGeely Automotive Research Institute(Ningbo)Co.Ltd Document TypeNote-SWRS Document Release StatusRELEASED Document No Revision005 Volume No01 Page No1352(1572) Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU modified. Any condition that triggers a change of memory (erase/write) of a logical block shall result in that the logical block is set to (or kept) invalid.Source:Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 400994v2When the ECUinternalconditions for altering (erase/write) a logical block is true, e.g. triggered by a physical/functional EraseMemory, RequestDownload etc., request, the ECU must ensure that the validity status of the addressed logical block is set to invalidpriorto the actual memory erasure (or data write) operation is started. The logical block shall be invalid if the authenticity verification is failed. For every RequestDownload, the ECU shall always check that the logical block is 'invalid', otherwise the ECU shall:(i) abort the request, for ECUs where a EraseMemory requestmustbe received prior to the RequestDownload or(ii) set the logical block to 'invalid' and continue with the requested service, where no EraseMemory is required

title: Condition for a logical block to be valid
body: 3158 v4 Condition for a logical block to be valid Version history:(4):Purpose:A logical block must be verified successfully with respect to its authenticity every time it has been altered, in order to be considered as valid.Source:Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 400992v3A logical block mustonlybe set to valid if it has passed the authenticity verification as defined in Figure - Authenticity Verification function. The verification shall be done on data in the non-volatile memory (i.e. at the target location). Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU Figure - Authenticity Verification function(1) - Applicable only if code signing certificates are applied, see [Software Authentication for file based systems] for additional requirements.(2) - Signature verification. Note that the start address and length are used as input to ensure the placement, i.e. the length must for some use cases be calculated (delta encoding). The format and length of the verification block table shall be verified. Prior to the signature verification is performed, the integrity of the public key shall be ensured.(3) - Verify that the hash value (per data block) is identical to the definition in the verification block table.(4) - Verify that the non-programmed areas (not part of the authenticated verification block table) are erased. Previously programmed data that is no longer in use shall have been erased Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU ("uninstalled").(5) - Additional checks, e.g. if the ECU has support to prevent downgrade, meaning that an older (no longer valid) software part must not be installed as it might include some vulnerabilities. CEVT to be consulted if such protection shall be applied (processes must be defined at off-board to support such a use case).When the authenticity verification function is completed, it must be ensured that the verification status (validity status information) is stored correctly.Mandatory for the ECU Software Structure: The Logical Blocks defined in the programmed ESS covers the complete memory, i.e. all memory are always to be verified.4.6.1.2.2.5.3 Validity Status InformationA software part is considered as complete (valid) when the authenticity verification of the belonging logical block is passed. Hence, besides the verificaiton at download the ECU must either verify the software at every boot (recommended) or store information in a protected non-volatile memory about the verification status of each logical block (e.g. valid or invalid), with respect to the authenticity verification at software download. This information is referred to as validity information. Every time a logical block is altered, e.g. erased or programmed, its status must be set to invalid until a successful verification has been completed.For ECUs verifying the authenticity of the bootloader and application software(s) prior to every execution (e.g. at start), there is no need to store the validity status information in a non-volatile memory. Due to e.g. start-up timing requirements, the ECU possibilities to do the signature check (as in CheckMemory) at every start is limited. To be able to perform a verification at start, the solutions provided by the ECU hardware platform in terms of cryptographic support is to be used.

title: Validity Status Information - Properties
body: 3160 v6 Validity Status Information - Properties Version history:(6): Clarification Purpose: The validity information is the status of the authenticity verification. Only a trusted entity must be able to store (alter) the validity information. A minimum size is defined to avoid that a "bit-flip" result in that a logical block is set to 'valid'.Source:Verification Method: Test + AnalysisLegacy ID: 400961v6 The validity status information for each logical block, i.e. if the block has passed- or failed the authenticity verification at software download, shall have a minimum length of 8 octets. One single value shall represent 'Valid' and all other values shall be interpreted as 'Invalid'. 'Valid' must not be represented by setting all bytes to the same value, e.g. 0xFF, or to the value of erased memory.If the authenticity verification is not performed at every boot sequence, the validity information must be stored in a non-volatile protected (secure) memory. The best available solution provided by the ECU shall be used (hardware security module or equivalent, EEPROM, a pattern in flash etc.). The validity status must not be altered by other means than by the trustworthy verifying component, i.e. it must not be altered by the application or by a tester tool Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU or any other unauthorized entity addressing that area. It must also not be possible to read, or upload, using a tester or debugger tool.Note: An ECU unique value for 'Valid' shall be applied.4.6.1.2.2.5.4 Public Key StorageSee [General Software Authentication] for requirements about public key programming during test and production.

title: Public Key storage
body: 3156 v3 Public Key storage Version history:(3): ClarificationPurpose: The trust anchor shall not be possible to manipulate, that could be used to bypass the protection.Source:Verification Method: Test + AnalysisLegacy ID: 366329v2The trust anchor, i.e. the public key, shall be stored in a protected (read-only) area, typically in a hardware secure module or a protected boot area. It shall be one-time-programmable.

title: Re-programmable initial development key
body: 3157 v3 Re-programmable initial development key Version history:(3): Change the Verification Method from Test to Analysis+TestPurpose: Define key management with respect to the test, development and release (production).Source:Verification Method: Analysis AND TestLegacy ID: 429095v1The ECU shall use an initial public key for development purposes. It is stored in the ECU by the ECU supplier (e.g. "virgin" ECU). When the initial development key is stored in the ECU, the public key for production shall always be possible to program. When a valid public key has been programmed, the initial development key must no longer be used by the ECU. The development key defined in [General Software Authentication] shall be applied unless else is explicitly specified.4.6.1.2.2.6 Programming Sequence - Authenticity VerificationThis section will show define the ECU actions part of the programming sequence, as previously shown in Figure - Programming Sequence and authenticity verification.4.6.1.2.2.6.1 Memory Erasure

title: Erase Identifier - restrictions
body: 3134 v4 Erase Identifier - restrictions Version history:(4): Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU Purpose: To ensure that a complete logical block is erased is required for several purposes: (1) To ensure that all information about validity status is always erased (if part of the logical block). Otherwise, implicitly knowledge of the bootloader implementation is required to ensure that it is erased. (2) No unknown data is stored in the addressed logical block, i.e. previously installed data deleted ("uninstalled). (3) It will also enable simplified off-board review of the logical block definitions, by checking that the erase identifier is identical to the expected logical block.Source:Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 400878v3The erase identifier range(s) of the software part header must match a valid logical block. The ECU shall at an eraseMemory request verify that the erase startAddress and Length matches a logical block range, otherwise the ECU shall abort the request. If the eraseMemory request is valid, the ECU must ensure that the complete memory for the addressed logical block is erased.4.6.1.2.2.6.2 Request Download

title: Request Download - restrictions on number of addressed logical blocks
body: 3135 v5 Request Download - restrictions on number of addressed logical blocksVersion history:(5): ClarificationPurpose: To verify that there is only one software part allocated to each logical block and to enable verification for the downloaded data range, i.e. each logical block is verified independently.Source:Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 400894v3The ECU shall check that only one logical block is being updated for a single downloaded software part, i.e. one logical block is allowed to be addressed from a valid RequestDownload to a CheckMemory request is detected. If any memory outside that first logical block is addressed by a RequestDownload request(s), e.g. a second logical block or some location not defined by the ESS at all, the ECU shall abort the RequestDownload and inform the client via a NRC.As the processed length (compressed/encrypted) length is used as memorySize parameter of the RequestDownload request, there are scenarios when it is not possible to detect this at the RequestDownload stage but identified later when the data is uncompressed/decrypted and about to be written to the memory. Anyhow, the download shall be aborted when it is detected.To be able to recover when download sequence is aborted, for example trying download the same software part once again or continue downloading the next software part (another logical block), the ECU shall upon a rejected request enter a state where no logical block is active and wait for next request to erase or program the memory. Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU Figure - Simplified logical block active states overviewNotes:- "Figure Simplified logical block active states overview" shows the principle only, details are omitted. 'Valid requests' are e.g. ReadDataByIdentifier requests, TransferData, RequestsTransferExit. "Error handling" includes the previously described scenario, where e.g. a RequestDownload addresses a logical block that is the 'active' block.- The figure does not show the actual verification status of each logical block.Example.- the ECU is having a file based memory structure, not requiring an explicit erase memory request prior to request download. SBL is already verified and activated. ![](images/d5406c9a16fface11b1953213f87ddb11c1f74f840ca5a5c0d10e6344502e884.jpg) GEELYGeely Automotive Research Institute(Ningbo)Co.Ltd Document TypeNote-SWRS Document Release StatusRELEASED Document No Revision005 Volume No01 Page No1359(1572) Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU Source:Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 405471v2The result values from the CheckMemory request shall be one byte long and represented according to Table - CheckMemory return Values. This means that the authenticity verification for a given logical block is passed when the routine returns 0 (CheckMemoryResultValue is 0x00) Return values from the CheckMemory routine - CheckMemoryResponseValueValue Description Others User defined 0x0B Certificate verification failed, i.e. applicable for ECUs supporting code signing certificates. 0x0A Error during storage of validity status information 0x09 An additional processor reported failed verification, i.e. only applicable for ECUs having additional processors. 0x08 ESS does not cover all programmable memory, i.e. only applicable when the logical block for the ESS is verified. 0x07 Read error during hash calculation over memory content. 0x06 No data downloaded at all, nothing to verify. 0x05 The “blank” check failed, i.e. unexpected data at areas not included in the authenticated verification block table (e.g. data has not been "uninstalled"). 0x04 The address or hash values of the downloaded data blocks does not match the expected values 0x03 Invalid format or length of the Verification Block Table 0x02 The public key (“root certificate”) is not stored or is not complete (integrity check failed). 0x01 The signed data could not be authenticated, i.e. signature verification failed 0x00 The verification is passed Table - CheckMemory return values

title: Check Memory - verification of programmed data
body: 3130 v3 Check Memory - verification of programmed data Version history:(3): Purpose: The CheckMemory is executed in the ECU via the routineldentifier(Check Memory). This will inform the ECU that a software part is downloaded and that the authenticity verification of the stored data shall be started. For some scenarios, the software download tools will require two attempts (e.g. for development and production units) Source:Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 405174v2The ECU shall start the authenticity verification of programmed data when the routineldentifier Document Name Base Tech SWRS DHU CheckMemory is received. It shall be possible to make two consecutive CheckMemory attempts (i.e. one false attempt is possible). The verification result from the latest CheckMemory attempt shall be applied in the ECU. If the CheckMemory verification has failed and no more attempts are allowed, a new data transfer of the software part must be performed in order to verify the software at a CheckMemory request again. If a third consecutive CheckMemory request is sent, that request must be aborted. Tester Description Data Explanation Tx CheckMemory request (f,f) 11 04 31 01 02 12 xx xx Rx Flow control 30 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 Tx CheckMemory request (c,f) 21 xx xx xx xx xx xx xx ... ... ... Rx CheckMemory request (c,f) 25 xx xx 00 00 00 00 00 Response pending (if needed) Negative response 03 7F 31 78 00 00 00 00 Rx Positive response 06 71 01 02 12 10 01 00 Verification failed Tx CheckMemory request (f,f) 11 04 31 01 02 12 y/y y/y A second consecutive CheckMemory attempt is ok, as no other request has been sent in between the CheckMemory requests. Rx Flow control 30 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 Tx CheckMemory request (c,f) 21 y/y y/y y/y y/y y/y y/y y/y ... ... ... Rx CheckMemory request (c,f) 25 y/y y/y 00 00 00 00 00 Negative response 03 7F 31 78 00 00 00 00 Rx Positive response 06 71 01 02 12 10 00 00 Verification successful GEELYGeely Automotive Research Institute(Ningbo)Co.Ltd Document TypeNote-SWRS Document Release StatusRELEASED Document No Revision005 Volume No01 Page No1361(1572) Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU When the application start up conditions are fulfilled, according to the Complete&Compatible function, the application start address must be within the range of a validated logical block.4.6.1.2.2.6.6 Download and activate the SBLIt is important that the authenticity of the secondary bootloader (SBL) is verified prior to its activated. Otherwise, there is an increased risk of having the primary bootloader replaced or by other means bypass the provided verification mechanisms and start the application. The principle of verifying the SBL is the same as for any other logical blocks in the non-volatile memory, but for the SBL it is recommended to implement a single data block (but with addition of a verification block table). This might result in a simplified verification of the SBL. A single block SBL is however not suitable for ECU hardware architectures having additional microcontrollers, but only one SBL (software part) is used. Refer to requirements about secondary processors. ![](images/ca181f9e8ba007afa8e011c86b615edf7edec628f867bbb6070f5599e18509a6.jpg) Figure - Overview - Programming Sequence SBL GEELYGeely Automotive Research Institute(Ningbo)Co.Ltd Document TypeNote-SWRS Document Release StatusRELEASED Document No Revision005 Volume No01 Page No1362(1572) Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU The Figure - Overview - Programming Sequence SBL shows an overview of the programming sequence, a more detailed description of the Tester-ECU requests and responses are to be shown in next coming sections.

title: Secondary Bootloader - Condition for activation
body: 3131 v4 Secondary Bootloader - Condition for activation Version history:(4):Purpose: The authenticity of the secondary bootloader must be verified. Otherwise, the verification mechanism could be bypassed and arbitrary application could be started.Source:Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 400704v3The primary bootloader must ensure that the authenticity verification of the secondary bootloader is passed prior to it is activated. If the verification fails, the ECU shall remain in the primary bootloader and the volatile memory buffer shall be cleared. The used address parameter of the ActivateSBL routine control must be within the address range of the validated block(s).

title: Secondary Bootloader Verification of unused data
body: 3132 v2 Secondary Bootloader Verification of unused data Version history:(2):Purpose: The authenticity verification shall check that there is no data programmed to memory not part of the authenticated verification block table. The SBL is stored in a volatile memory, RAM, and dependent of the actual RAM implementation it might be faster for the bootloader to fill (write) the unused memory with known data (e.g. 0xFF) instead of checking (read) that no data has been programmed to memory not defined in the verification block.Source:Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 416451v1The bootloader shall ensure that there is no SBL data programmed to memory that is not defined in the verification block table.4.6.1.2.2.6.7 Request Upload

title: RequestUpload - Restricted use
body: 3136 v2 RequestUpload - Restricted use Version history:(2): ClarificationPurpose: Define restricted areas and recommendations if the RequestUpload service is supported.Source:Verification Method: Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU Legacy ID: 429415v1If the RequestUpload service is supported by the ECU, the following areas shall be blocked and not possible to upload data from:(i) Boot area and where the verification function is stored(ii) Area where the public key is stored(iii) Area where validity status information is stored(iv) Area where any confidential key is storedNote: For intellectual properties rights (e.g. when the software part is encrypted at download), the service shall be used with care.4.6.1.2.2.7 Additional requirements for ECUs having multiple processorsThe term main processor is in this context used to define the microcontroller having the interface to the network used for software download. The requirements in this section are valid for ECUs where all software to the secondary processor is not directly sent to the secondary processor but being addressed to the main processor, i.e. it is considered as one single ECU from a tester point of view. Figure - Additional processors - OverviewThe bootloader of the main processor must be able to identify the software parts belonging to a memory device at the secondary processor, typically by using an address offset, and transfer it accordingly. It is recommended that the main processors keeps some information about the memory layout of also the secondary processor in order to do a first filtering before the data is transferred to the secondary processor. The principle to apply is that the logical blocks shall be Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU verified by the entity where it is executed.

title: Multiple processors - verification principle
body: 3124 v2 Multiple processors - verification principle Version history:(2):Purpose: From a security point of view, the software is to be finally verified at the target processor. This will reduce the risk of having software altered when it is in transit.Source:Verification Method: Test + AnalysisLegacy ID: 401206v1The logical block shall be verified by the target processor respectively, i.e. either by the main- or the secondary processor.Note: The actual ECU implementation is highly HW dependent, e.g. capabilities of the processors and internal interfaces.4.6.1.2.2.7.1 Multiple processors - Secondary BootloaderThe Secondary Bootloader is a special scenario, where it is required to address two (main/secondary processor) different memory devices in a single software part. See Figure - SBL verification for ECUs having additional processor. Figure - SBL verification for ECUs having additional processorResponsibility of the main processor:The main processor will verify the authenticity of the verification block table and verify and the data block within its memory range. The main processor will request the verification result from the secondary processor, i.e. for the data blocks addressed to the secondary processor. Hence, the main processor must forward a copy of the verification block, its signature and all data blocks belonging to the secondary processor. Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU Responsibility of the secondary processor:The secondary processor will also verify the authenticity of the verification block table but not verify the number of data blocks part of the verification block. The actual number of downloaded data blocks, verification block excluded, shall be 1. The secondary processor shall verify that the start address, length and hash value of the downloaded data block is identical to the values defined in the verification block. It shall report the verification result to the main processor.

title: Multiple processors - Main processor SBL verification
body: 3125 v2 Multiple processors - Main processor SBL verification Version history:(2):Purpose: Define the verification performed by the main processor with respect to the SBL.Source:Verification Method: Test + AnalysisLegacy ID: 402299v1The main processor shall (at least) verify the data blocks dedicated to memory space of the main processor itself. The main processor shall forward the data blocks belonging to the secondary processor together with a copy of the verification block table.Note: The verification is, besides this exception, to be performed as for any other logical block (e.g. including signature verification etc.).

title: Multiple processors - Secondary processor SBL verification
body: 3126 v3 Multiple processors - Secondary processor SBL verification Version history:(3):Purpose: Define the verification performed by the secondary processor with respect to the SBL.Source:Verification Method: Test + AnalysisLegacy ID: 402300v2The secondary processor shall first verify the verification block table and then the downloaded data blocks within its memory space. The secondary processor will not receive all data blocks as defined in the verification block table.4.6.1.2.2.8 Additional requirements for ECUs implementing delta encodingThe delta file will contain information about the target version, as for any other processing method. Document Name Base Tech SWRS DHU Figure - Content of a delta file Figure - Content of a delta file shows that the required header information for authenticity verification is added to the delta file, i.e. the signature of the target software (version 2.0). For ECUs implementing delta encoding, there are some conflicting requirements, e.g. that a complete logical block must always be erased but delta requirement to only erase sectors that are altered (no eraseMemory requests are required by the client). If the ECU is storing Validity Status Information in the flash memory within a logical block range, that flash sector will require some "special handling" to ensure that the altered logical block is always set to invalid. Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU the application data part has been altered or not. See example:Example.(1) - Some part in the logical block is about to be altered.(2) - The bootloader must always set the logical block to invalid, prior to the memory is altered,i.e. the Validity Status is set to invalid at the RequestDownload request (erase memory requestis not applied for delta encoding)(3) - When the Validity Status is erased, the shared sector is copied to the delta back-up sector.(4) - The shared sector is erased(5) - The data stored in the back-up sector is copied to the shared sector again, now with thevalidity status set to invalid.(6) - Start the delta download(7) - Verify the logical blockIt is ECU specific how the Validity Status is stored, previous section is to illustrate an exampleonly.

title: Delta encoding - Verification
body: 3127 v2 Delta encoding - Verification Version history:(2):Purpose: The verification of a delta installation shall fulfill the same level of authenticityverification as for any other processing method. Due to the nature of a deltainstallation, some requirements are clarified by this dedicated requirement.Source:Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 416271v1When a delta encoding processing method is used, following must (still apply):The final target shall be verified, i.e. the unprocessed data after the delta encoding hasbeen applied.The verification block table and CheckMemory parameters shall be generated from thetarget software and copied to the delta file when it is generated.A single logical block shall be addressed, e.g. the "delta-library" used must not itselfperform any read/erase operations (these must be requested from the bootloader)4.6.1.2.2.9 Signing method

title: Software authentication signing method and algorithms
body: 3137 v2 Software authentication signing method and algorithms Version history:(2):Purpose: Define how to identify the signing methods to be used, e.g. the public-keyalgorithm, key sizes etc.Source:Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 420111v1The ECU shall implement the default signing method as defined in [General Software Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU Authentication].4.6.1.2.2.10 Software Authentication - Generic security requirementsThis section contains the generic Software Authentication security requirements. The actual implementation might differ, e.g. dependent of if code signing certificates or only the key-pair are used when signing/verifying the software, when the ECU could perform the authenticity verification etc.

title: Allocation of the Authenticity Verification function
body: 3138 v2 Allocation of the Authenticity Verification function Version history:(2):Purpose: Tamper resistance, to prevent to that the function is bypassed.Source:Verification Method: AnalysisLegacy ID: 366327v1The authenticity verification function shall be stored in a protected area. If a hardware security module is deployed to the ECU this is required to be used for signature verification function.

title: Authenticity verification at software download (Program mode)
body: 3141 v2 Authenticity verification at software download (Program mode) Version history:(2):Purpose: Verifying code after a software download (at installation) is the minimum level of the concept.Source:Verification Method: Test + AnalysisLegacy ID: 360452v1The authenticity verification function shall always be performed at software download (installation).

title: Authenticity verification at every start-up
body: 3139 v3 Authenticity verification at every start-up Version history:(3): ClarificationPurpose: Define when the ECU authenticity verification shall be started (mandatory on condition)Source:Verification Method: Test + AnalysisLegacy ID: 419731v1If the ECU is able to fulfill the application start-up conditions, the authenticity verification shall be started every time the (main) application is to be started (via bootloader), typically at every ECU Reset or Power-Up. Hence, the validity status information shall not be permanently stored in the ECU. Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU Note: Design consideration - if the verification using digital signatures is not feasible every start,the ECU could after a successful signature verification at software download calculatea message authentication code (MAC) over the verified logical block. During start, that MAC isverified. ECU internal secret keys shall be applied in that case, both the keys and MAC shall bestored in protected memory. This shall be considered if the ECU has the capabilities tocalculate and store the MAC and still fulfill the start-up timing If the verification cannot beperformed at start (boot), it must be proven by the ECU supplier by providing e.g. hardware- orperformance figures why it is not possible and how the system is hardened against anyupdates except the defined software download sequence. If any software fails to beauthenticated during boot, that sequence shall be aborted.Design considerations: If the signature verification (as part of CheckMemory) could not beapplied at start-up at any stage, the boot and application software(s) are to be signed (andverified) explicitly for verification at boot. These methods relies on solutions using eithersymmetric or asymmetric keys as provided by the ECU hardware. It relies on HW support toprovide the initial root-of-trust (read only) code and a one-time-programmable verification key.Unless others are explicitly required, any others keys but the public key used at CheckMemoryare supplier responsibility. Symmetric key solutions (e.g. AES-CMAC calculated over a logicalblock) requires that the confidential key is in a secured memory, protected from being alteredand read as well as ensuring that a verification request origins from a trustworthy component ina secure environment.Note 1: Adaptation data that is changed when application is running is not part of start-upcheck.Example. Figure - Chain-of-trust for authenticity verification at startNote 2: If the ECU calculates a cryptographic message authentication code (MAC, e.g. AES-CMAC) upon a valid signature verification at software download and verifies that MAC at everystart-up, device unique keys must be used. Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU

title: Authenticity verification at run time (main application running)
body: 3140 v2 Authenticity verification at run time (main application running) Version history:(2):Purpose: This requirement is optional. Authenticity checks could be performed at some time(s) when the main application is up and running. This run time check is to be performed by an additional trustworthy entity, a hardware secure module, and not the main application itself.Source:Verification Method: Test + AnalysisLegacy ID: 419911v1An optional check could be performed by an trustworthy entity, e.g. a hardware security module, when the main application is running. What to verify and how to react is ECU and function specific, but a minimum action is to store an event (security audit log) that is possible to read using a diagnostic identifier.

title: Debug tools and ports
body: 3142 v1 Debug tools and ports Version history:(1):Purpose: To avoid memory manipulation and e.g. deactivate the verification function or program software.Source:Verification Method: Test + AnalysisLegacy ID: 419132v0The ECU must be protected from all kind of memory manipulations (e.g. via diagnostic services or debuggers) except the diagnostic services supported and specified by in Global Master Reference Database.4.6.1.2.3 Time window for PROG detectionIf not explicitly stated in respectively bootloader implementation specification shall the primary bootloader (PBL) have a time window (Timeout_Prog) for detection of the DiagnosticSessionControl service. This backdoor solution shall be used if the ECU believes it has valid software(s) present, but the application software is not correctly jumping to the PBL. This method may only be used in a stand alone scenario, due to the impossibility for the gateway ECUs to transmit the DiagnosticSessionControl service in time.The tester shall send out the DiagnosticSessionControl service with diagnosticSessionType set to programmingSession and suppressPosRspMsgIndicationBit equal to TRUE during a minimum time of 5 seconds. The repetition rate of the DiagnosticSessionControl service shall be sent within 5ms but preferably at 2 ms or faster. Figure - Typical boot sequence of ECU's in a vehicle

title: Time window (Timeout_Prog)

body: 3116 v2 ProgSignature - CLEAR Version history: (2): Purpose: To prevent unwanted bootloader activation Source: Verification Method: Test Legacy ID: 53932v1 The ProgSignature shall be cleared with a recommended value of 0x000000000000000000 by the bootloader before starting the application.

title: ProgSignature - SET
body: 3117 v2 ProgSignature - SET Version history: Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU (2):Purpose: To be able to enter the primary bootloader from the application by sending the DiagnosticSessionControl(programmingSession) service once.Source:Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 53930v1The ProgSignature shall be written to a fixed address in the volatile memory, with a length of 8 bytes and a recommended value of 0x50726f675369676e (equal to text string "ProgSign" in ASCII-format) by the application after receiving the DiagnosticSessionControl(programmingSession) request.Note: The fixed address must be synchronized between the application and bootloader.4.6.1.2.5 ECU program modeProgram mode means that the ECU executing the primary or secondary bootloader.This section describes the bootloader state and flow chart diagram in a general way. title: Disable monitoring and logging of DTCs
body: 3114 v2 Disable monitoring and logging of DTCs Version history:(2):Purpose: To prevent logging and monitoring of DTCs when the bootloader executing.Source:Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 53929v1The ECU shall ensure that the monitoring and logging of all diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs) is disabled when executing the bootloader (programmingSession).

title: Suspend non diagnostic communication
body: 3115 v2 Suspend non diagnostic communication Version history:(2):Purpose: To only have diagnostic communication between tester and ECU when executing the bootloader.Source:Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 53927v1Whenever an ECU is executing the bootloader, it shall ensure that non diagnostic communication e.g. network management messages between ECUs are suspended.4.6.1.2.5.1 Simplified bootloader state and flow chart diagramThe bootloader state diagram, Figure " Simplified bootloader state diagram" shows a simplified example of the different states the ECU can enter in the bootloader. The state diagram is in Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU detailed described in each bootloader implementation specification for respectively network.From power on or reset initiated by the application the PBL shall start executing the initialization state where the PBL decide whether the application shall be started or not.The primary bootloader (PBL) shall have a time window (Timeout_Prog) for detection of the DiagnosticSessionControl service. This backdoor solution shall be used if the ECU believes it has a valid software(s) present, but the application software is not jumping to the PBL or if the application is not able to process a diagnostic request (see section "Time window for PROG detection").The programmingSession state is entered if the reset was initiated by the diagnostic request DiagnosticSessionControl(programmingSession) in the application (Warm start) or if no valid software(s) occurs (see section "Enter the bootloader (PBL) from the application" and "Validation of ECU Software(s)").The application is started if the start-up was a cold start and valid software(s) is present. Client Server Server (Non volatile memory) Transfer of Block #n RequestDownload Receive buffer Write data- Write data- Write data- TransferData (F.F) TransferData (C.F) TransferData (last C.F) PosResp_TransferData Start hash Calculate hash Calculate hash Transfer of Last Block TransferData (F.F) Receive buffer Write data- Write data- Write data- TransferData (C.F) TransferData (last C.F) PosResp_TransferData Continue hash Calculate hash Calculate hash Transfer completed RequestTransferExit Receive buffer Calculate hash Calculate hash PosResp_RequestTransferExit() Check Authenticity CheckMemory Receive buffer Calculate hash Calculate hash PosResP_CheckMemory GEELYGeely Automotive Research Institute(Ningbo)Co.Ltd Document TypeNote-SWRS Document Release StatusRELEASED Document No Revision005 Volume No01 Page No1380(1572) Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU Purpose: To decrease the total programming time.Source:Verification Method: AnalysisLegacy ID: 53980v2The ECU shall in between each TransferData request calculate the hash value, when next TransferData request is received the calculation shall be halted and continue after the data block is written to the non-volatile memory. The ECU must therefore remember where the calculation shall continue.Important is that the pre-calculation must be done on data in the non-volatile memory. It is not allowed to pre-calculate received data in the volatile memory.4.6.1.2.8 Writing of received data to non-volatile memoryTo decrease the total programming time it is important to start writing data to the non-volatile memory before the complete message is received, decompression included if supported. The positive response shall be sentafterall data included in the TransferData request is written to the non-volatile memory.If the message is interrupted or no response is given to the client the block will be resent. As non-volatile memories normally only allow one write operation for each erase operation the ECU must know how many data bytes it has written to the non-volatile memory. If the client transfers the same block again the ECU shall count the number of received data bytes and start to write data at the first unwritten non-volatile memory position. title: Writing of received data
body: 3188 v2 Writing of received data Version history:(2):Purpose: To decrease the total programming time the ECU shall start writing data to the non-volatile memory before the complete message is received.Source:Verification Method: AnalysisLegacy ID: 53978v1The ECU shall start writing data to the non-volatile memory before the complete message is received, decompression included if supported. The positive response shall be sent after all data included in the TransferData request is written to the non-volatile memory.As non-volatile memories normally only allow one write operation for each erase operation the ECU must know how many data bytes it has written to the non-volatile memory. If the client transfers the same block again the ECU shall count the number of received data bytes and start to write data at the first unwritten non-volatile memory position.4.6.1.2.9 Separate memory sectorsTo decrease the total programming time it shall be possible to replace only the specific data file that shall be replaced and not being forced to replace all software(s) that already are present in Document Name Base Tech SWRS DHU the ECU. Since the erase of the memory only can be performed for a complete memory sector shall all data files which are possible to download to the ECU not share same memory sector. title: Separate memory sectors
body: 3123 v2 Separate memory sectors Version history: (2): Purpose: To decrease the total programming time it shall be possible to replace only the specific data file that shall be replaced and not being forced to replace all software(s) that already is present in the ECU. Source: Verification Method: Test Legacy ID: 53975v1 Two or more data files shall not share a memory sector. 4.6.1.2.10 File download order The data files which are downloadable to the ECU shall be capable of being downloaded to the ECU individually or in any grouping combination independent of order. The only exception to this is that the secondary bootloader shall always be required to be downloaded first when supported. As an example, if the ECU supports a secondary bootloader (SW - A), Application (SW - B), and a Signal configuration (SW - C), then the following download sequences shall be Document NameBase Tech SWRS DHU supported:Transition to programmingSession, download SW - A then BTransition to programmingSession, download SW - A then CTransition to programmingSession, download SW - A, B, then CTransition to programmingSession, download SW - A, C, then B

title: File download order
body: 3118 v4 File download order Version history:(4):Purpose: To be able to download data files to the ECU individually or in any grouping combination independent of order.Source:Verification Method: TestLegacy ID: 53973v3No restrictions on the download order/sequence of the downloadable data files are allowed, with the exception of the SBL which shall be downloaded first.It shall be possible to download each data file separately without any requirements of downloading other data files before, exception is the SBL.Note: If an ECU Software Structure (ESS) is to be downloaded, it shall always be downloaded next to the SBL. Added here for information, it is a client requirement.4.6.1.2.11 Delta encodingThe purpose with Delta encoding is to compress the size of the data to be transmitted to the ECU in order to reduce the time/cost spent during the programming phase. The delta encoding method is to calculate the difference between the new and the old software version, where only the difference between the two versions is transferred to the target ECU.
